ai.v1.AccountSelection.description: AccountSelection says whether a message's run reads an account at all.
ai.v1.AccountSelection.title: AccountSelection

ai.v1.ApprovalDecision.description: ApprovalDecision is the user's answer to an approval request.
ai.v1.ApprovalDecision.title: ApprovalDecision

ai.v1.ApprovalParameter.description:
ApprovalParameter is one key parameter of the action an approval approves,
 for example "Slice interval" and "5 s".

label.description: Short label, in plain words.
label.title: label

value.description: The value, in plain words, with its unit or asset when it has one.
value.title: value

ai.v1.ApprovalParameter.title: ApprovalParameter

ai.v1.ApprovalRequested.description:
ApprovalRequested reports that the run waits for the user to approve an
 action, such as placing an order. The run continues once DecideApproval
 answers it, or the approval expires. Nothing runs without an approval.

accountId.description:
Trading account (subaccount) the action acts on: the run's account, as
 SendMessageRequest.subaccount_id named it.
accountId.title: account_id

approvalId.description: Public approval ID, the argument of DecideApproval.
approvalId.title: approval_id

cancelOrders.description: The open orders the approval cancels.
cancelOrders.title: cancel_orders

cancelTriggers.description: The triggers the approval cancels together.
cancelTriggers.title: cancel_triggers

expiresAt.description: When the approval expires if undecided.
expiresAt.title: expires_at

orderChange.description: The change the approval makes to open limit orders.
orderChange.title: order_change

parameters.description:
The action's key parameters in display order, such as the market, side,
 quantity, prices, a TWAP's duration and slices or a ladder's range,
 written from the same exact action as the summary. Show them with the
 summary.
parameters.title: parameters

placeOrders.description: The limit orders the approval places together.
placeOrders.title: place_orders

summary.description: What approving does, written from the exact action, never by the model.
summary.title: summary

swap.description: The swap the approval executes within the trading account.
swap.title: swap

triggerChange.description: The change the approval makes to a trigger.
triggerChange.title: trigger_change

ai.v1.ApprovalRequested.title: ApprovalRequested

ai.v1.ApprovalResolved.description: ApprovalResolved reports the final state of an approval request.

approvalId.description: Public approval ID, as in its ApprovalRequested event.
approvalId.title: approval_id

ai.v1.ApprovalResolved.title: ApprovalResolved

ai.v1.ApprovalStatus.description: ApprovalStatus is the state of an approval request.
ai.v1.ApprovalStatus.title: ApprovalStatus

ai.v1.AssistantKey.description:
AssistantKey is the assistant's key for one of the caller's accounts. The
 assistant holds its private key; the API key it belongs to is listed and
 revoked with the caller's other API keys.

keyId.description: Opaque identifier of the API key.
keyId.title: key_id

label.description:
Name of the key's subaccount, as its owner set it. Returned only when
 ListAssistantKeys asks for ASSISTANT_KEY_VIEW_FULL. Empty for the main
 account, for a subaccount without a name, and when the name could not be
 read: the keys are listed either way.
label.title: label

subaccountId.description: Subaccount the key acts on. Omitted for the main account.
subaccountId.title: subaccount_id

ai.v1.AssistantKey.title: AssistantKey

ai.v1.AssistantKeyAccount.description: AssistantKeyAccount names one account to give the assistant a key for.

subaccountId.description: Subaccount. Omit for the main account.
subaccountId.title: subaccount_id

ai.v1.AssistantKeyAccount.title: AssistantKeyAccount

ai.v1.AssistantKeyState.description: AssistantKeyState is the state of an assistant key the assistant holds.
ai.v1.AssistantKeyState.title: AssistantKeyState

ai.v1.AssistantKeyView.description:
AssistantKeyView selects how much of each assistant key ListAssistantKeys
 returns.
ai.v1.AssistantKeyView.title: AssistantKeyView

ai.v1.AttachedExit.description: AttachedExit is an attached take-profit or stop-loss.

limitPrice.description:
The exit's limit price, an exact decimal string in the quote asset.
 Omitted when the exit is a market order.
limitPrice.title: limit_price

triggerPrice.description:
The price that fires the exit, an exact decimal string in the quote
 asset.
triggerPrice.title: trigger_price

ai.v1.AttachedExit.title: AttachedExit

ai.v1.AttachedExits.description:
AttachedExits are exits that protect what a market or limit order fills,
 armed as it fills. They close the order's position: they sell what a buy
 order bought, so a take-profit fires above and a stop-loss below the entry,
 and they buy back what a sell order sold, the other way round.

oco.description:
True when the exits are linked one-cancels-the-other, as RiskPolicy.oco.
 It decides only what canceling an exit's order ends: with oco set,
 canceling one exit's order ends both exits; without it, only that exit
 ends and the other keeps protecting the remaining position. Canceling an
 exit itself with CancelTrigger ends only that exit either way, and the
 other exit stays active.
oco.title: oco

stopLoss.description:
The stop-loss. Omitted when there is none. Never set together with
 trailing_stop.
stopLoss.title: stop_loss

takeProfit.description: The take-profit. Omitted when there is none.
takeProfit.title: take_profit

trailingStop.description: The trailing stop. Omitted when there is none.
trailingStop.title: trailing_stop

ai.v1.AttachedExits.title: AttachedExits

ai.v1.AttachedTrailingStop.description: AttachedTrailingStop is an attached trailing stop.

activationPrice.description:
Tracking starts once the price reaches it, an exact decimal string in
 the quote asset. Omitted when tracking starts at once.
activationPrice.title: activation_price

distance.description: A price distance, an exact decimal string in the quote asset.
distance.title: distance

distanceBps.description: A distance in basis points of the price: 50 is 0.5%.
distanceBps.title: distance_bps

limitPrice.description:
The most the buy-back pays, an exact decimal string in the quote asset.
 Set only when the order sells.
limitPrice.title: limit_price

ai.v1.AttachedTrailingStop.title: AttachedTrailingStop

ai.v1.BalanceHistoryChart.description:
BalanceHistoryChart shows how the caller's balance of each asset changed
 over a window ending at the time of the run.

accountId.description:
Trading account (subaccount) the history was read from: the run's account, as
 SendMessageRequest.subaccount_id named it.
accountId.title: account_id

history.description:
The window and its series, as GetBalanceHistory returns them for the
 caller's trading account. A series whose every point is zero is left out,
 so an account that held nothing in the window has no series.
history.title: history

ai.v1.BalanceHistoryChart.title: BalanceHistoryChart

accountId.description:
Account the balances were read from: the run's trading account, as
 SendMessageRequest.subaccount_id named it, or the caller's main account
 when the request named none.
accountId.title: account_id

balances.description: Balances, one per asset, highest available trading amount first.
balances.title: balances

ai.v1.CancelOrdersPreview.description:
CancelOrdersPreview is the exact set of open orders an approval cancels:
 orders named one by one, or every open order a cancel-all matches. It
 cancels orders only; triggers stay active.

cancelAll.description: True for a cancel-all: every open order on symbols and side.
cancelAll.title: cancel_all

liveTriggersKept.description:
A cancel-all's live triggers on its markets that stay active, as
 counted when it was requested. A lower bound when
 live_triggers_kept_lower_bound is true.
liveTriggersKept.title: live_triggers_kept

liveTriggersKeptLowerBound.description:
True when live_triggers_kept counts only the live triggers read, and
 more may stay active.
liveTriggersKeptLowerBound.title: live_triggers_kept_lower_bound

orders.description:
Every order it cancels: a cancel-all's oldest first, otherwise in the
 order the user named them. Approving cancels exactly these; an order that
 matches a cancel-all after the approval is not cancelled under it.
orders.title: orders

side.description:
A cancel-all's side, BUY or SELL. Unspecified for both sides, and for
 orders named one by one.
side.title: side

symbols.description:
A cancel-all's markets, for example "BTC-USDT". Empty for every market,
 and for orders named one by one.
symbols.title: symbols

ai.v1.CancelOrdersPreview.title: CancelOrdersPreview

ai.v1.CancelRunRequest.description: CancelRunRequest selects the run to cancel.
ai.v1.CancelRunRequest.title: CancelRunRequest

ai.v1.CancelRunResponse.description: CancelRunResponse confirms that the cancellation was recorded.
ai.v1.CancelRunResponse.title: CancelRunResponse

ai.v1.CancelTriggerPreview.description:
CancelTriggerPreview is the exact trigger an approval cancels, as it was
 when the cancellation was requested.

cancelsOpenOrders.description:
True when cancelling it also cancels its open orders: a TWAP's or a
 ladder's.
cancelsOpenOrders.title: cancels_open_orders

filledQuantity.description:
A TWAP's or ladder's quantity filled so far, an exact decimal string in
 the base asset. Omitted for other types.
filledQuantity.title: filled_quantity

levelCount.description: A ladder's number of levels. Omitted for other types.
levelCount.title: level_count

levelsFilled.description: A ladder's levels with at least one fill. Omitted for other types.
levelsFilled.title: levels_filled

quantity.description: Its total quantity, an exact decimal string in the base asset.
quantity.title: quantity

sliceCount.description: A TWAP's number of slices. Omitted for other types.
sliceCount.title: slice_count

slicesDone.description: A TWAP's slices done so far. Omitted for other types.
slicesDone.title: slices_done

symbolId.description: Numeric spot market identifier.
symbolId.title: symbol_id

triggerPrice.description:
A stop-loss's or take-profit's trigger price, or a trailing stop's
 current trigger price, an exact decimal string in the quote asset.
 Omitted for a TWAP or ladder, and when it has none yet.
triggerPrice.title: trigger_price

type.description: STOP_LOSS, TAKE_PROFIT, TRAILING_STOP, TWAP or LADDER.
type.title: type

ai.v1.CancelTriggerPreview.title: CancelTriggerPreview

ai.v1.CancelTriggersPreview.description:
CancelTriggersPreview is the exact set of live triggers an approval
 cancels together, in the order the user named them, each as it was when
 the cancellation was requested. Approving cancels exactly these triggers
 and no other: a trigger created after the approval is not cancelled under
 it. Cancelling a leg of a one-cancels-the-other pair also ends its other
 leg, as cancelling that one trigger does.
ai.v1.CancelTriggersPreview.title: CancelTriggersPreview

ai.v1.CompleteAssistantKeysRequest.description: CompleteAssistantKeysRequest selects the setup whose keys were registered.
ai.v1.CompleteAssistantKeysRequest.title: CompleteAssistantKeysRequest

ai.v1.CompleteAssistantKeysResponse.description: CompleteAssistantKeysResponse returns the keys the assistant now uses.

keys.description: The caller's assistant keys the assistant holds, oldest first.
keys.title: keys

ai.v1.CompleteAssistantKeysResponse.title: CompleteAssistantKeysResponse

ai.v1.Conversation.description: Conversation is one conversation of the caller with the assistant.

lastAccount.description:
The account the conversation's latest message selected, from any client,
 as of this list: a message sent since may have selected another.
 ListMessagesResponse.last_account is the account as it stands when the
 conversation is opened. Every message still names its own account:
 SendMessageRequest.subaccount_id and account_selection.
lastAccount.title: last_account

subject.description:
What the conversation is about, fixed when it started. Omitted for a
 general conversation.
subject.title: subject

title.description:
Short title, derived from the conversation's first messages. Empty until
 one is available.
title.title: title

updatedAt.description: When the latest message of the conversation was recorded.
updatedAt.title: updated_at

ai.v1.Conversation.title: Conversation

ai.v1.ConversationAccount.description:
ConversationAccount is the account a message of a conversation selected, as
 its SendMessageRequest named it.

accountSelection.description:
ACCOUNT_SELECTION_NONE when the message read no account; otherwise
 ACCOUNT_SELECTION_UNSPECIFIED.
accountSelection.title: account_selection

subaccountId.description:
The trading account (subaccount) the message named. Omitted for the main
 account, and when account_selection is ACCOUNT_SELECTION_NONE.
subaccountId.title: subaccount_id

ai.v1.ConversationAccount.title: ConversationAccount

ai.v1.CurrentPage.description:
CurrentPage is the page of the client the user is on as they send a message.
 It names the page by its template and title, never by its address: a client
 must never send the URL the user sees, its query string or fragment, or any
 id, symbol or other value taken from the path.

destinationId.description:
The id of the client's destination for the page, when the page is one of
 its destinations, for example "page-settings": lowercase letters, digits
 and hyphens, 1 to 64 characters, as in Destination.id. Omit it for a page
 that is none of them.
destinationId.title: destination_id

route.description:
The page's route template, each variable path segment named by its
 parameter in brackets, for example "/account/settings/[section]": it
 starts with "/" and has at most 200 characters, each a letter, a digit or
 one of "/", "-", "_", ".", "[" and "]".
route.title: route

title.description:
The page's title as the client shows it, for example "Settings", 1 to 80
 characters. Never the user's own data, such as an account label.
title.title: title

ai.v1.CurrentPage.title: CurrentPage

approvalId.description: Approval to decide, from an ApprovalRequested event.
approvalId.title: approval_id

ai.v1.DecideApprovalResponse.description: DecideApprovalResponse returns the recorded state of the approval.
ai.v1.DecideApprovalResponse.title: DecideApprovalResponse

ai.v1.DeleteMemoryRequest.description: DeleteMemoryRequest selects the memory to forget.
ai.v1.DeleteMemoryRequest.title: DeleteMemoryRequest

ai.v1.DeleteModelKeyRequest.description: DeleteModelKeyRequest deletes the caller's own OpenAI API key.
ai.v1.DeleteModelKeyRequest.title: DeleteModelKeyRequest

ai.v1.DepositAddressCard.description:
DepositAddressCard shows one of the caller's deposit addresses, to copy. An
 address takes deposits only on its own chain: show that chain's name next to
 the address, and warn that sending another asset, or using another chain,
 can lose the funds.

accountId.description:
Trading account (subaccount) the address belongs to: the run's account, as
 SendMessageRequest.subaccount_id named it.
accountId.title: account_id

assetId.description:
Public unified asset ID (AssetConfig.ledger_id) the caller asked to
 deposit to this address. Omitted when the card shows the address without
 one asset, for example in a list of the caller's addresses.
assetId.title: asset_id

depositAddress.description:
The address and the chain it is assigned on. Resolve the chain's name, and
 the assets it carries, with GetDepositWithdrawConfig.
depositAddress.title: deposit_address

ai.v1.DepositAddressCard.title: DepositAddressCard

ai.v1.Destination.description:
Destination is one place in the client the assistant may offer the user to
 go to: a page, or a dialog such as deposit or transfer. The client declares
 the destinations it has with each message; the assistant suggests them by
 id, and the client maps each id to its own page or dialog.

description.description:
What the user does there, in a few words or keywords, at most 200
 characters, for example "sub accounts, account management". The assistant
 reads it to choose a destination.
description.title: description

id.description:
The client's id of the destination, for example "page-subaccounts":
 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, 1 to 64 characters.
id.title: id

title.description:
Its name as the client shows it, for example "Subaccounts", 1 to 80
 characters.
title.title: title

ai.v1.Destination.title: Destination

ai.v1.DestinationsSuggested.description:
DestinationsSuggested reports the places in the client the assistant
 offers the user to go to, for example to create a subaccount or change a
 setting: show each as a button. The ids are those the run's SendMessage
 declared in destinations; the client maps each to its own page or dialog.
 The event follows the ToolFinished event, with ok true, of the
 suggest_destinations call that chose them.

destinationIds.description:
1 to 3 destination ids, most relevant first, each declared in the run's
 SendMessage destinations. A client that no longer knows an id skips it.
destinationIds.title: destination_ids

toolCallId.description:
Identifier of the tool call, as in its ToolStarted and ToolFinished
 events.
toolCallId.title: tool_call_id

ai.v1.DestinationsSuggested.title: DestinationsSuggested

ai.v1.DiscardPartial.description:
DiscardPartial withdraws answer text that is about to be written again. The
 assistant was interrupted while writing and regenerates its answer from an
 earlier point; the regenerated text follows in later TextDelta events.

fromSeq.description:
Drop the text of every TextDelta of this run whose seq is equal to or
 greater than this value, and received before this event. Tool, view and
 other events stay.
fromSeq.title: from_seq

ai.v1.DiscardPartial.title: DiscardPartial

ai.v1.DisplaySetting.description:
DisplaySetting is one of the client's display preferences the assistant may
 change for the user: cosmetic settings the user can change back at any
 time. Each value names the values the assistant may apply to it, exactly as
 DisplaySettingAction.value carries them. Security, funds, API keys,
 permissions and notification channels are never display settings.
ai.v1.DisplaySetting.title: DisplaySetting

ai.v1.DisplaySettingAction.description:
DisplaySettingAction asks the client to change one of its display settings
 for the user, or, when the user did not say to what, to show that setting's
 choices in the conversation so the user picks one. The setting is one the
 run's SendMessage declared in display_settings. The event follows the
 ToolFinished event, with ok true, of the set_display_preference call that
 chose it.

 Apply an action once, when it arrives in a run the client sent and follows:
 replaying a run's events later, for example to show an earlier
 conversation, applies none of them again. Offer the user a way to undo the
 change, back to the value the setting had before. A client that no longer
 has the setting, or does not accept the value, changes nothing.

toolCallId.description:
Identifier of the tool call, as in its ToolStarted and ToolFinished
 events.
toolCallId.title: tool_call_id

value.description:
The value to apply, one of the setting's values as DisplaySetting lists
 them. Omitted when the user did not name one: show the setting's choices
 instead, and change nothing until the user picks.
value.title: value

ai.v1.DisplaySettingAction.title: DisplaySettingAction

ai.v1.DraftVersion.description: DraftVersion is the strategy revision a subagent saved last.

revision.description: The revision the save created or kept: from 1.
revision.title: revision

versionId.description:
ID of the revision's version, which strategies.v1 GetStrategyVersion
 reads.
versionId.title: version_id

ai.v1.DraftVersion.title: DraftVersion

ai.v1.EquityHistoryChart.description:
EquityHistoryChart shows the value of the caller's holdings over a window
 ending at the time of the run.

accountId.description:
Trading account (subaccount) the history was read from: the run's account, as
 SendMessageRequest.subaccount_id named it.
accountId.title: account_id

history.description:
The window and its series, as GetEquityHistorySeries returns them for the
 caller's trading account, grouped by account bucket or by asset.
 btc_prices_q is not set. The account's total equity at a point is the sum
 of every series at that point.
history.title: history

ai.v1.EquityHistoryChart.title: EquityHistoryChart

ai.v1.FailureCategory.description: FailureCategory classifies why a run failed.
ai.v1.FailureCategory.title: FailureCategory

ai.v1.FundingMode.description: FundingMode is what pays for the caller's next messages to the assistant.
ai.v1.FundingMode.title: FundingMode

ai.v1.GetMessageImageRequest.description: GetMessageImageRequest selects one image of the caller's messages.
ai.v1.GetMessageImageRequest.title: GetMessageImageRequest

data.description: The image file, as MessageImage describes it.
data.title: data

mimeType.description: Media type of data: image/png, image/jpeg or image/webp.
mimeType.title: mime_type

ai.v1.GetModelKeyRequest.description: GetModelKeyRequest reads the status of the caller's own OpenAI API key.
ai.v1.GetModelKeyRequest.title: GetModelKeyRequest

ai.v1.GetModelKeyResponse.description: GetModelKeyResponse returns the status of the caller's own OpenAI API key.

key.description: The caller's key; unset when the caller has none.
key.title: key

ai.v1.GetModelKeyResponse.title: GetModelKeyResponse

ai.v1.GetTelegramApprovalLimitsRequest.description:
GetTelegramApprovalLimitsRequest reads the caller's Telegram approval
 limits.
ai.v1.GetTelegramApprovalLimitsRequest.title: GetTelegramApprovalLimitsRequest

ai.v1.GetTelegramApprovalLimitsResponse.description:
GetTelegramApprovalLimitsResponse returns the caller's Telegram approval
 limits and what counts against the daily one.

approvedLast24hUsd.description:
Notional value approved from Telegram in the last 24 hours while a limit
 was set, in US dollars: a decimal string with 2 decimal places.
approvedLast24hUsd.title: approved_last_24h_usd

limits.description: The limits; both unset when the caller set none.
limits.title: limits

ai.v1.GetTelegramApprovalLimitsResponse.title: GetTelegramApprovalLimitsResponse

ai.v1.GetUsageRequest.description: GetUsageRequest reads the caller's assistant credits today.
ai.v1.GetUsageRequest.title: GetUsageRequest

ai.v1.GetUsageResponse.description:
GetUsageResponse is the caller's assistant credits today. A credit is a
 fixed amount of AI usage: a longer answer, or one that uses more tools,
 uses more credits. The figures are the main account's, which every
 subaccount shares, and are the ones a new message is admitted against.

freeCredits.description: Today's free credits: the VIP tier's daily free credits.
freeCredits.title: free_credits

freeCreditsLeft.description:
Free credits left today: free_credits minus free_credits_used, and 0
 when none are left. With none left and CREDITS funding, a message is
 answered with RunFailed DAILY_LIMIT_REACHED.
freeCreditsLeft.title: free_credits_left

freeCreditsUsed.description:
Free credits used today, rounded down to a whole credit. May exceed
 free_credits: an answer started with credits left always finishes.
freeCreditsUsed.title: free_credits_used

fundingMode.description:
What pays for the caller's next messages. With OWN_KEY they use no
 credits, and the free credits below stay unused.
fundingMode.title: funding_mode

nextTier.description:
The next VIP tier and its daily free credits. Unset at the highest tier,
 and when the caller's tier could not be read.
nextTier.title: next_tier

resetsAt.description:
When the free credits reset: the next 00:00 UTC. Credits left unused do
 not carry over to the next day.
resetsAt.title: resets_at

vipTier.description:
The caller's VIP tier, whose free credits apply today. Unset when the
 tier could not be read: VIP 0's free credits then apply.
vipTier.title: vip_tier

ai.v1.GetUsageResponse.title: GetUsageResponse

ai.v1.ImageAttachment.description:
ImageAttachment is an image the caller attaches to a message, such as a
 screenshot of an order, an error or a chart.

data.description:
The image file: a PNG, JPEG or WebP image, at most 10 MiB, 8000 pixels on
 a side and 32 megapixels in all. Larger is IMAGE_TOO_LARGE; another format,
 or a file that cannot be decoded, is IMAGE_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED.
data.title: data

mimeType.description:
Media type of data: image/png, image/jpeg or image/webp. It must match the
 file's own format (IMAGE_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED otherwise).
mimeType.title: mime_type

ai.v1.ImageAttachment.title: ImageAttachment

ai.v1.LadderLevel.description: LadderLevel is one limit order of a ladder.

price.description: Its price, an exact decimal string in the quote asset.
price.title: price

quantity.description: Its quantity, an exact decimal string in the base asset.
quantity.title: quantity

ai.v1.LadderLevel.title: LadderLevel

ai.v1.LadderPreview.description:
LadderPreview is a ladder: good-till-canceled limit orders spread evenly
 across a price range, all placed at once.

allLevelsAtOnce.description: True when every level is placed at once, when the ladder is created.
allLevelsAtOnce.title: all_levels_at_once

highPrice.description: The highest level's price, an exact decimal string in the quote asset.
highPrice.title: high_price

levels.description:
Every level, lowest price first: 2 to 100. The quantity is split
 equally, rounded down to the step size; the highest level gets the rest.
levels.title: levels

lowPrice.description: The lowest level's price, an exact decimal string in the quote asset.
lowPrice.title: low_price

postOnly.description: True when every level is refused instead of trading at once.
postOnly.title: post_only

timeInForce.description: Every level's time in force: GTC.
timeInForce.title: time_in_force

ai.v1.LadderPreview.title: LadderPreview

ai.v1.LimitOrderPreview.description: LimitOrderPreview is a limit order: it trades at its price or better.

attached.description: Exits attached to the order. Omitted when it has none.
attached.title: attached

expireAt.description: When a GTD order expires. Omitted for other times in force.
expireAt.title: expire_at

postOnly.description: True when the order is refused instead of trading at once.
postOnly.title: post_only

price.description: The limit price, an exact decimal string in the quote asset.
price.title: price

ai.v1.LimitOrderPreview.title: LimitOrderPreview

ai.v1.ListAssistantKeysRequest.description: ListAssistantKeysRequest lists the assistant keys the assistant holds.

view.description:
How much of each key to return. Omit it for the default view, without
 account names; ASSISTANT_KEY_VIEW_FULL adds each key's account name and
 orders the keys by account (see ListAssistantKeysResponse.keys).
view.title: view

ai.v1.ListAssistantKeysRequest.title: ListAssistantKeysRequest

ai.v1.ListAssistantKeysResponse.description: ListAssistantKeysResponse returns the assistant keys the assistant holds.

keys.description:
The caller's assistant keys the assistant holds, at most one per account.
 The default view lists them oldest first. ASSISTANT_KEY_VIEW_FULL lists
 them as an account picker shows them: the main account's key first, then
 the subaccounts' keys by the subaccount's equity, highest first. Keys
 with equal equity, and those whose equity could not be read, which come
 last, are listed by account name.
keys.title: keys

ai.v1.ListAssistantKeysResponse.title: ListAssistantKeysResponse

ai.v1.ListConversationsRequest.description:
ListConversationsRequest pages through the caller's conversations, most
 recently updated first.

limit.description: Maximum conversations to return. 0 means the default of 20; maximum 100.
limit.title: limit

pageToken.description:
Opaque, keyset-backed, exclusive cursor from a previous response. Bound to
 the caller, updated_at and conversation_id.
pageToken.title: page_token

subject.description:
Only the caller's conversation about this subject: at most one. Omit it
 to list every conversation, those about a subject included.
subject.title: subject

ai.v1.ListConversationsRequest.title: ListConversationsRequest

conversations.description:
Conversations ordered by updated_at descending, then conversation_id
 descending. A conversation updated while paging moves to the front, so a
 chain of pages started earlier does not return it again.
conversations.title: conversations

nextPageToken.description: Cursor for the next page. Empty when no more results exist.
nextPageToken.title: next_page_token

ai.v1.ListMemoriesRequest.description: ListMemoriesRequest pages through the caller's memories, newest first.

limit.description: Maximum memories to return. 0 means the default of 50; maximum 200.
limit.title: limit

pageToken.description:
Opaque, keyset-backed, exclusive cursor from a previous response. Bound to
 the caller, created_at and memory_id.
pageToken.title: page_token

ai.v1.ListMemoriesRequest.title: ListMemoriesRequest

ai.v1.MemoriesRecalled.description:
MemoriesRecalled reports the memories one memory search of the run
 returned. The assistant searches the user's memories for their message
 before it answers, and may search again while answering, each time as a
 recall_memories tool call. A search returns only the memories relevant to
 what it searched for, so a message unrelated to every saved memory recalls
 none. Profile memories are never searched: the assistant applies them to
 every answer, and they are not reported here. The event follows that call's
 ToolFinished event with ok true; a failed search has a ToolFinished event
 with ok false and no MemoriesRecalled event.

 In an existing conversation, the assistant also gets the memories the user
 saved or changed in their other conversations since its previous answer in
 this one, whatever the message is about. When there are any, the run reports
 them before the answer as a memory_updates tool call (ToolStarted and
 ToolFinished with ok true) and its MemoriesRecalled event, so a client can
 show that memory was updated from another conversation. Otherwise the run
 has no memory_updates call.

memories.description:
For a recall_memories call: the relevant memories found, at most 8, most
 relevant first, empty when none is relevant. For a memory_updates call:
 the memories saved or changed in other conversations, at most 20, newest
 first, never empty. Never a profile memory.
memories.title: memories

toolCallId.description:
Identifier of the search's tool call, as in its ToolStarted and
 ToolFinished events.
toolCallId.title: tool_call_id

ai.v1.MemoriesRecalled.title: MemoriesRecalled

ai.v1.OcoLegPreview.description:
OcoLegPreview is one leg of an OCO: once the watched price reaches its
 trigger price, it places its order for the OCO's whole remaining quantity.

direction.description: Which way the watched price must move to reach trigger_price.
direction.title: direction

limitPrice.description:
The limit price of the good-till-canceled order it places, an exact
 decimal string in the quote asset. Omitted when it places a market order.
limitPrice.title: limit_price

triggerPrice.description: The price that fires the leg, an exact decimal string in the quote asset.
triggerPrice.title: trigger_price

triggerPriceSource.description: The price it watches: LAST_PRICE or INDEX_PRICE.
triggerPriceSource.title: trigger_price_source

ai.v1.OcoLegPreview.title: OcoLegPreview

ai.v1.OcoPreview.description:
OcoPreview is an OCO (one-cancels-the-other): a take-profit and a stop-loss
 that both trade the order's side for its whole quantity. A sell OCO sells
 base asset the account already holds: its take-profit fires when the price
 rises to its trigger price, its stop-loss when it falls to its own. A buy
 OCO buys the quantity of base asset with quote asset the account already
 holds, the other way round. Creating it reserves funds once, and both legs
 share them: a sell reserves the quantity of base asset, a buy the quote
 asset needed to buy the quantity, as the exchange computes it. Cancelling
 either leg cancels both.

reservedAsset.description:
The asset creating the OCO reserves once for both legs: the base asset for
 a sell, the quote asset for a buy. OrderPreview.reserved_amount states the
 amount when it is set.
reservedAsset.title: reserved_asset

ai.v1.OcoPreview.title: OcoPreview

OrderChange is one open limit order a modification changes, before and
 after.

filledQuantity.description: Quantity filled so far, an exact decimal string in the base asset.
filledQuantity.title: filled_quantity

newPrice.description:
The new limit price, an exact decimal string in the quote asset. Omitted
 when the price does not change.
newPrice.title: new_price

newQuantity.description:
The new total quantity, filled part included, an exact decimal string in
 the base asset. Omitted when the quantity does not change.
newQuantity.title: new_quantity

price.description: The limit price now, an exact decimal string in the quote asset.
price.title: price

quantity.description:
The total quantity now, filled part included, an exact decimal string in
 the base asset.
quantity.title: quantity

replaced.description:
True when the change replaces the order with a new order under a new
 order ID, at the back of the queue: a new price or a larger quantity.
 False when it amends the order in place, keeping its queue position.
replaced.title: replaced

ai.v1.OrderChange.title: OrderChange

ai.v1.OrderChangePreview.description:
OrderChangePreview is the exact change an approval makes to open limit
 orders of one market: their price or total quantity, before and after.

orders.description: Every order it changes, in the order the user named them.
orders.title: orders

symbolId.description: Numeric spot market identifier.
symbolId.title: symbol_id

ai.v1.OrderChangePreview.title: OrderChangePreview

ai.v1.OrderPreview.description:
OrderPreview is the exact order an approval places, as typed values to
 draw it: a TWAP's slices on a timeline, a ladder's levels on a price axis,
 a stop's trigger price against the current price. It is computed from the
 exact order by the assistant's order checks, never written by the model,
 and states the same order as the approval's summary and parameters.
 Prices are exact decimal strings in the quote asset, quantities in the
 base asset.

estimatedValue.description:
Estimated order value in the quote asset, a decimal string rounded to at
 most 2 decimals. Valued at: quote_amount or quote_proceeds when set; a
 market order or TWAP of market slices at reference_price; a pegged limit
 order at its current_price; a limit order, ladder level or limit
 slice at its price; a stop at its limit price, else its trigger price; a
 trailing stop at its limit price, else its activation price, else the last
 price. Omitted for an OCO, and when it cannot be estimated.
estimatedValue.title: estimated_value

limit.description: A limit order.
limit.title: limit

oco.description:
An OCO: a take-profit and a stop-loss that sell base asset the account
 holds, or buy base asset with quote asset it holds.
oco.title: oco

peggedLimit.description: A limit order with a static peg.
peggedLimit.title: pegged_limit

quantity.description:
Total quantity, an exact decimal string in the base asset. Omitted only
 for a buy sized by quote_amount and a sell sized by quote_proceeds.
quantity.title: quantity

quoteAmount.description:
A buy market order, or buy immediate-or-cancel limit order, sized by
 spend: the most quote asset it spends, an exact decimal string. Omitted
 when quantity or quote_proceeds is set.
quoteAmount.title: quote_amount

quoteProceeds.description:
A sell market order, or sell immediate-or-cancel limit order, sized by
 proceeds: it sells whole quantity steps until its proceeds before fees
 reach this amount of quote asset, an exact decimal string, and never
 receives more. The fee is charged in quote asset on those proceeds.
 Omitted when quantity or quote_amount is set.
quoteProceeds.title: quote_proceeds

referencePrice.description:
The current market price to draw the order against: for a stop-loss,
 take-profit, trailing stop or OCO the price it watches (last or index),
 for a pegged limit order the book side it is pegged to, for the others
 the best ask for a buy or the best bid for a sell. Omitted when the
 market has no such price.
referencePrice.title: reference_price

relativePrices.description:
The prices the user gave relative to another price, as resolved, in the
 order they appear in the order. Empty when every price was given as an
 absolute price.
relativePrices.title: relative_prices

reservedAmount.description:
What the exchange reserves on the trading account when it creates a
 stop-loss, take-profit, trailing stop, OCO or ladder: an exact decimal
 string, in the base asset for a sell, in the quote asset (fee reserve
 included) for a buy. Omitted for market and limit orders, which reserve as
 they are placed, for a TWAP, whose slices each use what is available when
 they are due, and for a buy OCO, whose reserve the exchange sets when it
 creates it.
reservedAmount.title: reserved_amount

symbolId.description: Numeric spot market identifier.
symbolId.title: symbol_id

ai.v1.PeggedLimitOrderPreview.description:
PeggedLimitOrderPreview is a limit order with a static peg: the exchange
 takes its price once, when it accepts the order, from one side of the book
 moved by a number of the pair's ticks, and never moves it with the book
 after. It never carries attached exits.

boundPrice.description:
The order's bound, an exact decimal string in the quote asset: the most
 a buy pays or the least a sell takes. The exchange checks the order's
 minimums, maximums and funds at it, and refuses the order when the
 price the peg gives passes it. It is not the order's price.
boundPrice.title: bound_price

currentPrice.description:
The price the peg gives at reference_price, the side's best price when
 the preview read it: an exact decimal string in the quote asset. The
 exchange takes it again when it accepts the order, so the order's price
 can differ.
currentPrice.title: current_price

expireAt.description: When a GTD order expires. Omitted for other times in force.
expireAt.title: expire_at

offsetTicks.description:
Signed number of the pair's ticks added to that side's best price: 2 is
 two ticks above it, -1 one tick below. Zero is the best price itself.
offsetTicks.title: offset_ticks

postOnly.description: True when the order is refused instead of trading at once.
postOnly.title: post_only

reference.description: The book side the price is taken from: BEST_BID or BEST_ASK.
reference.title: reference

tickSize.description: The pair's tick size, an exact decimal string in the quote asset.
tickSize.title: tick_size

 its own estimated value and reference price.
orders.title: orders

totalValues.description:
The estimated value of the whole set, one per quote asset, in the order
 the assets first appear in orders: the exact sum of its orders' values in
 that asset, then rounded.
totalValues.title: total_values

ai.v1.ReferencePrice.description:
ReferencePrice is one current market price the order preview read, to
 draw the order against.

observedAt.description:
When the price was set: for LAST_PRICE the time of the market's last
 trade, for the others when the assistant read it.
observedAt.title: observed_at

price.description: The price, an exact decimal string in the quote asset.
price.title: price

ai.v1.ReferencePrice.title: ReferencePrice

ai.v1.ReferencePriceSource.description: ReferencePriceSource names the market price a ReferencePrice is.
ai.v1.ReferencePriceSource.title: ReferencePriceSource

ai.v1.RelativePrice.description:
RelativePrice is a price of the order that the user gave relative to
 another price, for example "10% below the current price", and that the
 assistant resolved to the absolute price the order carries. The order is
 placed at that absolute price, as approved, even when the reference moves
 afterwards.

direction.description: Whether the price is above or below the reference.
direction.title: direction

field.description: Which price of the order it is.
field.title: field

limitPrice.description:
The order's own limit price, an exact decimal string in the quote
 asset: the reference of an attached exit of a limit order.
limitPrice.title: limit_price

market.description:
A market price the assistant read: for a stop-loss, take-profit or
 trailing stop the price it watches (last or index), for the others the
 best ask for a buy or the best bid for a sell; for an attached exit of
 a market order, that order's best ask or best bid. A reference set more
 than the approval's 10-minute lifetime before the approval was
 requested (a last price by its last trade) is refused.
market.title: market

offsetBps.description:
The offset from the reference in basis points: 1000 is 10%. From 0 to
 10000 above the reference, from 0 to 9999 below it. Zero is the
 reference itself, rounded onto the tick size as price says. A positive
 offset always resolves strictly above or below the reference, as
 direction says: one smaller than one tick size step is refused, never
 resolved to the reference or past it.
offsetBps.title: offset_bps

price.description:
The resolved price, an exact decimal string in the quote asset, as the
 order carries it: the reference moved by offset_bps, then rounded onto
 the market's tick size in the direction never worse for the order that
 trades at it: down for a buy, up for a sell. An attached exit trades
 the other way from its order.
price.title: price

rounding.description:
Which way the moved reference was rounded onto tick_size: DOWN for a
 price a buy trades at, UP for a sell.
rounding.title: rounding

tickSize.description:
The market's tick size the price was rounded onto, an exact decimal
 string in the quote asset.
tickSize.title: tick_size

ai.v1.RelativePrice.title: RelativePrice

approvalResolved.description: An approval was decided or expired.

destinationsSuggested.description: Places in the client the assistant offers the user to go to.

displaySettingAction.description: A display setting for the client to change, or to offer the choices of.

Position of the event in its run: 1 for the first event, then increasing

seq.title: seq

subagentStarted.description: A subagent started a delegated task.
subagentStarted.title: subagent_started

RunFailed is the last event of a run that ended without finishing its

ai.v1.SendMessageRequest.description:
SendMessageRequest sends the caller's message and starts a run that answers
 it.
conversation_id is required with expected_latest_run_id
subaccount_id must be omitted when account_selection is ACCOUNT_SELECTION_NONE
text is required unless images are attached
each destination id must be unique

accountSelection.description:
Whether the run reads an account. Omit it to read the account
 subaccount_id names, or the main account. ACCOUNT_SELECTION_NONE for a
 run that reads no account, such as a client whose user has not given the
 assistant access to any account: subaccount_id must then be omitted. It
 is part of the request the idempotency key covers.
accountSelection.title: account_selection

conversationId.description: Conversation to continue. Omit to start a new conversation.
conversationId.title: conversation_id

destinations.description:
The places in the client the run may suggest to the user, at most 100,
 each id at most once; their order does not matter. Omit them for a client
 that cannot take the user anywhere: the run then suggests nothing. They
 are part of the request the idempotency key covers.
destinations.title: destinations

displaySettings.description:
The display settings the client can change for the user when the run
 asks it to (DisplaySettingAction), each at most once; their order does
 not matter. Declare only those the client offers the user now. Omit them
 for a client without display settings: the run then changes none and
 points the user to their settings instead. They are part of the request
 the idempotency key covers.
displaySettings.title: display_settings

expectedLatestRunId.description:
Send the message only while this run is still the conversation's latest
 run: a client that continues a request it showed the user, such as a
 button under an answer, sets it to that answer's run, so the message never
 lands after a newer one. Checked as the message is recorded; when another
 run is the latest, nothing is recorded and the call is
 FAILED_PRECONDITION with CONVERSATION_ADVANCED. Requires conversation_id.
 Omit it to send whatever the conversation's latest run. It is part of the
 request the idempotency key covers: a repeat of a request already
 recorded returns its run, whatever ran since.
expectedLatestRunId.title: expected_latest_run_id

idempotencyKey.description:
Client-chosen key, unique per caller, that makes sending idempotent: the
 same key and request return the same run and conversation, also for a new
 conversation; another request with the same key is IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.
idempotencyKey.title: idempotency_key

images.description:
Images the message shows the assistant, at most 4, in the order the user
 attached them; more is TOO_MANY_IMAGES. The assistant reads them with the
 text, and they stay with the message: later answers in the conversation
 can refer to them, and ListMessages lists them. Text in an image is read
 as part of the picture, never as instructions to the assistant. They are
 part of the request the idempotency key covers.
images.title: images

page.description:
The page the user is on as they send the message. The run is told it, so
 it can say which page the user is on and point within that page rather
 than suggest it again. Omit it for a client without pages: the run is then
 told nothing about where the user is. It is part of the request the
 idempotency key covers: a retry sends the page the first attempt sent.
page.title: page

subaccountId.description:
Trading account (subaccount) the run reads and acts on. It must be one
 the caller's account owns; any other value, also one that does not
 exist, is INVALID_ARGUMENT. Omit it for the main account (unless
 account_selection is ACCOUNT_SELECTION_NONE): the run then
 reads the main account (its balances, funding included, every trading
 account with its equity, API keys, price alerts, fee rates and
 permissions) and places, changes or cancels no order, trigger or swap;
 asked to trade, it asks the user to select a trading account. It is part
 of the request the idempotency key covers.
subaccountId.title: subaccount_id

subject.description:
What the conversation is about. Without conversation_id, the message
 continues the caller's conversation about this subject, or starts it:
 there is at most one per subject. With conversation_id, omit it or send
 the conversation's own subject. A conversation's subject is fixed when it
 starts: any other subject, or a subject for a conversation that has none,
 is FAILED_PRECONDITION with CONVERSATION_SUBJECT_MISMATCH, and nothing is
 recorded. It is part of the request the idempotency key covers.
subject.title: subject

text.description:
Message text, plain text or Markdown, at most 16000 characters. Required
 unless images are attached; with images, it is the question about them.
text.title: text

ai.v1.SendMessageRequest.title: SendMessageRequest

conversationId.description: The conversation of the message: the requested one, or the new one.
conversationId.title: conversation_id

runId.description: The run that answers the message. Follow it with WatchRun.
runId.title: run_id

ai.v1.SetModelKeyRequest.description: SetModelKeyRequest saves the caller's own OpenAI API key.

apiKey.description:
An OpenAI secret API key: "sk-" followed by 20 to 300 letters, digits,

PriceAlert is one price alert of the caller.

 the other side of the alert price. A BELOW alert created while the price is
 already below the alert price therefore fires only after the price rises
 above it and falls back to it. An alert fires at most once; prices that
 arrive late, or a feed that stops updating, never fire it.

True once the price has been seen on the far side of the alert price, so

auth.v1.AssistantKeyPreset.description:
AssistantKeyPreset is a fixed permission set for a Polyester AI assistant
 key. SetAssistantKeys turns it into an API policy of the key's main account,
 named after the preset, so the policy and the key need only the set's one
 step-up proof. No preset ever allows a money-out action (EXTERNAL_WITHDRAW,
 INTERNAL_TRANSFER, MANAGE_ADDRESS_BOOK, MANAGE_AUTO_WITHDRAW), API-key or
 policy management, or any action that weakens account security.

policyId.description:

 main account as the key, must not be a template (FailedPrecondition with
 AUTH_POLICY_INVALID), and must not allow EXTERNAL_WITHDRAW,
 INTERNAL_TRANSFER, MANAGE_ADDRESS_BOOK or MANAGE_AUTO_WITHDRAW. Set
 exactly one of policy_id and preset.
policyId.title: policy_id

preset.description:
Permission preset that bounds the key, instead of policy_id. The key is
 bound to the preset's policy in the key's main account: the existing one
 with the preset's name and exactly its actions over all markets, else one
 created in the same change. The response's policy_id names it. Set
 exactly one of policy_id and preset.
preset.title: preset

publicKeyEd25519.description:
Ed25519 public key bytes the Polyester AI assistant signs with. Must be

publicKeyEd25519.title: public_key_ed25519

registrationDeadline.description:
Time until which the key may be registered, as the Polyester AI assistant
 issued it with the key (PrepareAssistantKeys), in whole milliseconds.
 Required for a new key: it must still be ahead, and at most 15 minutes
 ahead. Not needed when the account's current assistant key already has
 this public key.
registrationDeadline.title: registration_deadline

registrationProof.description:
The key's own Ed25519 signature over the caller's account, the key's
 account, its public key and registration_deadline, as the assistant
 issued it with the key (64 bytes). Required for a new key; not needed
 when the account's current assistant key already has this public key.
registrationProof.title: registration_proof

subaccountId.description:
Sub-account the key acts for (opaque ID). Unset means the caller's main

subaccountId.title: subaccount_id

auth.v1.PolicyAction.description:
PolicyAction is a high-level permission that can be granted by a policy.
 Product actions apply to sub-account and API-key policies, and their
 write-style actions also grant the matching read visibility where needed by
 the product experience. Account permissions, each documented below as an
 account permission or a main-account permission, apply to API-key policies
 only: a sub-account policy refuses them. Each account permission grants
 exactly the calls it names and never implies another permission. A
 main-account permission is honored only for an API key scoped to the main
 account; a key scoped to a sub-account is refused even when its policy
 grants it. Admin permissions, documented below, apply to API-key policies
 only and are honored only for an admin API key. An API key without a policy
 has no permission at all.

SocialVerification describes the caller's current verification state for one

attempts.description: Number of recorded provider-check attempts for this challenge.
attempts.title: attempts

challengeCode.description:
Challenge code the user must submit according to the verification method.
 Discord and Telegram codes are returned only when a challenge is issued.
 Codes expire after 15 minutes.
challengeCode.title: challenge_code

changeAvailableAt.description:
Time in UTC from which the caller may change or unlink its X/Twitter or
 Discord account again. Each provider allows one change or unlink per 30
 days; until this time, changing or unlinking the linked account fails with
 AUTH_SOCIAL_CHANGE_LIMIT_REACHED and a retry_after equal to it. Set
 whenever the limit applies, whether or not a verification failed. Empty
 when a change or unlink is allowed now, and always for Telegram. A first
 link, a link after an unlink, and a re-verification of the linked
 X/Twitter handle are not changes and are allowed while it is set.
changeAvailableAt.title: change_available_at

displayName.description:
Provider display name of the account being verified, for showing it to the
 user. Telegram only: the account's name, set once the code is submitted.
 Empty for other providers.
displayName.title: display_name

errorCode.description:
Stable machine-readable error code for the current failed verification.
 Unspecified when no typed error applies. REST JSON writes the value
 without the AUTH_ prefix, for example SOCIAL_ACCOUNT_COOLDOWN; ConnectRPC
 writes its full name, AUTH_SOCIAL_ACCOUNT_COOLDOWN.
errorCode.title: error_code

expiresAt.description: Time in UTC when the current challenge code expires.
expiresAt.title: expires_at

handle.description:
Provider handle being verified. Handles are returned lowercase and without
 a leading "@". For Telegram, the username of the account that submitted the
 code; empty when that account has no username.
handle.title: handle

lastError.description:
Last verification error, if the most recent check failed. Empty when there
 is no recorded error.
lastError.title: last_error

method.description:
Method used for this verification. If unspecified at start time, the
 provider default is used.
method.title: method

providerUserId.description:
Stable provider-side user identifier of the linked provider account. Empty
 while no account is linked. A restarted X/Twitter or Discord verification
 keeps the current link, and this value, until the new verification succeeds
 and replaces it. For Telegram, while the status is
 STATUS_AWAITING_CONFIRMATION, it is the numeric user ID of the Telegram
 account that submitted the code, the value ConfirmSocialVerification takes.
providerUserId.title: provider_user_id

requestedAt.description: Time in UTC when the current challenge code was issued.
requestedAt.title: requested_at

retryAfter.description:
Time in UTC from which a new verification may succeed, when this one
 failed with error_code SOCIAL_ACCOUNT_COOLDOWN or
 SOCIAL_CHANGE_LIMIT_REACHED (in ConnectRPC, AUTH_SOCIAL_ACCOUNT_COOLDOWN
 or AUTH_SOCIAL_CHANGE_LIMIT_REACHED). Empty otherwise.
retryAfter.title: retry_after

updatedAt.description: Time in UTC when this verification state last changed.
updatedAt.title: updated_at

verifiedAt.description:
Time in UTC when the linked provider account was last verified. Empty while
 no account is linked; kept, like provider_user_id, while a restarted
 verification runs.
verifiedAt.title: verified_at

 caller that lost CreateSubaccount's response can find it. Present only

 kind of caller that can create one; real-time updates omit it. Empty when
 none was given.
idempotencyKey.title: idempotency_key

ownerRootSmartAccountAddress.title: owner_root_smart_account_address

removed.description:
True when the caller no longer has access to this sub-account, for
 example after its owner removed the caller as a member: remove the
 sub-account from the caller's list. Only real-time updates set it;
 responses list only sub-accounts the caller can access. A change of the
 caller's role or access does not change revision or updated_at, so
 real-time updates deliver such changes in order and each one applies as
 it arrives. Ending access also ends the caller's subscriptions to this
 sub-account's real-time channels, and can, rarely, also end a
 subscription made after access was granted again. When the server ends a
 subscription to one of this sub-account's channels while the latest
 update lists this sub-account with a role and removed false, subscribe
 again: access is checked again on subscribe.

Why a terminal Swap did not trade its whole amount; unset when it did or
 when the asset was not converted.
reason.title: reason

Why the asset was not converted (route_unsupported, below_minimum,
 above_maximum, conversion_unavailable, price_unavailable,
 conversion_refused, rule_superseded or policy_denied); empty otherwise.
 Its balance stays on the account.

AutoWithdrawDestination pays one asset, in kind, to one external-chain
 address.

assetId.description: Ledger asset paid. At most one destination per asset.
assetId.title: asset_id

destinationAddress.description:
Destination address on destination_chain_id. It must be on the
 account's external withdraw whitelist when the rule is written and
 whenever a run pays it. Responses carry its canonical form.
destinationAddress.title: destination_address

destinationChainId.description:
Polyester chain id of the destination network: ChainConfig.chain_id
 from GetDepositWithdrawConfig, not the network's native chain id
 (ChainConfig.native_chain_id).
destinationChainId.title: destination_chain_id

maxAmountE18.description:
The most one run pays this asset, in 18-decimal asset units; at least
 min_amount_e18. A larger balance pays this ceiling and the rest stays on
 the account.
maxAmountE18.title: max_amount_e18

minAmountE18.description:
A run pays this asset only when the payable amount reaches this
 minimum, in 18-decimal asset units, and the rule's min_usd_value_e18;
 otherwise the balance stays on the account for a later run. Must be at
 least min_floor_e18 when the rule is set.
minAmountE18.title: min_amount_e18

minFloorE18.description:
Returned in responses only; ignored in requests. The least amount one
 payout to this destination can pay now, in 18-decimal asset units: the
 route's withdrawal minimum, and more than its current network fee. It
 follows the network fee, so it can change between reads. A run pays at
 least this floor and min_amount_e18, and a new rule needs a
 min_amount_e18 of at least the floor. Unset when the route or its network
 fee is not known now; a new rule for that destination is then refused
 with FEE_UNAVAILABLE or a route code.
minFloorE18.title: min_floor_e18

chain.withdraw.v1.AutoWithdrawPause.description: AutoWithdrawPause reports why a rule stopped running on its own.

assetId.description: Asset whose payout paused the rule; zero when no payout did.
assetId.title: asset_id

reason.description:
Machine-readable reason: destination_not_whitelisted when the
 destination left the account's external withdraw whitelist,
 destination_invalid when it is no longer a valid destination, or
 authority_revoked when the person who set the rule may no longer change
 it or withdraw from the account. On a broker vault the rule pauses with
 authority_revoked as soon as its author's broker role changes in any
 way: removed, demoted, or promoted (for example Finance to Owner), and
 also when the author is removed and added back. An Owner or Finance
 member resumes it with a fresh step-up.
reason.title: reason

chain.withdraw.v1.AutoWithdrawPause.title: AutoWithdrawPause

chain.withdraw.v1.AutoWithdrawPreviewAss.description:
AutoWithdrawPreviewAsset is what the next run would do with one asset,
 sized from the account's balance now.

assetId.description: Ledger asset.
assetId.title: asset_id

availableE18.description:
The account's available balance of the asset now, in 18-decimal asset
 units.
availableE18.title: available_e18

conversion.description:
Set on an asset the rule converts into its payout asset: what converting
 its whole available balance is quoted to deliver now. Such an asset pays
 nothing in kind (payable_e18 zero); its hold_reason is converts, or why
 it would stay on the account.
conversion.title: conversion

destinationAddress.description:
Canonical destination address; empty when the rule has no destination
 for the asset.
destinationAddress.title: destination_address

destinationChainId.description:
External destination chain identifier; zero when the rule has no
 destination for the asset.
destinationChainId.title: destination_chain_id

heldBackE18.description:
What would stay on the account, in 18-decimal asset units:
 available_e18 minus payable_e18.
heldBackE18.title: held_back_e18

holdReason.description:
Why held_back_e18 stays, or why nothing pays: below_minimum (below
 minimum_e18 or the rule's min_usd_value_e18), price_unavailable (the
 rule has a USD minimum and no current price values the asset),
 no_destination (the rule pays no destination for the asset),
 destination_cooling_down (a broker vault pays a destination only once
 it has been on the vault's external withdraw whitelist for 24 hours;
 see payable_from), above_max (the balance above max_amount_e18 stays),
 dust (less than one whole on-chain unit stays) or, on a rule with a
 payout asset, converts (the asset is converted into the payout asset
 instead; see conversion) or why it would not be converted (see
 conversion.skip_reason); empty when the whole balance pays.
holdReason.title: hold_reason

minimumE18.description:
The least one payout of the asset pays, in 18-decimal asset units: the
 destination's min_amount_e18, or its min_floor_e18 when that is higher
 and known now. Unset when the rule has no destination for the asset.
minimumE18.title: minimum_e18

networkFeeE18.description:
The network fee a payout to the destination is expected to be charged
 now, in 18-decimal asset units: the route's latest sampled network fee,
 the same figure min_floor_e18 stays above. It is taken out of the
 payout, so the destination receives about payable_e18 minus this fee.
 Unset when the rule has no destination for the asset or the fee is not
 known now.
networkFeeE18.title: network_fee_e18

networkFeeSampledAt.description: When network_fee_e18 was sampled; unset with it.

payableE18.description:

chain.withdraw.v1.CreateWalletTradingToF.description:
CreateWalletTradingToFundingBatchRequest moves up to 10 amounts from one
 Trading account to Funding accounts, authorized by one wallet personal_sign
 signature over the whole batch. The legs move together or not at all.

 The wallet signs the UTF-8 text below with EIP-191 personal_sign. Lines are
 separated by a single line feed (\n), with no trailing line feed. Numbers
 are base-10 integers without separators or leading zeros. The signer
 wallet and the verifying contract are lowercase 0x-prefixed hex. A leg's
 destination is its destination_address as sent, in the letter case sent
 (a checksummed address stays checksummed), without leading or trailing
 whitespace; an omitted destination_address leaves an empty value after
 "Destination: ". Values must not contain control characters.

     Polyester Trading Withdrawal Batch

     Version: 1
     Environment: polyester
     Action: TO_FUNDING
     Signer Wallet: <signer_wallet>
     Account ID: <the caller's public account ID>
     Target Account ID: <public ID of the source account: subaccount_id, or the account ID when omitted>
     Polyester Chain ID: <EVM chain ID of Polyester Chain, as eth_chainId returns it>
     Verifying Contract: <the withdraw verifying contract, as for CreateWalletTradingWithdraw>
     Deadline: <deadline_ts_sec>
     Nonce: <nonce>
     Idempotency Key: <idempotency_key>
     Legs: <number of legs>

     Leg 1 of <number of legs>
     Asset ID: <legs[0].asset_id>
     Amount E18: <legs[0].amount_e18>
     Destination: <legs[0].destination_address>

 followed by one such block per further leg, in request order, each after
 one empty line: "Leg 2 of <number of legs>", and so on. The header values
 are the ones a single wallet withdraw signs (CreateWalletTradingWithdraw),
 and the leg numbers bind the order of the legs. A batch signed for another
 chain ID or verifying contract is never paid.

deadlineTsSec.description:
Unix timestamp in seconds after which the signed batch is no longer
 accepted, at most 15 minutes ahead.
deadlineTsSec.title: deadline_ts_sec

idempotencyKey.description:
Client-chosen idempotency key for the whole batch, scoped to the source
 account. Retrying with the same key and the same signed batch returns the
 first answer; reusing it for another batch is refused with
 ERROR_CODE_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. The first answer stands, after the
 deadline too. A refused batch is final: a retry under its key answers the
 same refusal, even once its cause is gone, so a corrected batch needs a
 new key and signature.
idempotencyKey.title: idempotency_key

legs.description:
Moves to make, in order. 1 to 10 legs. Legs may repeat an asset or a
 destination.
legs.title: legs

nonce.description:
Client-generated unsigned 128-bit nonce bound to the signed batch. This
 is an identifier, not a decimal amount.
nonce.title: nonce

payloadSignature.description: EIP-191 personal_sign signature over the batch message described above.
payloadSignature.title: payload_signature

subaccountId.description:
Optional public subaccount id of the source Trading account. Omit to
 move funds from the caller's own Trading account.
subaccountId.title: subaccount_id

 match them by id.

startTime.description: Inclusive lower bound on post publication time. Optional.

 is no longer listed.

symbolId.title: symbol_id

checkpoints.v1.BiggestTrade.title: BiggestTrade

total.description: Number of operations and their USD total on this chain.

Checkpoint is one frozen season recap of a root account and all of its
 subaccounts. Only the account owner can read it.

badges.description: Badges earned in the season, in badge display order.
badges.title: badges

biggestTrade.description:
The fill valued biggest_trade_usd, the earliest on a tie. Omitted when no
 fill could be valued.
biggestTrade.title: biggest_trade

biggestTradeUsd.description:
Largest single trade fill in USD, encoded as a non-negative base-10
 decimal string without separators or a currency symbol.
biggestTradeUsd.title: biggest_trade_usd

busiestDay.description:
UTC date with the most trade fills, formatted as YYYY-MM-DD. Omitted
 without trades.
busiestDay.title: busiest_day

cancelRatio.description:
Share of placed orders that ended canceled, a base-10 decimal string from
 0 to 1.
cancelRatio.title: cancel_ratio

dailyClaimAmounts.description:
Daily claim totals per asset, by asset ascending, each valued in USD
 when it was paid. Assets excluded from value are listed by amount only.
dailyClaimAmounts.title: daily_claim_amounts

dailyVolume.description:
Volume and trade fills of every UTC day of the season, oldest first, days
 without trades included.
dailyVolume.title: daily_volume

daysActive.description: Number of UTC days with at least one trade.
daysActive.title: days_active

fillRate.description:
Share of placed orders that ended fully filled, a base-10 decimal string
 from 0 to 1.
fillRate.title: fill_rate

finalValueUsd.description:
USD value of all trading and funding balances at the end of the season
 that count toward account value, encoded as a base-10 decimal string.
 Assets excluded from value add nothing. Omitted when any other balance
 had no USD value.
finalValueUsd.title: final_value_usd

firstTradeAt.description: UTC time of the first trade fill in the season. Omitted without trades.
firstTradeAt.title: first_trade_at

fundingBalances.description:
Funding balance per asset at the end of the season, valued in USD at that
 time; assets excluded from value are listed by amount only. Shown for
 the record only.
fundingBalances.title: funding_balances

fundingByDay.description:
Deposit and withdrawal USD values per UTC day with at least one of them,
 oldest first.
fundingByDay.title: funding_by_day

incomplete.description:
Values computed from partial evidence, in ascending enum order. Empty
 when every value is exact.
incomplete.title: incomplete

inflowUsd.description:
USD value brought in during the season: daily claim payouts, deposits
 and transfers in, each valued when it happened, over assets that count
 toward account value; assets excluded from value add nothing. Encoded as
 a non-negative base-10 decimal string without separators or a currency
 symbol. Omitted when any other part had no USD value.
inflowUsd.title: inflow_usd

longestStreak.description: Longest run of consecutive UTC days with at least one trade.
longestStreak.title: longest_streak

makerTrades.description: Trade fills on the maker side.
makerTrades.title: maker_trades

medianLimitRestMs.description:
Typical time a good-till-canceled or good-till-date limit order rested
 before it filled or was canceled, in milliseconds. Omitted when no such
 order ended in the season.
medianLimitRestMs.title: median_limit_rest_ms

mostActiveHourUtc.description:
UTC hour of day, 0 through 23, with the most trade fills. Omitted without
 trades.
mostActiveHourUtc.title: most_active_hour_utc

netInflowUsd.description:
inflow_usd minus outflow_usd, encoded as a base-10 decimal string that
 may be negative. Omitted when either is omitted.
netInflowUsd.title: net_inflow_usd

number.description:
Positive checkpoint number. Checkpoint 1 is the first season; numbers
 increase by season.
number.title: number

openingValueUsd.description:
USD value of the funding balances restored to the account when the
 season opened, valued at the end of the season like final_value_usd,
 over assets that count toward account value; assets excluded from value
 add nothing. Encoded as a non-negative base-10 decimal string without
 separators or a currency symbol; "0" when the season opened with no
 balances. Omitted when a restored balance had no USD value.
openingValueUsd.title: opening_value_usd

outflowUsd.description:
USD value taken out during the season: withdrawals and transfers out,
 each valued when it happened, over assets that count toward account
 value; assets excluded from value add nothing. Encoded as a non-negative
 base-10 decimal string without separators or a currency symbol. Omitted

 and reserve rates can change then, or stay the same. Omitted when no

nextChangeAt.title: next_change_at

postOnlyReserveFeeRatePercent.description:
Fee rate a new post-only limit order on this market reserves its fee at
 when the fee is paid in the quote asset, encoded as a non-negative
 base-10 percentage string without a percent sign, between 0 and 100
 inclusive: the highest maker rate of every VIP tier under the fee
 schedule in force on this market, as reserve_fee_rate_percent describes.
postOnlyReserveFeeRatePercent.title: post_only_reserve_fee_rate_percent

reserveFeeRatePercent.description:
Fee rate a new order on this market reserves its fee at when the fee is
 paid in the quote asset, encoded as a non-negative base-10 percentage
 string without a percent sign, between 0 and 100 inclusive. It is the
 highest maker or taker rate of every VIP tier under the fee schedule in
 force on this market, so it is at least the effective rates and
 discounts never lower it. A buy limit order that pays its fee in the
 quote asset reserves N + F, computed in units of 10^-18 of the quote
 asset whatever the quote asset's own decimals: N is its price times its
 quantity rounded up to 10^-18, and F is N times this rate rounded up to
 10^-18. It has sufficient quote balance when N + F is at most the
 available quote balance, compared in the same 10^-18 units; other order
 validation and market limits still apply. A post-only limit order
 reserves at post_only_reserve_fee_rate_percent instead. An order that
 can only take, a market order or an IOC or FOK limit order such as a
 buy sized by a quote amount, fixes its fee cap when it is accepted: the
 lower of this rate and taker_fee_rate_percent in force then. A
 fixed-quantity buy among them that pays its fee in the quote asset
 reserves its fee at that cap; a buy sized by a quote amount holds its
 whole budget, which a lower cap lets buy more. A standalone stop-loss,
 take-profit or trailing stop whose order can only take fixes the cap
 when the stop is created, and each slice of a TWAP whose slices can
 only take when that slice is placed. Take-profit and stop-loss orders
 attached to an order or paired in an OCO, and orders that can rest, are
 capped at this rate, a post-only one at
 post_only_reserve_fee_rate_percent. Rates read before an order is sent
 are an estimate: a VIP tier or fee policy change before the order is
 accepted changes them. Each fill is charged the rate of the VIP tier
 and fee policy current when the fill is settled, never above the
 order's cap: in the quote asset on the fill's notional, or for a buy
 paying its fee in the base asset, in base on the quantity it receives.
 The cap is an upper bound on every fill, not a fixed rate: a VIP tier
 change after the order is accepted can move a later fill's rate up or
 down within it, but never above it. The rest of the reserve is released
 as the order fills or ends.
reserveFeeRatePercent.title: reserve_fee_rate_percent

fees.v1.SpotFeeRateBreakdown.description:
SpotFeeRateBreakdown lists the components of one market's effective fee
 rates in force. A client reproduces maker_fee_rate_percent and
 taker_fee_rate_percent exactly by applying the steps below to the maker
 and the taker rate separately, in this order, in integer arithmetic. Work
 in units of 0.0000001 percent: write every rate as an integer R, the
 percentage times 10,000,000. Write every multiplier and discount as an
 integer M or D, the percentage times 100. trunc(x / 10000) divides and
 rounds toward zero.

 1. Start from the VIP tier rate: R = tier_maker_fee_rate_percent or
    tier_taker_fee_rate_percent.
 2. When market_multiplier is set, multiply by it:
    R = trunc((R × M + 5000) / 10000).
 3. When R is above 0, let D be the highest maker or taker discount of
    account_discounts, 0 when the list is empty. When D is above 0, apply
    it: R = trunc((R × (10000 − D) + 5000) / 10000).
 4. When R is above 0 and referral_discount is set with a maker or taker
    discount D above 0, apply it the same way:
    R = trunc((R × (10000 − D) + 5000) / 10000).

 The result is the effective rate times 10,000,000. The steps multiply: a
 10% account discount and a 20% referral discount on a 0.1% rate leave
 0.1% × 0.9 × 0.8 = 0.072%. A negative maker rate is a rebate, which only
 the multiplier scales.

accountDiscounts.description:
Account discounts in force on this market, in no particular order. The
 highest maker discount and the highest taker discount apply, each
 possibly from a different discount.
accountDiscounts.title: account_discounts

marketMultiplier.description:
Fee schedule multipliers in force on this market. Omitted when none is
 in force, which leaves the tier rates unchanged.
marketMultiplier.title: market_multiplier

referralDiscount.description:
Referral discount in force for the account. Omitted when none is in
 force.
referralDiscount.title: referral_discount

tierMakerFeeRatePercent.description:
Maker fee rate of the account's VIP tier under the fee policy in force,
 before the market multiplier and discounts, encoded as a base-10
 percentage string without a percent sign. Values are between -100 and
 100 inclusive; a negative rate is a rebate.
tierMakerFeeRatePercent.title: tier_maker_fee_rate_percent

tierTakerFeeRatePercent.description:
Taker fee rate of the account's VIP tier under the fee policy in force,
 before the market multiplier and discounts, encoded as a non-negative
 base-10 percentage string without a percent sign, between 0 and 100
 inclusive.
tierTakerFeeRatePercent.title: tier_taker_fee_rate_percent
