google.protobuf.FieldMask.description:
`FieldMask` represents a set of symbolic field paths, for example:

     paths: "f.a"
     paths: "f.b.d"

 Here `f` represents a field in some root message, `a` and `b`
 fields in the message found in `f`, and `d` a field found in the
 message in `f.b`.

 Field masks are used to specify a subset of fields that should be
 returned by a get operation or modified by an update operation.
 Field masks also have a custom JSON encoding (see below).

 # Field Masks in Projections

 When used in the context of a projection, a response message or
 sub-message is filtered by the API to only contain those fields as
 specified in the mask. For example, if the mask in the previous
 example is applied to a response message as follows:

     f {
       a : 22
       b {
         d : 1
         x : 2
       }
       y : 13
     }
     z: 8

 The result will not contain specific values for fields x,y and z
 (their value will be set to the default, and omitted in proto text
 output):


     f {
       a : 22
       b {
         d : 1
       }
     }

 A repeated field is not allowed except at the last position of a
 paths string.

 If a FieldMask object is not present in a get operation, the
 operation applies to all fields (as if a FieldMask of all fields
 had been specified).

 Note that a field mask does not necessarily apply to the
 top-level response message. In case of a REST get operation, the
 field mask applies directly to the response, but in case of a REST
 list operation, the mask instead applies to each individual message
 in the returned resource list. In case of a REST custom method,
 other definitions may be used. Where the mask applies will be
 clearly documented together with its declaration in the API.  In
 any case, the effect on the returned resource/resources is required
 behavior for APIs.

 # Field Masks in Update Operations

 A field mask in update operations specifies which fields of the
 targeted resource are going to be updated. The API is required
 to only change the values of the fields as specified in the mask
 and leave the others untouched. If a resource is passed in to
 describe the updated values, the API ignores the values of all
 fields not covered by the mask.

 If a repeated field is specified for an update operation, new values will
 be appended to the existing repeated field in the target resource. Note that
 a repeated field is only allowed in the last position of a `paths` string.

 If a sub-message is specified in the last position of the field mask for an
 update operation, then new value will be merged into the existing sub-message
 in the target resource.

 For example, given the target message:

     f {
       b {
         d: 1
         x: 2
       }
       c: [1]
     }

 And an update message:

     f {
       b {
         d: 10
       }
       c: [2]
     }

 then if the field mask is:

  paths: ["f.b", "f.c"]

 then the result will be:

     f {
       b {
         d: 10
         x: 2
       }
       c: [1, 2]
     }

 An implementation may provide options to override this default behavior for
 repeated and message fields.

 In order to reset a field's value to the default, the field must
 be in the mask and set to the default value in the provided resource.
 Hence, in order to reset all fields of a resource, provide a default
 instance of the resource and set all fields in the mask, or do
 not provide a mask as described below.

 If a field mask is not present on update, the operation applies to
 all fields (as if a field mask of all fields has been specified).
 Note that in the presence of schema evolution, this may mean that
 fields the client does not know and has therefore not filled into
 the request will be reset to their default. If this is unwanted
 behavior, a specific service may require a client to always specify
 a field mask, producing an error if not.

 As with get operations, the location of the resource which
 describes the updated values in the request message depends on the
 operation kind. In any case, the effect of the field mask is
 required to be honored by the API.

 ## Considerations for HTTP REST

 The HTTP kind of an update operation which uses a field mask must
 be set to PATCH instead of PUT in order to satisfy HTTP semantics
 (PUT must only be used for full updates).

 # JSON Encoding of Field Masks

 In JSON, a field mask is encoded as a single string where paths are
 separated by a comma. Fields name in each path are converted
 to/from lower-camel naming conventions.

 As an example, consider the following message declarations:

     message Profile {
       User user = 1;
       Photo photo = 2;
     }
     message User {
       string display_name = 1;
       string address = 2;
     }

 In proto a field mask for `Profile` may look as such:

     mask {
       paths: "user.display_name"
       paths: "photo"
     }

 In JSON, the same mask is represented as below:

     {
       mask: "user.displayName,photo"
     }

 # Field Masks and Oneof Fields

 Field masks treat fields in oneofs just as regular fields. Consider the
 following message:

     message SampleMessage {
       oneof test_oneof {
         string name = 4;
         SubMessage sub_message = 9;
       }
     }

 The field mask can be:

     mask {
       paths: "name"
     }

 Or:

     mask {
       paths: "sub_message"
     }

 Note that oneof type names ("test_oneof" in this case) cannot be used in
 paths.

 ## Field Mask Verification

 The implementation of any API method which has a FieldMask type field in the
 request should verify the included field paths, and return an
 `INVALID_ARGUMENT` error if any path is unmappable.

ledger.read.v1.StatementExport.description:
StatementExport is a whole-period account statement produced in the
 background as one CSV file.

 The file is RFC 4180 CSV in UTF-8 with CRLF line endings: the header row,
 then every row of the period up to complete_through, oldest first. A period
 without movements yields the header row alone. Each row is the effect of
 one entry on one account bucket in one asset. An entry is one ledger
 operation, such as a trade with its fees, a deposit, a withdrawal step or an
 internal transfer.

 Columns, in order:
 - `time`: entry time, RFC 3339 in UTC with microseconds, for example
   `2026-11-12T19:52:07.734123Z`.
 - `entry_id`: entry identifier, an unsigned 128-bit integer as a decimal
   string. It is the `transfer_id` of the entry's first transfer leg on the
   account within the export's period, as LedgerReadService.ListTransfers
   returns it, and is the same whichever asset the export is limited to. A
   period boundary can fall between the legs of one entry: each export then
   holds its own part of the entry, under the `transfer_id` of that part's
   first leg, so do not join rows across periods on `entry_id` alone.
 - `type`: `trade` for a trade's settlement and its fees; otherwise the
   entry's transfer reason, such as `deposit`, `withdraw`,
   `internal_transfer`, `funding_to_trading` or `system_adjustment`.
 - `account`: account bucket, `funding` or `trading`.
 - `asset`: asset symbol.
 - `amount`: signed balance change of the entry in whole units of the
   asset, excluding the fees in `fee`, for example `-5000` or `0.1`. Fees
   the account receives are included here.
 - `fee`: fees the account paid in the asset for the entry, in whole units
   of the asset; `0` when none.
 - `balance`: account bucket balance in the asset after the entry, in whole
   units of the asset. For consecutive rows of the same bucket and asset,
   each balance equals the previous balance plus `amount` minus `fee`.
 - `link_id`: correlation ID shared by related transfer legs, the trade's
   match ID for trades; empty when unavailable.
 - `flow_id`: public lifecycle flow ID when the entry belongs to a chain
   lifecycle flow, such as a deposit, a withdrawal or an internal transfer,
   as LedgerReadService.ListTransfers returns it; empty otherwise.

 Amounts are exact decimal strings with up to 18 fractional digits and no
 trailing zeros.

 A READY file downloads in one of two ways:
 - StatementExportService.GetStatementExportDownloadUrl returns a URL valid
   for 60 seconds from signing that needs no credentials, so a browser can
   save the file straight to disk.
 - An authenticated `GET /v1/statements/exports/{exportId}/file` returns the
   file as `text/csv` and supports HTTP `Range` requests.

 Both save the file as `statement-<exportId>.csv`. Before the file is READY
 both answer FAILED_PRECONDITION with STATEMENT_EXPORT_NOT_READY, REST
 `409 Conflict`; a FAILED export answers STATEMENT_EXPORT_FAILED, REST `409`;
 an EXPIRED export, or a file already deleted, answers
 STATEMENT_EXPORT_EXPIRED, REST `410 Gone`, and so does a download URL
 request for a file with less than 5 seconds left; a CANCELED export
 answers STATEMENT_EXPORT_CANCELED, REST `409`. REST errors are
 `application/problem+json` whose `code` is the ErrorCode name, such as
 `STATEMENT_EXPORT_NOT_READY`: `401` without valid credentials, `403
 PERMISSION_DENIED` for an API key without READ_STATEMENTS, `404 NOT_FOUND`
 for an export the caller cannot read, and `503 UPSTREAM_ERROR`, with
 `Retry-After`, when the request can be retried.

 An export belongs to the root account whose session or API key created it.
 Any session or API key of that root that may read the export's account can
 read and download it, whichever of them created it. A member of a
 subaccount shared from another root sees only the exports its own root
 created, and the subaccount's owner does not see those: an export of
 another root, or of an account the caller can no longer read, answers
 NOT_FOUND, as one that does not exist.

marketdata.v1.GetCandlesRequest.description:
GetCandlesRequest selects a spot market candle series.

 The response is ordered newest-first by candle bucket start time. When both
 start_time and end_time are set, both bounds are inclusive.
start_time and end_time must not be more than 5 minutes in the future
end_time must be >= start_time when both are set

Inclusive upper bound for candle bucket start time, as a UTC timestamp.
 Must be greater than or equal to start_time when both are set, and must not

Include the current open candle when it is available and inside the
 requested range.
 The open candle is prepended to the newest-first candle list and does not
 count toward the closed-candle limit.

includeReference.description:
Include the composite reference market candle series for the same market,

 Reference candles cover only the time before the pair's listing: each one's
 bucket starts before the bucket that contains listing_at, as GetSpotConfig
 reports it. From that bucket on, the pair's own candles cover the market.
 Without listing_at no listing cutoff applies; availability, the requested
 range and pagination still do.
 The reference series can be empty when no reference series is available for
 the requested timeframe, or when the requested range starts after listing.
includeReference.title: include_reference

marketdata.v1.GetIndexPriceCandlesReques.description:
GetIndexPriceCandlesRequest selects one page of a spot market's index price
 candles.

 The series is continuous across the listing: buckets that start before the
 bucket containing the pair's listing_at (as GetSpotConfig reports it) are
 reference candles, and from that bucket on they are index price candles. A
 bucket is never both. Without listing_at, or with a listing_at in the future,
 the series is reference candles only. Only closed candles are returned,
 newest-first by bucket start time, with the same bucket alignment as
 GetCandles. When both start_time and end_time are set, both bounds are
 inclusive.
start_time and end_time must not be more than 5 minutes in the future
end_time must be >= start_time when both are set

endTime.description:
Inclusive upper bound for candle bucket start time, as a UTC timestamp.
 Must be greater than or equal to start_time when both are set, and must not

 response, bound to symbol_id, timeframe, and start_time and end_time as
 sent, an absent bound included. It continues toward older candles. At
 most 512 characters. For a known symbol_id, a cursor that is longer,
 malformed, from GetCandles or GetCandlesColumns, or bound to another
 request fails with invalid_argument (PAGE_TOKEN_INVALID); an unknown
 symbol_id fails with not_found (UNKNOWN_SYMBOL) first.

marketdata.v1.GetIndexPriceCandlesRespon.description:
GetIndexPriceCandlesResponse contains one page of a spot market's index price
 candles in columns: element i of every repeated field describes the same
 candle.

 Candles are ordered newest-first by ts_sec, strictly descending, with no
 two at the same ts_sec. There is no volume field: neither a reference candle
 nor an index price candle carries trading volume. Gaps exist: a bucket from
 the listing on in which the index price had no valid value is omitted, never
 filled from the reference series, so treat a missing ts_sec as a gap. Index
 price candles begin with the release that introduced them; buckets after a
 listing but before that release are omitted the same way. A closed candle
 appears once its series has processed the bucket, and candles of longer
 timeframes are refreshed periodically, so the newest closed candles can
 appear some time after their bucket closes. Reference candles of the most
 recent 48 hours can still be revised. Reference candles reach back 180 days
 at timeframes shorter than one hour, five years from one hour to twelve
 hours, and up to 20 years, as far as the market's history goes, at one day
 and longer. Index price candles are kept without a time limit.

low.title: low

marketdata.v1.GetTradesRequest.description:
GetTradesRequest selects recent public trades for one spot market.

 Results are ordered newest-first by execution timestamp, with match_id as a
 tie-breaker. When both start_time and end_time are set, both bounds are
 inclusive.

 With after_trade_id set, the request instead walks the symbol's trades by
 trade identifier (match_id), oldest first and gap-free, to backfill trades
 missed on a live stream: see after_trade_id.
after_trade_id cannot be combined with start_time, end_time, side or page_token
start_time and end_time must not be more than 5 minutes in the future
end_time must be >= start_time when both are set

afterTradeId.description:
Exclusive trade-identifier cursor for gap-free backfill. When set, the
 results are the symbol's trades with match_id greater than
 after_trade_id, ascending by match_id, up to limit, and only trades at or
 below the response's complete_through_trade_id: every page is gap-free.
 Trade identifiers order trades across epochs too, so a walk crosses
 epoch ends without a gap. Pass 0 to start from the symbol's first trade,
 then the response's next_after_trade_id. Cannot be combined with
 start_time, end_time, side or page_token.
afterTradeId.title: after_trade_id

endTime.description:
Inclusive upper bound for trade execution time. Must be greater than or
 equal to start_time when both are set, and must not be more than 5 minutes
 in the future.
endTime.title: end_time

limit.title: limit

Opaque keyset cursor from a previous response. The cursor is exclusive and
 bound to symbol, time bounds, side filter, and newest-first sort order.
pageToken.title: page_token

side.description: Optional filter by trade aggressor side. Unspecified returns both sides.
side.title: side

Inclusive lower bound for trade execution time. Must not be more than

startTime.title: start_time

symbolId.title: symbol_id

marketdata.v1.GetTradesResponse.description: GetTradesResponse contains public trades for one spot market.

completeThroughTradeId.description:
Set only with after_trade_id; 0 otherwise. Every trade of the symbol
 with match_id at or below this value exists and is returned by this
 method. Identifiers in that range that no trade has, the rest of an
 ended epoch and every identifier below a later epoch's first, are
 covered too. Newer trades may exist that are not available here yet; it
 only grows.
completeThroughTradeId.title: complete_through_trade_id

epochEnds.description:
Set only with after_trade_id. Every epoch whose last trade (or, for an
 epoch without trades, its start) lies between after_trade_id and
 next_after_trade_id, both inclusive, ascending by epoch. A page that
 ends exactly on an epoch's last trade is followed by a page that still
 reports that epoch's end.
epochEnds.title: epoch_ends

nextAfterTradeId.description:
Set only with after_trade_id; 0 otherwise. The after_trade_id of the
 next call; it never moves backwards. On a full page (limit trades) it is
 the last trade's match_id. Otherwise it is the greater of after_trade_id
 and complete_through_trade_id, so a walk progresses across epoch ends
 and empty epochs without trades to carry it. When it equals the
 request's after_trade_id, nothing newer is available yet: retry later
 with backoff.
nextAfterTradeId.title: next_after_trade_id

nextPageToken.description:
Opaque cursor for the next page. Empty when no more results exist, and
 always empty with after_trade_id.
nextPageToken.title: next_page_token

trades.description:
Trades ordered newest-first by execution timestamp, with match_id as a
 tie-breaker; with after_trade_id, ascending by match_id.
trades.title: trades

marketdata.v1.HeatmapDeltaBucket.description:
HeatmapDeltaBucket is one bucket's changes to the top-N view of both sides.
 A level that enters the top N during the bucket appears with its quantity,
 even when the bucket did not change it, for example after a better level
 was deleted. A level that leaves the top N appears with quantity zero, even
 when it still rests deeper in the book. Changes deeper than the top N are
 omitted.

asks.description: Changes to the top-N ask levels in this bucket.
asks.title: asks

bids.description: Changes to the top-N bid levels in this bucket.
bids.title: bids

bookSeqEnd.description: Latest monotonic order book sequence represented by this bucket.
bookSeqEnd.title: book_seq_end

bookSeqStart.description: Earliest monotonic order book sequence represented by this bucket.
bookSeqStart.title: book_seq_start

tsSec.description: Bucket start timestamp (seconds since epoch, UTC), aligned to `interval`.
tsSec.title: ts_sec

updatesInBucket.description: Number of upstream L2 updates aggregated into this interval bucket.
updatesInBucket.title: updates_in_bucket

marketdata.v1.HeatmapDeltaBucket.title: HeatmapDeltaBucket

marketdata.v1.HeatmapDeltaChain.description:
HeatmapDeltaChain is the historical payload for all intervals.
 Reconstruct by applying deltas over base_keyframe, oldest first: set each
 listed level's quantity, and delete it when the quantity is zero. After each
 bucket the result is exactly the top-N levels per side of the requested
 depth and quantity mode, the same at every page limit. No further clipping
 is needed.
 - CLOSE: the order book at the bucket's close. It equals the base_keyframe
   of a chain anchored at that bucket.
 - PEAK: each price's highest quantity during the bucket, among the prices
   that held liquidity during it.

baseKeyframe.description:
Top-N order book from which to apply the returned deltas, from strictly
 before the first of them. In CLOSE mode it holds closing quantities. In
 PEAK mode it is only the starting point of the replay, not a bucket view:
 its quantities may differ between page limits, so do not render it as a
 bucket. A base advanced through stored buckets holds the peaks of its last
 bucket, and a base taken from a stored keyframe holds that keyframe's

marketdata.v1.HeatmapLiveBucket.description:
HeatmapLiveBucket is the canonical live payload for real-time heatmap updates.
 It represents the latest state of one bucket (open or finalized). A bucket
 can be published again after it was finalized, when later updates for it
 arrive: the new payload holds every update of the bucket and a higher
 book_seq_end. Keep the payload with the highest book_seq_end per ts_sec.
 Finalized buckets are delivered at least once: the same finalized payload
 can arrive more than once, for example after a service restart; keep the
 highest book_seq_end per ts_sec. Updates of a bucket still open are best
 effort; a later update or the final payload supersedes them. A market's
 buckets are published here only once the service projects the market
 live: a bucket that holds only earlier updates is history, available
 through GetOrderbookHeatmap and never published live.

asks.description: Sparse ask-side level changes represented by this bucket.

bids.description: Sparse bid-side level changes represented by this bucket.

effectiveBinTicks.description:
Effective bin stride for this symbol as a price delta in 1e-9 quote-unit
 ticks.
effectiveBinTicks.title: effective_bin_ticks

isFinal.description:
True when this bucket is finalized; false for provisional updates to an
 open bucket. A finalized bucket can still be republished with a higher
 book_seq_end.
isFinal.title: is_final

quantityMode.description: Quantity semantics for qty_scaled in bids and asks.

marketdata.v1.LivePriceBand.description:
LivePriceBand is one pair's price band as of as_of_ts_ns: the reference
 price and the limit prices the pair admits. It is advisory: the pair checks
 every order against its own band when the order arrives, and the band may
 have moved by then.

 Limits are inclusive and side-specific. A buy limit order is checked
 against max_buy_price_ticks, and a sell limit order against
 min_sell_price_ticks; min_buy_price_ticks and max_sell_price_ticks apply
 only when present. REST responses render prices as decimal strings and
 times as RFC 3339 timestamps.

asOfTsNs.description:
When the band was last confirmed current, in nanoseconds since the Unix
 epoch (UTC).
asOfTsNs.title: as_of_ts_ns

epoch.description:
The band's epoch. It never decreases, and a band of a greater epoch is
 newer. Compare update_id only within one epoch.
epoch.title: epoch

maxBuyPriceTicks.description:
The highest buy limit price admitted, inclusive, in quote-asset units
 scaled by 1e9. Present only when the state is ACTIVE.
maxBuyPriceTicks.title: max_buy_price_ticks

maxSellPriceTicks.description:
The highest sell limit price admitted, inclusive, in quote-asset units
 scaled by 1e9. Present only when the state is ACTIVE and the band limits
 passive prices too; absent otherwise, when any sell price above
 min_sell_price_ticks is admitted.
maxSellPriceTicks.title: max_sell_price_ticks

minBuyPriceTicks.description:
The lowest buy limit price admitted, inclusive, in quote-asset units
 scaled by 1e9. Present only when the state is ACTIVE and the band limits
 passive prices too; absent otherwise, when any buy price below
 max_buy_price_ticks is admitted.
minBuyPriceTicks.title: min_buy_price_ticks

minSellPriceTicks.description:
The lowest sell limit price admitted, inclusive, in quote-asset units
 scaled by 1e9. Present only when the state is ACTIVE.
minSellPriceTicks.title: min_sell_price_ticks

parameters.description:
The band's settings, as GetSpotConfig returns them. Absent when the state
 is OFF, or when the settings in effect cannot be expressed exactly in
 basis points and milliseconds; the limits above are authoritative either
 way.
parameters.title: parameters

reanchorEligibleTsNs.description:
From when the next order operation on the pair may move the reference
 price, in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC). Nothing moves at that
 time by itself: from then on, an order, modification, cancellation or
 trigger on the pair can move the reference to a newer trade's price, or to
 the index price. Present when the state is ACTIVE or EMPTY.
reanchorEligibleTsNs.title: reanchor_eligible_ts_ns

reanchorPending.description:
True when a trade newer than the reference price is waiting: once the
 re-anchor eligibility time has passed, the next order operation moves the
 reference to it, unless the index price moves it instead. False does not
 promise that the band stays: a move to the index price needs no trade.
reanchorPending.title: reanchor_pending

referencePriceTicks.description:
The band's reference price in quote-asset units scaled by 1e9. Present
 when the state is ACTIVE or EMPTY.
referencePriceTicks.title: reference_price_ticks

referenceSource.description:
Where the reference price came from. REFERENCE_SOURCE_UNSPECIFIED when
 the state is OFF or UNKNOWN.
referenceSource.title: reference_source

symbolId.description: Stable numeric pair id from GetSpotConfig.
symbolId.title: symbol_id

updateId.description:
Increases with each band update within an epoch, and may increase without
 one. Compare it only within one epoch: a greater value is newer.
updateId.title: update_id

updatedTsNs.description:
When the band last changed, in nanoseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC): its
 first setting, OFF included, a change of its settings, or a move of its
 reference price, to the same price included.
updatedTsNs.title: updated_ts_ns

validUntilTsNs.description:
as_of_ts_ns plus 5 seconds. After it, treat the band as unknown and read
 it again.
validUntilTsNs.title: valid_until_ts_ns

maxLimitQtyBase.description:
Largest quantity of one limit order, as a decimal string in base-asset
 units. A replace is checked on its new total less the quantity already
 filled. An order above it is rejected with MAX_QTY. Absent when the pair
 has no maximum.
maxLimitQtyBase.title: max_limit_qty_base

maxMarketNotionalQuote.description:
Additional maximum notional for market orders as a decimal string in
 quote-asset units. Base-sized market orders are valued at the buy protection
 price or the sell reference price before slippage, without rounding. For
 quote-sized market buys, the entire all-in maximum quote debit must also fit
 this maximum, and for quote-sized market sells the entire quote proceeds
 target. Exceeding it returns MAX_NOTIONAL. Absent when no maximum is

maxMarketQtyBase.description:
Largest quantity of one market order, as a decimal string in base-asset

 base. An order above it is rejected with MAX_QTY. Absent when the pair
 has no maximum.

The venue's default limit on resting orders a typical account may hold on
 this pair at once: good-till-cancelled and good-till-date orders that have
 not ended. Immediate-or-cancel, fill-or-kill and market orders never
 count, and a replaced order keeps its place. An order past it is rejected
 with MAX_OPEN_ORDERS_PER_PAIR. An account may have a lower limit of its
 own; that is not part of this public configuration and would be returned
 by an account-scoped read.
maxOpenOrdersPerPair.title: max_open_orders_per_pair

maxOrderNotionalQuote.description:
Maximum per-order notional as a decimal string in quote-asset units.
 Base-sized orders are checked using quantity times limit price, or market
 protection price, without rounding. For quote-sized buys, the entire all-in
 maximum quote debit must also fit this maximum, and for quote-sized sells
 the entire quote proceeds target. Exceeding it returns MAX_NOTIONAL.
 Absent when no maximum is configured.

marketdata.v1.PriceBand.description:
PriceBand limits how far from the market an order may be priced or trade.
 Its reference price follows the pair's last trade, updated at most once
 per reference window, and moves to the pair's index price when the two
 diverge by more than the band. A buy limit order priced above the upper
 limit, or a sell limit order priced below the lower limit, is rejected with
 PRICE_BAND_VIOLATION. A market order, or another order whose price the
 exchange sets, trades only up to the limit; its unfilled remainder is
 canceled with CANCEL_REASON_PRICE_BAND. A resting order is never canceled
 by the band, and a limit order priced away from the market on the passive
 side is accepted.

lowerBps.description:
How far below the reference price a sell may be priced or trade, in
 basis points (1 bp = 0.01%). The lower limit is the reference price times
 (1 - lower_bps / 10000), rounded up to the tick size.
lowerBps.title: lower_bps

referenceWindowMs.description:
How long the reference price stays fixed before it can move to a newer
 trade, in milliseconds. Zero moves it with every order.
referenceWindowMs.title: reference_window_ms

upperBps.description:
How far above the reference price a buy may be priced or trade, in basis
 points. The upper limit is the reference price times
 (1 + upper_bps / 10000), rounded down to the tick size.
upperBps.title: upper_bps

marketdata.v1.PriceBandReferenceSource.description: PriceBandReferenceSource is where a band's reference price came from.
marketdata.v1.PriceBandReferenceSource.title: PriceBandReferenceSource

marketdata.v1.PriceBandState.description: PriceBandState is a pair's price band state.
marketdata.v1.PriceBandState.title: PriceBandState

marketdata.v1.SideFilter.title: SideFilter

marketdata.v1.Timeframe.description:
Timeframe represents an OHLCV candle bucket.

 All buckets are in UTC; daylight saving time never shifts a boundary.
 Fixed-duration buckets start at whole multiples of their duration since
 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z, so every bucket up to 1 day starts on a UTC midnight
 boundary and `DAY_3` buckets start every third day counted from
 1970-01-01. `WEEK_1` buckets start on Monday 00:00 UTC. `MONTH_1` is
 calendar-based (UTC month boundaries). Values are listed shortest first.
marketdata.v1.Timeframe.title: Timeframe

marketdata.v1.TradeEpochEnd.description:
TradeEpochEnd reports where one epoch of a symbol's trade identifiers
 ended. Trade identifiers of epoch e are greater than (e-1) * 2^40 and less
 than e * 2^40; a later epoch's identifiers are greater than every earlier
 epoch's.

lastTradeId.description:
match_id of the epoch's last trade; (epoch-1) * 2^40 when the epoch
 ended without trades.
lastTradeId.title: last_trade_id

marketoverview.v1.GetSpotVolumeHistoryRe.description:
Aligned columnar trailing-24h USD series over the most recent 24 hours.
 The grid always contains 97 samples ending at the latest completed UTC
 quarter-hour. Index i maps to start_ts_sec + i * 900 seconds. Each sample
 covers [sample time - 24h, sample time); only the preceding 48 hours contribute.
 USD conversion uses historical quote/USD prices at each completed bucket
 boundary. When conversion is unavailable, USDT and USDC are valued at USD parity.
 If any contributing trade cannot be valued, or a USD amount overflows,
 the RPC fails as unavailable; partial or zero-filled valuations are not returned.
 Intervals without executed trades are zero. Results may be reused for 15 seconds.

bucket.description: Sampling interval between points; currently always "15m".
bucket.title: bucket

endTsSec.description: Last sample timestamp in seconds since Unix epoch (UTC), inclusive.
endTsSec.title: end_ts_sec

pairs.title: pairs

points.title: points

 Do not sum overlapping trailing-24h samples to obtain period traded volume.

marketoverview.v1.ListMarketOverviewRequ.description:
ListMarketOverviewRequest lists market overview rows. The symbol_id
 filter and the range filters combine: a market is returned only when it
 matches every filter given. Filters apply before sorting and paging.
 A range whose minimum exceeds its maximum is refused as invalid, with a
 violation on the range field (last_price, change_24h or volume_24h); a
 negative price or volume bound is refused with a violation on the bound
 itself, such as last_price.max_ticks.

change24h.description:
Only markets whose signed change_24h_bps is within this range; sorting by
 ORDER_BY_CHANGE_24H_BPS still uses the absolute change. When a bound is
 set, a market whose 24h change has no open (open_24h_ticks is 0) never
 matches. Omit for no change filter.
change24h.title: change_24h

includeSparklines.description: When true, include sparklines in each MarketOverview.
includeSparklines.title: include_sparklines

lastPrice.description:
Only markets whose last_price_ticks is within this range. When a bound is
 set, a market with no trade yet never matches. Omit for no price filter.
lastPrice.title: last_price

limit.description:
Maximum number of markets to return. Defaults to 50 when omitted; maximum
 is 2000.
limit.title: limit

orderBy.description: Sort key. When unset/UNSPECIFIED, defaults to descending 24h USD volume.
orderBy.title: order_by

pageToken.description:
Opaque keyset cursor from a previous response. The cursor is exclusive and
 bound to symbol IDs, the range filters, sort key, and sort direction:
 reuse it with the same filters. A cursor reused with other filters or
 another sort is refused as invalid; request the first page again.
 Sparkline options affect only response enrichment and may change between
 pages. Each page is cut from current values, so a market whose sort value
 or range membership changes between pages can appear twice or not at all
 across them. For a consistent list, request a single page with the
 maximum limit.
pageToken.title: page_token

sparklineIntervals.description:
Which sparklines to include. If empty and include_sparklines is true,
 server defaults to 24h.
sparklineIntervals.title: sparkline_intervals

symbolId.description:
Filter by stable numeric pair IDs from GetSpotConfig. When empty, returns
 every configured market, including disabled ones. An ID that names no
 configured market is rejected as invalid. Markets whose delisting time has
 passed are never returned.
symbolId.title: symbol_id

volume24h.description:
Only markets whose volume_24h_usd_scaled is within this range. When a
 bound is set, a market whose USD volume is omitted never matches. Omit
 for no volume filter.
volume24h.title: volume_24h

markets.description: Market overview rows for the requested page.
markets.title: markets

nextPageToken.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Empty when no more results exist.
nextPageToken.title: next_page_token

bestAskQtyScaled.description:

 24h open is the price at the start of the minute that contains the time
 24h ago or, for a market that first traded later, its first trade. 0 while
 the 24h open is unavailable (open_24h_ticks is 0 then): the market has no
 trade yet (its last trade timestamp is 0 too), its first trade is a few
 seconds old, or its trade history is temporarily unavailable.

high24hTicks.description:
Rolling 24h stats. The 24h window starts at the start of the minute that
 contains the time 24h ago and ends now; its prices, volumes and trade
 count cover the same window.

 quote units scaled by 1e9.
high24hTicks.title: high_24h_ticks

Current multi-venue index price in quote units scaled by 1e9.

low24hTicks.description:
Lowest price in the 24h window, counting its open and every trade, in

The 24h open that change_24h_bps is measured from, in quote units scaled

 few seconds old, or its trade history cannot be read for a while.

 scaled by 1e9: the last trade price before the day's first minute or, for

 the day open is last_price_ticks against this price. 0 while the open is

 means no fresh band is known, not that the pair has no band. This is a
 convenience copy: the market overview stream sends a row again when its
 band changes, appears or lapses, not on each confirmation, so a copy whose
 valid_until_ts_ns has passed is unknown. Check order prices against
 GetPriceBand or the price band stream.
priceBand.title: price_band

stats1h.description:
Rolling 1h stats, over the same minute-granular window as the 24h stats.
 Absent while the window's open is unavailable, including when history is
 temporarily unavailable: the market has no trade yet, its first trade is
 a few seconds old, or the window's trade history cannot be read for a
 while. Later fields may add volumes per window.

volume24hBaseScaled.description:

volume24hBaseScaled.title: volume_24h_base_scaled

volume24hQuoteScaled.description:
Rolling 24h quote volume scaled by the pair's quote_quantity_scale from
 GetSpotConfig. Omitted if the amount exceeds the signed 64-bit range.
volume24hQuoteScaled.title: volume_24h_quote_scaled

volume24hUsdScaled.description:
Rolling 24h USD volume, scaled by 1e6 (one unit is 0.000001 USD).
 Applies the current quote/USD conversion to the rolling quote volume.
 When conversion is unavailable, USDT and USDC are valued at USD parity.
 Omitted for other quote assets when a current conversion is unavailable.
volume24hUsdScaled.title: volume_24h_usd_scaled

vwap24hTicks.description:
24h volume-weighted average trade price in quote units scaled by 1e9,
 rounded down: the exact 24h quote notional divided by the 24h base volume.
 The notional is not rounded to the quote scale, so dividing the displayed
 volume_24h_quote_scaled by volume_24h_base_scaled can differ slightly;
 clients cannot reproduce this value from the displayed volumes. The base
 volume is exact when the base asset's market_data_volume_scale equals its
 quantity_scale in GetSpotConfig. Otherwise each second with trades rounds
 its base volume to the volume scale, by at most half of one volume unit,
 so the base volume can be off by that much per second with trades and the
 price error shrinks as the total base volume grows. Omitted when the
 window has no base volume or the 24h base volume is omitted.
vwap24hTicks.title: vwap_24h_ticks

depth.description:
Price levels per side. Every tier is served; DEPTH_UNSPECIFIED selects
 DEPTH_50. To follow the book in real time, subscribe to the order book
 stream at a streamed tier, then fetch this snapshot at exactly that tier.
depth.title: depth

orderbook.v1.GetOrderBookRequest.title: GetOrderBookRequest

orderbook.v1.GetOrderBookResponse.description:
GetOrderBookResponse is a depth snapshot for the binary (protobuf) API (scaled integers).
 REST surfaces expose decimal strings via DTO conversion. A configured symbol
 whose book is being built, or was invalidated, returns a successful snapshot
 with available false and no levels: its book is unknown, not empty. Read
 available before treating empty sides as no liquidity.

asks.description:
Best ask first; ascending price. When available is true, empty means no
 current liquidity; when it is false, always empty.
asks.title: asks

available.description:
True when the book is current: bids and asks are its levels, and empty
 sides mean no liquidity. False while the book is being built or after it
 was invalidated: its levels are unknown, not empty, and the response
 carries none. Request the snapshot again later.
available.title: available

bids.description:
Best bid first; descending price. When available is true, empty means no
 current liquidity; when it is false, always empty.
bids.title: bids

bookEpoch.description:
Epoch of book_seq. Order snapshots by (book_epoch, book_seq): a higher
 epoch is newer whatever its book_seq, and a new epoch may restart
 book_seq. Discard a snapshot whose epoch is older than the newest one
 seen for the symbol. 0 while available is false.
bookEpoch.title: book_epoch

bookSeq.description:
Book sequence of this snapshot within book_epoch. Monotonic within one
 epoch; compare it only with sequences of the same epoch.
bookSeq.title: book_seq

depth.description:
Tier this snapshot was served at: the request's depth, or DEPTH_50 when
 the request left it unset. Set in every response, available or not.
depth.title: depth

symbolId.description: Numeric symbol identifier (client resolves to symbol string).
symbolId.title: symbol_id

 quote_proceeds_scaled SELL), the quantity the quote amount buys or sells at

 successor order under a new order ID, with its queue priority reset. Either

orders.v1.BatchReplaceOrdersRequest.description:
BatchReplaceOrdersRequest modifies same-symbol orders as one quote refresh:
 each item is amended in place or replaced as ModifyOrder decides by default.
 A request can be refused as a whole before admission, changing nothing: for
 example an invalid request_id or number of items, an item that names no
 order, supplies no patch field or breaks a field rule, or a failed
 authentication, permission or receive-window check. Once a request reaches
 admission, each item is admitted or rejected on its own.
 Identical retries replay the admission result for 60 seconds from acceptance;
 a different payload under the same key conflicts. Use a fresh key for a new batch.
 Read the batch's status with GetBatchReplaceStatus within the same window;
 after it, reconcile the individual orders and never resubmit an accepted batch.
 The response answers admission, before an admitted item's change completes.
 Until it completes, a later change of that order, an item of the next batch
 included, is rejected with a retryable code: ORDER_MODIFY_IN_PROGRESS when it
 names the order by client order ID, and ORDER_PLACEMENT_PENDING (or
 ORDER_MODIFY_IN_PROGRESS) when it names the replacement_order_id returned
 here. Resend only the rejected items, in a new batch under a fresh key, after
 a short backoff: the rejected batch's key keeps replaying its rejection, and
 admitted items must not be sent again.
 An admitted item that amends or replaces its order can still be refused when
 it applies: the item changes nothing, leaving the order as it was (at its old
 price, quantity and client order ID unless it had ended), and a refused
 replacement's successor never exists as an order. Such an item that has not applied 2 seconds after its admission is
 refused with ERROR_CODE_MODIFY_APPLY_EXPIRED, so none applies later than
 that. The trading WebSocket reports each such refusal with one
 BatchReplaceItemReject, which can arrive before this response. A refusal at
 admission is reported in this response alone, so the same code there means
 the item was never admitted. For 60 seconds from acceptance,
 GetBatchReplaceStatus reports a refused item as REJECTED, and GetOrder of a
 refused replacement's successor answers REJECTED with the same code, with no
 order terms: you know them from the batch you sent. After
 that window, a successor that is not found while the order it would have
 replaced is not CANCELED with CANCEL_REASON_REPLACED never becomes an order:
 the item was refused, or it applied by ending that order at its filled
 quantity, which that order's CANCEL_REASON_QTY_AT_OR_BELOW_FILLED shows
 unless a later change of yours ended it so.
each item target must be unique within a batch

orders.v1.CancelAllAfterRequest.description:
CancelAllAfterRequest arms/disables a dead-man switch for automatic cancel-all.
 When the switch fires, it cancels what a CancelAllOrders with the same

 See CancelAllAfter.

If true, the switch's expiry also stops the account's triggers in its
 scope, as CancelAllOrders with `include_triggers` does: those created
 before the expiry time, even when the expiry is processed later, and
 none of them places an order once it is processed. A trigger created at
 or after the expiry time is not stopped. Defaults to false: only orders
 are canceled on expiry. Each arm or refresh sets it again; a disable
 ignores it.

CancelAllOrdersRequest cancels all matching open orders for an account,

 ladders and attached legs without it. To cancel triggers without

 stop-loss, take-profit, trailing stop, TWAP, ladder, standalone OCO (both

 matched symbols whose orders trade on the side filter, created before the
 request was accepted. Each ends canceled with reason
 `TRIGGER_CANCEL_REASON_CANCEL_ALL` and releases its reserved funds, its
 open orders are canceled with the others, and none places an order after

fieldPath.description:
Protobuf field path, using canonical field names, relative to the message

 in that request, a batch item's field under its index (items[i]). A batch
 item's own result answers that item alone and names the field in the
 item, without its index. A BatchCreateOrders item's rejection
 (BatchCreateRejected) names it as a CreateOrderRequest carrying the item
 would, under order, for example
 order.attached_risk.take_profit.trigger_price_ticks; the item is the
 result's position in the response. A BatchReplaceOrders item's error
 (BatchReplaceAdmissionItem) names it as the request item does, for
 example new_attached_risk.stop_loss or order_id; the item is the result's
 item_index. REST names the same fields by REST field names: a
 BatchCreateOrders item's as a REST create carrying it would, for example
 order.attachedRisk.takeProfit.triggerPrice, and a BatchReplaceOrders
 item's as the REST request item does, for example newPrice.

orders.v1.GetBatchReplaceStatusRequest.description:
GetBatchReplaceStatusRequest retrieves one accepted batch by server identity.
 A batch's status is retained for 60 seconds from its acceptance, the same
 time-limited window in which an identical retry replays its admission. It
 is readable as soon as BatchReplaceOrders returns; each item's execution
 phase then advances asynchronously. UNAVAILABLE means the status cannot be
 established yet: retry the same request within the window. NOT_FOUND means
 the account has no retained batch with this identity: none was accepted for
 it, or the window ended. NOT_FOUND never proves that a replacement was
 rejected. After the window, reconcile the individual orders, and never
 submit an accepted batch again because its status is not found.

displayQtyScaled.description:
Optional iceberg display quantity, scaled by the pair's
 base_quantity_scale from GetSpotConfig. Zero places a plain order. When
 positive, the order book shows at most this quantity of the order; once
 that shown part is fully executed, the next part is shown at the same
 price, behind the orders already resting there. It must be below
 base_qty_scaled, a multiple of the pair's quantity step, at least the
 pair's minimum quantity, and at least base_qty_scaled divided by 100,
 rounded up, so the order splits into at most 100 parts: otherwise the
 order is refused with ICEBERG_DISPLAY_TOO_SMALL or
 ICEBERG_DISPLAY_INVALID. An iceberg order cannot carry attached_risk
 (ICEBERG_NOT_ALLOWED). The display cannot be modified. Lowering the
 order's quantity in place to the display or below is allowed: the order
 then shows all of its remaining quantity. A replace keeps the display
 while the new quantity is above it; otherwise the new order is a plain
 order with no display.
displayQtyScaled.title: display_qty_scaled

orders.v1.MarketIoc.description:
MarketIoc configures a market order. Market orders always execute as
 immediate-or-cancel and therefore cannot rest or be post-only.

 The order fills only up to its protection price, a BUY at or below it and
 a SELL at or above it. The protection price is the reference price
 (client_ref_price_ticks, or the server's reference when it is omitted)
 moved by the maximum slippage, up for a BUY and down for a SELL, then put
 on the pair's tick grid toward the reference: a BUY's is rounded down and
 a SELL's up, so it never allows more than the slippage and can be up to
 one tick tighter. Neither client_ref_price_ticks nor max_slippage_ticks
 has to be a multiple of the pair's tick size; only the protection price
 is. For example, on a pair whose tick size is 0.01, a reference of
 73840.125 and a slippage of 50.12 give a BUY protection price of 73890.24
 (73890.245 rounded down) and a SELL protection price of 73790.01
 (73790.005 rounded up). The order's price_ticks shows the protection
 price; market_client_ref_price_ticks and market_max_slippage_ticks show
 the values exactly as given.

clientRefPriceTicks.description:
Optional positive client reference price in quote units scaled by 1e9
 (1e-9 quote units, not the pair's tick size). It need not be on the
 pair's tick grid; only the protection price derived from it is, as
 MarketIoc describes. When omitted, admission uses server-side reference
 pricing. A reference too far from the server's is refused with
 ERROR_CODE_STALE_QUOTE.
clientRefPriceTicks.title: client_ref_price_ticks

maxSlippageBps.description:
Maximum allowed slippage in basis points (1 bp = 0.01%), from 1 to 10000.
 A SELL order accepts at most 9999: a 100% cap would leave it no
 positive price to sell at, so 10000 is rejected with
 ERROR_CODE_MAX_SLIPPAGE_INVALID.
maxSlippageBps.title: max_slippage_bps

maxSlippageTicks.description:
Positive maximum absolute price delta in quote units scaled by 1e9. The
 "ticks" in this name are 1e-9 quote units, not the pair's tick size,
 and the value need not be a multiple of the pair's tick size: the
 protection price derived from it is put on the tick grid toward the
 reference, as MarketIoc describes.
maxSlippageTicks.title: max_slippage_ticks

orders.v1.MarketIoc.title: MarketIoc

orders.v1.ModifyBehavior.description:
ModifyBehavior controls how ModifyOrder should handle amend-vs-replace paths.
 MODIFY_BEHAVIOR_UNSPECIFIED is treated as AMEND_OR_REPLACE by server logic.

 An amend keeps the order in place, under the same order ID and with its
 queue priority kept; a replace ends it and creates a successor under a new
 order ID, with its queue priority reset. Either way, a new total quantity at
 or below the order's filled quantity when the change applies, fills after
 the request was sent included, ends the order at its filled quantity
 (CANCEL_REASON_QTY_AT_OR_BELOW_FILLED) with no successor, and ModifyOrder
 answers AMENDED with the order's ID rather than an error.

 Order the states of one order ID by version (Order.version), keeping the
 highest applied. A terminal status is final: no later state of that order ID
 is open. Price and quantity order only two open states of one GTC or GTD
 limit order at version 1 or above: its price stays the same and its total
 quantity never rises, so the state with the larger total quantity is the
 older.
orders.v1.ModifyBehavior.title: ModifyBehavior
