attachedRisk.description:
Attached risk controls + runtime state on the parent order.
 Empty when no attached risk exists. Order reads include it only when the
 request asks for it (include_attached_risk, include_attached_risk_state):
 an omission on request, never a removal. The private WebSocket always
 carries it in full, as a read asking for both does.
attachedRisk.title: attached_risk

avgPriceE18.description:
Average execution price across the lineage through this generation, in
 quote units scaled by 1e18: the exact executed quote amount divided by
 cum_qty_scaled, rounded half to even at the 18th decimal. Unset if no
 fills.
avgPriceE18.title: avg_price_e18

avgPriceTicks.description:
Average execution price across the lineage through this generation,
 in quote units scaled by 1e9, rounded down. Zero if no fills.
 avg_price_e18 carries the exact average.
avgPriceTicks.title: avg_price_ticks

batchRequestId.description:
Batch-replace identity that admitted this order, retained after it ends.
 Also set for batch-replaced trigger-generated orders. Zero when this order
 was not admitted by a batch replacement; a later batch replacing this order
 does not change its admission identity.
batchRequestId.title: batch_request_id

cancelReason.description:
For a CANCELED order, why it ended. Not set for every other status; JSON
 and REST responses then omit it.
cancelReason.title: cancel_reason

clientOrderId.description:
Client-provided, account-scoped identifier for correlation, lookup, and
 cancellation. Empty when none was supplied.
clientOrderId.title: client_order_id

createdTsNs.description: Creation timestamp in nanoseconds since epoch (UTC).
createdTsNs.title: created_ts_ns

cumNotional.description:
Exact quote amount of the fills across the lineage through this
 generation, before fees: the sum over the fills of their quantity,
 scaled as cum_qty_scaled, times their price in quote units scaled by
 1e9. It is in quote units scaled by 10^(9 + base_quantity_scale), with
 the pair's base_quantity_scale from GetSpotConfig for symbol_id; REST
 shows it in quote units. avg_price_e18 is this amount over
 cum_qty_scaled. Unset if no fills. A fill settles its quote rounded down
 to 18 decimal places, which is this amount exactly unless
 base_quantity_scale is above 9.

 For a BUY sized by a quote amount (submitted_max_quote_debit_scaled),
 the quote the order used is this amount plus fee_total's amount_e18
 when fee_asset is QUOTE, or minus it when fee_total's is_rebate is true,
 since a rebate is credited; it is this amount alone when fee_asset is
 BASE, whose fee is taken from the base received. What it left unspent is
 submitted_max_quote_debit_scaled less the quote it used.

 For a SELL sized by a quote proceeds target
 (submitted_quote_proceeds_scaled), this amount is the proceeds it
 received before fees, never above the target; the quote it was credited
 is this amount less fee_total's amount_e18, or plus it when fee_total's
 is_rebate is true. What it did not receive is
 submitted_quote_proceeds_scaled less this amount.
cumNotional.title: cum_notional

cumQtyScaled.description:
Cumulative filled quantity across the lineage through this generation,
 scaled by the pair's base_quantity_scale from GetSpotConfig for symbol_id.
cumQtyScaled.title: cum_qty_scaled

displayQtyScaled.description:
Iceberg display quantity the order was placed with, scaled by the pair's
 base_quantity_scale from GetSpotConfig for symbol_id: the most of the
 order the order book shows at once. Zero for a plain order. A replace
 keeps it while the new quantity is above it; a replace to the display or
 below it is a plain order, zero here.
displayQtyScaled.title: display_qty_scaled

expireAt.description:
Exact UTC expiry time for GTD orders, within the supported signed
 Unix-nanosecond range from 1677-09-21T00:12:43.145224193Z through
 2262-04-11T23:47:16.854775807Z. Omitted for all other time-in-force policies.
 The order cannot execute when the current time equals this value.
expireAt.title: expire_at

feeAsset.description:
Fee asset selected for fills.
 Unset for the replacement order of a batch item refused when it applied
 (REJECTED with batch_request_id set), which never existed and carries no
 order terms: the client knows them from the batch it sent.
feeAsset.title: fee_asset

feeTotal.description:
Total fee of the fills across the lineage through this generation, net
 of rebates, in the order's fee asset. A fill's fee is recorded once the
 fill is settled, which can be seconds after the order ended.

 Order history reads and single-order reads that include execution
 history (the default) carry it, over the fills recorded so far: its
 quantity shows which fills it covers, and it is the order's whole fee
 once that quantity equals the order's filled quantity. Open-order reads,
 single-order reads without execution history and private stream order
 updates leave it unset, an ended order's update included.

 To show the fee of an order seen on the private stream, or the quote a
 BUY sized by a quote amount used: once an update shows the order ended
 with a filled quantity above zero, read the order by its ID, and read it
 again, a few hundred milliseconds apart, until the fee total's quantity
 equals the order's filled quantity.
feeTotal.title: fee_total

hiddenQtyScaled.description:
Part of leaves_qty_scaled an iceberg order keeps hidden from the order
 book, scaled by the pair's base_quantity_scale from GetSpotConfig for
 symbol_id. The order book shows leaves_qty_scaled minus this quantity.
 Zero for a plain order and for terminal orders.
hiddenQtyScaled.title: hidden_qty_scaled

inheritedCumQtyScaled.description:
Cumulative filled base quantity inherited from predecessors when this
 replacement was accepted, scaled by the pair's base_quantity_scale from
 GetSpotConfig for symbol_id. Zero for the original order and immutable
 within a generation. cum_qty_scaled minus this value is the quantity
 executed by this generation, not the quantity new to a client session.
inheritedCumQtyScaled.title: inherited_cum_qty_scaled

leavesQtyScaled.description:
Remaining working quantity scaled by the pair's base_quantity_scale from
 GetSpotConfig for symbol_id. Zero for terminal orders.
leavesQtyScaled.title: leaves_qty_scaled

lineage.description:
Logical-order identity and requested generation. Always populated by order reads.
 A batch item's refused replacement never joined its predecessor's
 lineage: it is its own, at generation 1.
lineage.title: lineage

marketClientRefPriceTicks.description:
Client reference price the MARKET order set for its slippage protection,
 in quote units scaled by 1e9, exactly as given: it need not be on the
 pair's tick grid (see MarketIoc). Zero when the order set none.
marketClientRefPriceTicks.title: market_client_ref_price_ticks

marketMaxSlippageBps.description: Optional MARKET max slippage in basis points (1 bp = 0.01%).
marketMaxSlippageBps.title: market_max_slippage_bps

marketMaxSlippageTicks.description:
MARKET maximum absolute price delta the order carries, in quote units
 scaled by 1e9 (1e-9 quote units, not the pair's tick size), exactly as
 given: it need not be a multiple of the pair's tick size (see MarketIoc).
 Positive when the order set this cap; zero when it did not, for example
 because it set market_max_slippage_bps instead.
marketMaxSlippageTicks.title: market_max_slippage_ticks

orderType.description:
Order type.
 Unset for the replacement order of a batch item refused when it applied
 (REJECTED with batch_request_id set), which never existed and carries no
 order terms: the client knows them from the batch it sent.
orderType.title: order_type

origQtyScaled.description:
Current accepted total order quantity, updated by successful modifies,
 scaled by the pair's base_quantity_scale from GetSpotConfig for symbol_id.
 0 as a placeholder for the replacement order of a batch item refused when
 it applied, which carries no order terms: the client knows them from the
 batch it sent.
origQtyScaled.title: orig_qty_scaled

origin.description: Runtime lineage metadata (why the order exists and what generated it).
origin.title: origin

postOnly.description: True if the order was submitted as post-only (maker-only).
postOnly.title: post_only

priceTicks.description:
Price in quote units scaled by 1e9. For a LIMIT order, its limit price.
 For a MARKET order, whatever placed it, its protection price: the worst
 price it may fill at, a BUY at or below it and a SELL at or above it. It
 is the order's reference price moved by its maximum slippage, or by the
 pair's default market slippage for its side (200 basis points if none is
 configured), put on the pair's tick grid toward the reference: a BUY's
 rounded down and a SELL's up, so it never allows more than the slippage.
 The reference and the slippage need not be on the tick grid themselves
 (see MarketIoc). A stop-loss's, take-profit's or
 trailing stop's market order takes the price that fired it as its
 reference; a buy stop's is never above the protection price at its
 trigger price. 0 as a placeholder for the replacement order of a batch
 item refused when it applied, which carries no order terms.
priceTicks.title: price_ticks

rejectReason.description:
For a REJECTED order, why it was refused: the same error code the Orders
 API returns for the same refusal. Not set for every other status; JSON and
 REST responses then omit it.
rejectReason.title: reject_reason

selfTradePreventionMode.description:
Self-trade prevention mode.
 Unset for the replacement order of a batch item refused when it applied
 (REJECTED with batch_request_id set), which never existed and carries no
 order terms: the client knows them from the batch it sent.
selfTradePreventionMode.title: self_trade_prevention_mode

side.description:
Order side.
 Unset for the replacement order of a batch item refused when it applied
 (REJECTED with batch_request_id set), which never existed and carries no
 order terms: the client knows them from the batch it sent.
side.title: side

submittedMaxQuoteDebitScaled.description:
Submitted hard all-in quote debit limit, scaled by the pair's
 quote_quantity_scale from GetSpotConfig. Present only when that sizing
 method was submitted.
submittedMaxQuoteDebitScaled.title: submitted_max_quote_debit_scaled

submittedQuoteProceedsScaled.description:
Submitted quote proceeds target, scaled by the pair's
 quote_quantity_scale from GetSpotConfig. Present only when that sizing
 method was submitted.
submittedQuoteProceedsScaled.title: submitted_quote_proceeds_scaled

symbolId.description:
Trading symbol numeric identifier.
 Unset for the replacement order of a batch item refused when it applied
 (REJECTED with batch_request_id set), which never existed and carries no
 order terms: the client knows them from the batch it sent.
symbolId.title: symbol_id

terminalTsNs.description: Terminal timestamp in nanoseconds since epoch (UTC). Zero for open orders.
terminalTsNs.title: terminal_ts_ns

timeInForce.description:
Time-in-force policy.
 Unset for the replacement order of a batch item refused when it applied
 (REJECTED with batch_request_id set), which never existed and carries no
 order terms: the client knows them from the batch it sent.
timeInForce.title: time_in_force

version.description:
Per-order state version: the same counter as the version of the order's
 events on the private WebSocket and the trade WebSocket. It is 0 while the
 order is accepted but not yet on the book (status PENDING), then 1 from its
 first book state, and it increases with every later published change of the
 order's state, such as an amend in place, a fill, a change of its attached
 risk, a cancel or a replace. It is an unsigned 32-bit counter that
 increases on every change of the order: it would wrap to 0 only after
 4,294,967,295 changes to one order ID. A replace that gives the order a new
 ID starts that order's own version.

 A read can lag behind the order's events. Keep the highest version
 applied for each order ID, from reads and events alike, and drop any read
 whose version is below it: that read shows an older state. A stream need
 not show every version, so a gap is not an error; read the order to
 recover its current state.

 fee_total is not covered by this version: a fill's fee is recorded after
 the fill, so responses with the same version can show different fee
 totals. A read includes attached_risk only on request, so its absence
 from a response is no change of the order.
version.title: version

orders.v1.Order.title: Order

orders.v1.OrderFeeTotal.description:
OrderFeeTotal is the total fee of an order's fills, net of rebates, as
 settled. A fill's fee is recorded shortly after the fill executes, so the
 total can trail the fills the order shows: qty_scaled says which fills it
 covers.

amountE18.description:
Net fee magnitude in fixed 18-decimal units of the order's fee_asset:
 the fees of the covered fills less their rebates. Zero when they charged
 no fee.
amountE18.title: amount_e18

isRebate.description:
True when the covered fills' rebates exceed their fees, so the amount
 was credited to the account rather than charged.
isRebate.title: is_rebate

qtyScaled.description:
Executed quantity of the fills the total covers, scaled by the pair's
 base_quantity_scale from GetSpotConfig. Equal to the order's
 cum_qty_scaled once every fill's fee is recorded. While a fill is still
 being recorded the two differ, and a later read of the order includes
 it.
qtyScaled.title: qty_scaled

orders.v1.OrderFeeTotal.title: OrderFeeTotal

orders.v1.OrderIntent.description:
OrderIntent contains one order's complete, transport-independent placement
 intent. Single and batch create use this same message.
max_quote_debit_scaled is valid only for BUY market IOC or BUY limit IOC orders
quote_proceeds_scaled is valid only for SELL market IOC or SELL limit IOC orders
SELL orders must use the QUOTE fee asset

attachedRisk.description: Optional attached risk controls that arm after the parent order fills.
attachedRisk.title: attached_risk

baseQtyScaled.description:
Exact positive gross base quantity scaled by the pair's
 base_quantity_scale from GetSpotConfig.
baseQtyScaled.title: base_qty_scaled

clientOrderId.description:
Optional account-scoped identifier for correlation, lookup, and cancellation.
 While this identifier is retained, reuse returns
 CONFLICT_DUPLICATE_CLIENT_ORDER_ID for every new submission, even with the
 same payload. This identifier enables GetOrder reconciliation after a
 timeout; it does not provide exact replay. At most 36 ASCII characters
 using letters, digits, period, underscore, colon, slash, or hyphen.
clientOrderId.title: client_order_id

feeAsset.description:
Asset charged for fees. Defaults to QUOTE. BASE is available only for BUY
 orders on a pair whose allow_buy_fee_from_base is true in GetSpotConfig;
 SELL orders must use QUOTE. Otherwise the order is refused with
 ERROR_CODE_FEE_ASSET_NOT_ALLOWED.
feeAsset.title: fee_asset

limitGtc.description: Resting GTC limit order, optionally post-only.
limitGtc.title: limit_gtc

limitGtd.description: Limit order with an exact expiry time.
limitGtd.title: limit_gtd

marketIoc.description: Market order with implicit IOC behavior.
marketIoc.title: market_ioc

maxQuoteDebitScaled.description:
Hard all-in quote debit limit scaled by the pair's quote_quantity_scale
 from GetSpotConfig. Valid only for BUY market IOC and BUY limit IOC.
 The order spends up to this amount at the prices it fills at. Once what
 is left buys no further quantity step, it ends FILLED; if the book or
 its price limit stops it first, its remainder is canceled. It can carry
 attached_risk: the legs protect the quantity it actually buys. Must be
 positive.
maxQuoteDebitScaled.title: max_quote_debit_scaled

peg.description:
Optional static peg. The selected limit execution still requires its price
 bound. Quote sizing, market execution and attached risk are invalid.
peg.title: peg

quoteProceedsScaled.description:
Quote proceeds target scaled by the pair's quote_quantity_scale from
 GetSpotConfig. Valid only for SELL market IOC and SELL limit IOC. The
 order sells whole quantity steps until its proceeds, the sum of each
 fill's price times quantity before fees, reach this amount, and never
 receives more. The fee is charged in quote on those proceeds. The order
 holds the base this amount sells at its limit price, or a market
 order's maximum slippage price, and is rejected INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS when
 that base is not available. Once what is left sells no further quantity
 step, it ends FILLED; if the book or its price limit stops it first,
 its remainder is canceled. It cannot carry attached_risk. Must be
 positive.
quoteProceedsScaled.title: quote_proceeds_scaled

selfTradePreventionMode.description:
Self-trade prevention mode against orders of the same root account,
 including all its subaccounts. Defaults to EXPIRE_MAKER if unspecified.
selfTradePreventionMode.title: self_trade_prevention_mode

symbolId.description: Stable numeric pair ID from GetSpotConfig.
symbolId.title: symbol_id

orders.v1.OrderIntent.title: OrderIntent

orders.v1.OrderLineage.description: OrderLineage identifies a logical order and one of its accepted generations.

generation.description: One-based replacement generation, distinct from per-order state version.
generation.title: generation

id.description:
Stable logical-order ID: the first generation's public order ID.
 Replace preserves this ID; an independent new order starts a new lineage.
id.title: id

orders.v1.OrderLineage.title: OrderLineage

orders.v1.OrderOrigin.description:
OrderOrigin explains why an order exists and where it came from.

 Population rules:
 - direct/manual orders: scope=DIRECT; trigger fields unset/unspecified.
 - attached children: scope=ATTACHED_RISK; parent_order_id is set.
 - standalone trigger children: scope=STANDALONE_TRIGGER.
 - child_seq is set for multi-child strategies (for example TWAP/LADDER).

childSeq.description: Child sequence number for multi-child trigger strategies. Zero when not applicable.
childSeq.title: child_seq

parentOrderId.description: Parent order ID for attached-risk child orders.
parentOrderId.title: parent_order_id

scope.description: Broad class describing how the order was created.
scope.title: scope

triggerId.description: Trigger identifier when the order was created by a trigger.
triggerId.title: trigger_id

triggerType.description:
Trigger strategy that created this order. Not set for direct orders; JSON
 and REST responses then omit it.
triggerType.title: trigger_type

orders.v1.OrderOrigin.title: OrderOrigin

orders.v1.OrderOriginScope.description: OrderOriginScope captures broad origin classes for an order.
orders.v1.OrderOriginScope.title: OrderOriginScope

orders.v1.OrderStatus.description:
OrderStatus describes the order's execution lifecycle state on read surfaces.
 CreateOrder acknowledges admission without returning execution status.
orders.v1.OrderStatus.title: OrderStatus

orders.v1.OrderTransfer.description: OrderTransfer is the Connect-facing minimal per-leg transfer view.

accountCode.description: Account bucket affected by this transfer leg.
accountCode.title: account_code

amountE18.description: Transfer amount at fixed 18-decimal ledger scale.
amountE18.title: amount_e18

assetId.description: Asset identifier for the transferred asset.
assetId.title: asset_id

isDebit.description: True when the transfer debits the account; false when it credits the account.
isDebit.title: is_debit

matchId.description: Match identifier that linked this transfer to an execution, scoped by symbol_id.
matchId.title: match_id

symbolId.description: Market of the execution; together with match_id identifies its match.
symbolId.title: symbol_id

transferCode.description: Product reason for this transfer leg.
transferCode.title: transfer_code

tsNs.description: Transfer timestamp in nanoseconds since epoch (UTC).
tsNs.title: ts_ns

orders.v1.OrderTransfer.title: OrderTransfer

orders.v1.OrderTriggerType.description: OrderTriggerType captures the trigger strategy that generated the order.
orders.v1.OrderTriggerType.title: OrderTriggerType

orders.v1.OrderType.description: OrderType identifies whether an order uses limit-price or market execution.
orders.v1.OrderType.title: OrderType

orders.v1.PegReference.description: The displayed book side used for a static entry peg.
orders.v1.PegReference.title: PegReference

orders.v1.PreviewOrderRequest.description:
PreviewOrderRequest asks whether one complete order intent is currently
 admissible. It uses the same order contract as CreateOrderRequest. Previewing
 creates no order, hold, reservation, or client-order-ID claim.

order.description: Order intent to evaluate without submitting it. Required.
order.title: order

subaccountId.description:
Optional public subaccount ID. When omitted, subaccount-scoped API keys
 use their bound subaccount; other callers use their authenticated root
 account.
subaccountId.title: subaccount_id

orders.v1.PreviewOrderRequest.title: PreviewOrderRequest

orders.v1.PreviewOrderResponse.description:
PreviewOrderResponse reports whether an order is currently admissible and
 returns any sizing and price-protection values resolved during evaluation.
 Quote debit and fees are not returned.
 The result is advisory: account, market, and policy inputs may change, and
 CreateOrder always evaluates the intent again.

admissible.description:
Whether the order passed the current validation, policy, risk, and
 available-balance checks.
admissible.title: admissible

evaluatedAt.description: Time at which this admission evaluation completed.
evaluatedAt.title: evaluated_at

protectedPriceBoundTicks.description:
Protective execution boundary. REST returns protectedPriceBound as a decimal
 string in quote asset units per base asset unit, for example "2751.6".
 Protobuf uses quote units scaled by 1e9. This is not an expected fill price.
 Present when price protection was resolved.
protectedPriceBoundTicks.title: protected_price_bound_ticks

rejection.description:
Typed reason the order is not currently admissible. Omitted when
 admissible is true.
rejection.title: rejection

resolvedBaseQtyScaled.description:
Gross base quantity admission resolved. REST returns resolvedBaseQty as a
 decimal string in base asset units, for example "0.005". Protobuf uses the
 pair's base_quantity_scale from GetSpotConfig. Present when sizing was
 resolved. For base_qty_scaled sizing, the order's quantity. For quote sizing
 (max_quote_debit_scaled BUY or quote_proceeds_scaled SELL), the quantity the
 quote amount buys or sells at the order's limit price, or at the market
 protection price at preview time (protected_price_bound_ticks). CreateOrder
 resolves the protection price and the order's quantity again at submission,
 so the submitted order can buy or sell more or less than this. The executed
 quantity is the order's cumulative filled quantity (cum_qty_scaled in
 GetOrder) or the sum of its fills (GetUserTrades, or the fills of its
 private order events).
resolvedBaseQtyScaled.title: resolved_base_qty_scaled

orders.v1.PreviewOrderResponse.title: PreviewOrderResponse

orders.v1.RiskExecution.description:
RiskExecution selects the child execution supported by attached take-profit
 and stop-loss policies.

marketIoc.description: Market child with implicit IOC behavior.
marketIoc.title: market_ioc

orders.v1.RiskExecution.title: RiskExecution

orders.v1.RiskLimitGtc.description:
RiskLimitGtc configures an attached risk leg that submits a resting limit
 child. Attached risk legs do not support post-only.

priceTicks.description: Positive limit price in quote units scaled by 1e9.
priceTicks.title: price_ticks

orders.v1.RiskLimitGtc.title: RiskLimitGtc

orders.v1.RiskMarketIoc.description:
RiskMarketIoc configures an attached risk leg that submits a market child
 with implicit immediate-or-cancel behavior. It takes no max-slippage cap:
 the child always uses the pair's default market slippage for its side, or
 200 basis points if no positive default is configured. A cap cannot be
 added later either: ModifyTrigger with max_slippage on a take-profit or
 stop-loss leg that uses it is rejected with
 ERROR_CODE_TRIGGER_NOT_MODIFIABLE and leaves the leg unchanged, while its
 trigger price remains modifiable.
orders.v1.RiskMarketIoc.title: RiskMarketIoc

orders.v1.RiskPolicy.description:
RiskPolicy defines optional risk controls (take-profit, stop-loss or
 trailing stop) attached to an order. The legs protect the parent order's
 filled position: they arm as the parent fills and follow its later fills.
 A buy sized by max_quote_debit_scaled has no fixed quantity: its legs
 protect what its fills buy. When the order is created, each leg's exit is
 checked against the pair's minimums at the quantity the whole amount buys
 at the order's limit price, or a market order's maximum slippage price:
 the least it buys if it spends the amount.

 Each leg's exit must be able to meet the pair's minimum quantity, step size
 and minimum notional for the parent's whole quantity, valued where it would
 execute: a buy-back at its maximum price (a market exit's slippage bound
 above its trigger price, a limit exit's limit price, a trailing stop's limit
 price), a market sell exit at its slippage bound below its trigger price, a
 limit sell exit at its limit price, and a trailing sell exit by its quantity
 alone. An order, or a ModifyOrder, whose leg could never meet them is
 rejected with that check's code (ERROR_CODE_MIN_QTY,
 ERROR_CODE_QTY_STEP_SIZE or ERROR_CODE_MIN_NOTIONAL), as for the order
 itself, and its ErrorDetail names the leg with a field violation on its
 attached-risk field (take_profit, stop_loss or trailing_stop) whose rule is
 that code. Nothing is placed or changed.

 A buy's take-profit trigger price must be above its parent's price and its
 stop-loss trigger price below it, so the take-profit is above the stop-loss;
 a sell's the other way round. The parent's price is a limit order's limit
 price, or for a market order the best price it takes (the best ask for a
 buy, the best bid for a sell), against which only a leg on the last price
 is checked. A leg at or past that price is rejected with
 ERROR_CODE_TRIGGER_PRICE_INVALID for a limit order and
 ERROR_CODE_TRIGGER_WOULD_TRIGGER_IMMEDIATELY for a market order, and its
 ErrorDetail names the leg with a field violation on its trigger price (for
 example order.attached_risk.take_profit.trigger_price_ticks) whose rule is
 that code and whose message states the order the prices must take for the
 order's side. When both legs are past it, the take-profit is named. A
 ModifyOrder's new_attached_risk is checked against the order's price the
 same way; its message states the order for both sides. Nothing is placed
 or changed.

 The legs of one parent share that position, whether or not oco is set, and
 only one exit works at a time. The first leg whose condition is met submits
 an exit for the whole remaining position, rounded down to the pair's step
 size; a remainder below one step stays in the balance. If another leg's
 condition is met while that exit works, the working exit is canceled; once
 it ends, that leg is checked again against the latest price it watches and,
 if its condition still holds, exits what remains. After an exit ends, the legs keep
 protecting whatever position remains, unless you canceled the exit: canceling
 a leg's exit order, alone or with a cancel-all, ends that leg, and with oco
 set the other leg too. Canceling a leg itself with CancelTrigger ends only
 that leg, whether or not oco is set, and the other leg stays active.

 The legs end once the parent order is terminal and no position they can
 exit remains: the leg whose exit ended last completes, and the others are
 canceled with TRIGGER_CANCEL_REASON_OCO. If the parent order ends without a
 fill, the legs are canceled with
 TRIGGER_CANCEL_REASON_PARENT_CANCELED_NO_FILL. If no exit ran and the
 parent's whole fill is below one step, the legs fail.

 The legs reserve what their exits would sell or spend, once for both legs:
 the base a sell exit sells, as each parent fill settles, and the quote a
 buy-back may spend at its legs' highest maximum price. A buy-back is
 reserved from the order's creation for the part of that cost the sale
 itself may not return, so an order whose balance cannot cover it is
 rejected with ERROR_CODE_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS. The reserve shows in the
 balance's reserved amount, and an exit uses it when it is submitted. While
 the legs protect a position, orders and withdrawals that would use the
 reserved funds are rejected with ERROR_CODE_INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS: reduce or
 cancel the legs first. What the legs no longer need is released as they
 change and in full when they end.
oco requires take_profit and exactly one stop leg (stop_loss or trailing_stop)

oco.description:
If true, the take-profit and the configured stop leg (stop-loss or
 trailing stop) are linked and shown as one-cancels-the-other. Requires a
 take-profit and exactly one stop leg. The legs of every parent share one
 position and end together as described on RiskPolicy, so this setting
 does not change when exits are submitted. It decides only what canceling
 a leg's exit order ends: with oco set, canceling one leg's exit ends both
 legs; without it, only that leg ends and the other keeps protecting the
 remaining position. Canceling a leg itself with CancelTrigger ends only
 that leg either way, and the other leg stays active. Changing only this
 setting with ModifyOrder keeps the existing legs, with their IDs, arming
 and a trailing stop's tracked peak; changing a leg's terms, such as its
 trigger price, limit price or trailing distance, still replaces that leg.
 Default is false.
oco.title: oco

orders.v1.RiskPolicy.title: RiskPolicy

orders.v1.SelfTradePreventionMode.description:
SelfTradePreventionMode controls what happens when an order would trade
 against another order of the same root account, including all its
 subaccounts: two subaccounts of one root never trade with each other. The
 incoming order's mode decides which orders expire or are reduced.
orders.v1.SelfTradePreventionMode.title: SelfTradePreventionMode

orders.v1.Side.description: Side identifies whether an order buys or sells the base asset.
orders.v1.Side.title: Side

orders.v1.StaticPeg.description:
Derives a limit price once at entry. Available only with base quantity and
 limit execution, without attached risk. The limit execution's price_ticks is
 required: a BUY maximum price or SELL minimum price. A derived price beyond
 that bound is rejected. The order never follows later book changes.

offsetTicks.description:
Signed number of configured price increments added to the reference.
 One increment is the pair’s configured price increment in quote units; this count
 is not Q9 and does not select occupied price levels. Defaults to zero.
offsetTicks.title: offset_ticks

reference.description: Required public book side. An empty selected side rejects the order.
reference.title: reference

orders.v1.StaticPeg.title: StaticPeg

orders.v1.StopLossPolicy.description:
StopLossPolicy defines a stop-loss attached to an order. It watches the last
 traded price or the index price (trigger_price_source), arms after the
 parent fills, and submits the selected child.

child.description: Required child execution when the threshold is crossed.
child.title: child

triggerPriceSource.description:
Price the stop-loss watches. Unspecified or LAST_PRICE watches the last
 traded price. INDEX_PRICE watches the market's index price; on a market
 without an index price the order is rejected before any fill with
 reject_reason ERROR_CODE_TRIGGER_PRICE_SOURCE_UNSUPPORTED, and a modify
 that adds such a leg is refused with the same code, leaving the order and
 its legs unchanged. MARK_PRICE is not supported. A modify naming
 another source replaces the leg.
triggerPriceSource.title: trigger_price_source

triggerPriceTicks.description: Positive trigger price in quote units scaled by 1e9.
triggerPriceTicks.title: trigger_price_ticks

orders.v1.StopLossPolicy.title: StopLossPolicy

orders.v1.TakeProfitPolicy.description:
TakeProfitPolicy defines a take-profit attached to an order. It watches the
 last traded price or the index price (trigger_price_source), arms after the
 parent fills, and submits the selected child.

child.description: Required child execution when the threshold is crossed.
child.title: child

triggerPriceSource.description:
Price the take-profit watches. Unspecified or LAST_PRICE watches the last
 traded price. INDEX_PRICE watches the market's index price; on a market
 without an index price the order is rejected before any fill with
 reject_reason ERROR_CODE_TRIGGER_PRICE_SOURCE_UNSUPPORTED, and a modify
 that adds such a leg is refused with the same code, leaving the order and
 its legs unchanged. MARK_PRICE is not supported. A modify naming
 another source replaces the leg.
triggerPriceSource.title: trigger_price_source

triggerPriceTicks.description: Positive trigger price in quote units scaled by 1e9.
triggerPriceTicks.title: trigger_price_ticks

orders.v1.TakeProfitPolicy.title: TakeProfitPolicy

orders.v1.TimeInForce.description:
TimeInForce controls how long an order may remain active and whether it must
 fill completely.
orders.v1.TimeInForce.title: TimeInForce

orders.v1.TrailingStopPolicy.description:
TrailingStopPolicy defines a trailing stop attached to an order.
 Tracks peak (for sell) or trough (for buy) and fires when price reverses by
 the distance.

activationPriceTicks.description:
Optional activation price: trailing only starts after this price is
 reached. If omitted, trailing starts immediately after the parent order
 fills. Expressed in quote units scaled by 1e9.
activationPriceTicks.title: activation_price_ticks

limitPriceTicks.description:
Positive maximum price of a trailing stop that buys back, in quote units
 scaled by 1e9: the most its exit pays per unit, at which the quote it may
 spend is reserved with the exit's fee. Required when the parent order
 sells, so the trailing stop buys; must be unset when the parent order
 buys. A rise that fires above it still fires, and the exit fills only at
 or below it. Changing it with ModifyOrder replaces the leg.
limitPriceTicks.title: limit_price_ticks

maxSlippageBps.description:
Maximum allowed slippage in basis points (1 bp = 0.01%), from 1 to 9999
 whichever side the exit trades. An order whose trailing stop sets 10000
 is rejected with ERROR_CODE_MAX_SLIPPAGE_INVALID, because a 100% cap
 would leave an exit that sells no positive price to sell at.
maxSlippageBps.title: max_slippage_bps

maxSlippageTicks.description:
Positive maximum absolute price delta in quote units scaled by 1e9. The
 "ticks" in this name are 1e-9 quote units, not the pair's tick size,
 and the value need not be a multiple of the pair's tick size: the
 child's protection price, the price that fired it moved by this delta,
 is put on the tick grid toward that price, as MarketIoc describes.
maxSlippageTicks.title: max_slippage_ticks

trailingDistanceBps.description: Trailing distance in basis points (1 bp = 0.01%), from 1 to 10000.
trailingDistanceBps.title: trailing_distance_bps

trailingDistanceTicks.description: Positive trailing distance as a price delta in 1e-9 quote-unit ticks.
trailingDistanceTicks.title: trailing_distance_ticks

triggerPriceSource.description:
Price the trailing stop watches and trails: its peak or trough, activation
 and fire all follow this price. Unspecified or LAST_PRICE watches the last
 traded price. INDEX_PRICE watches the market's index price; on a market
 without an index price the order is rejected before any fill with

 prices are final; every closed day for LIFETIME; none for TODAY. The daily returns are compounded, so

maxDrawdownEnd.title: max_drawdown_end

maxDrawdownPercent.description: Largest fall from a peak, in percent.
maxDrawdownPercent.title: max_drawdown_percent

maxDrawdownStart.description: When the largest fall started: its peak.
maxDrawdownStart.title: max_drawdown_start

realizedPnl.description:
Profit and loss realized by the period's sells, in the quote asset, after
 their fees. Signed base-10 decimal string, for example "12.5" or
 "-3.25".
realizedPnl.title: realized_pnl

returnPercent.description: Return over the period, in percent, for example "4.2" or "-1.5".
returnPercent.title: return_percent

sharpeRatio.description:
Annualized Sharpe ratio of the daily returns, with a zero risk-free rate,
 for example "1.4". Unset when undefined: with fewer than two daily
 returns, or when they never vary.
sharpeRatio.title: sharpe_ratio

startEquity.description:
Equity at the period's start, exactly, as an exact decimal in the quote
 asset: the equity curve is sampled, so read the bounds here. For the
 tuning period (or the whole window without a split) it is the initial
 balances, any base asset valued at the reference open of the window's
 first bar. For the held-back period it is the equity at the split, the
 open position marked at the last close before it.
startEquity.title: start_equity

winRatePercent.description: Share of closed trades that made a profit, in percent.
winRatePercent.title: win_rate_percent

strategies.v1.BacktestMetrics.title: BacktestMetrics

strategies.v1.BacktestReport.description:
BacktestReport is the result of a finished backtest. Only bots that trade
 with market orders, including exits on watched price levels, are
 backtested. Every amount is in the bot's markets' one quote asset. The
 results below are for the base cost scenario; scenarios gives the range.

baselines.description: The baselines over period: buy-and-hold and cash.
baselines.title: baselines

dataGaps.description: Spans without market data, oldest first.
dataGaps.title: data_gaps

equity.description:
The equity curve over the whole window, with buy-and-hold's, at most
 1,000 points, oldest first. It is sampled, but always holds the peaks and
 troughs of every largest fall reported.
equity.title: equity

evidenceGrade.description: How much the result can be trusted.
evidenceGrade.title: evidence_grade

fidelity.description:
What was simulated and how, as a short label naming every assumption:
 the candles, the reference prices, the spread and slippage, when orders
 fill, the fees and the starting balance.
fidelity.title: fidelity

heldBackBaselines.description: The baselines over held_back_period. Empty without one.
heldBackBaselines.title: held_back_baselines

heldBackMetrics.description: Results over held_back_period. Unset without one.
heldBackMetrics.title: held_back_metrics

heldBackPeriod.description:
The most recent months, held back from tuning. Unset when the window is
 too short to hold months back.
heldBackPeriod.title: held_back_period

heldBackSeen.description:
True when the caller's earlier backtests already showed part of
 held_back_period, so it is no longer excluded from tuning.
heldBackSeen.title: held_back_seen

heldBackStart.description: Where held_back_period starts on the curve. Unset without one.
heldBackStart.title: held_back_start

period.description:
The period the bot was tuned on. With a window too short to hold months
 back, it is the whole window.
period.title: period

scenarios.description:
The result under each cost scenario, low, base and high: the range to
 read, never one exact number.
scenarios.title: scenarios

trades.description:
The first trades of the whole window, oldest first: at most 20.
 ListBacktestTrades lists all of them.
trades.title: trades

warnings.description: What to keep in mind when reading the result.
warnings.title: warnings

windowMaxDrawdownEnd.description: When the whole window's largest fall ended: its trough.
windowMaxDrawdownEnd.title: window_max_drawdown_end

windowMaxDrawdownPercent.description: The largest fall over the whole window, in percent.
windowMaxDrawdownPercent.title: window_max_drawdown_percent

windowMaxDrawdownStart.description: When the whole window's largest fall started: its peak.
windowMaxDrawdownStart.title: window_max_drawdown_start

strategies.v1.BacktestReport.title: BacktestReport

strategies.v1.BacktestScenario.description: BacktestScenario is a backtest's result under one cost scenario.

heldBackMetrics.description: Results over the report's held-back period. Unset without one.
heldBackMetrics.title: held_back_metrics

name.description: The scenario: low, base or high.
name.title: name

slippageBps.description: Slippage per side, in basis points.
slippageBps.title: slippage_bps

strategies.v1.BacktestScenario.title: BacktestScenario

strategies.v1.BacktestSummary.description: BacktestSummary is the headline of a version's latest backtest.

attempts.description: Backtests run so far for this bot's family of versions.
attempts.title: attempts

heldBackMetrics.description: Results over the held-back period. Set only when status is DONE.
heldBackMetrics.title: held_back_metrics

metrics.description: Results over the tuning period. Set only when status is DONE.
metrics.title: metrics

strategies.v1.BacktestSummary.title: BacktestSummary

strategies.v1.BacktestTrade.description: BacktestTrade is one trade a backtest made.

afterGap.description:
True when the market data the order would have filled on was missing,
 so it filled at the first price after the gap.
afterGap.title: after_gap

price.description: Price, as an exact decimal in the quote asset.
price.title: price

quantity.description: Quantity, as an exact decimal in the base asset.
quantity.title: quantity

realizedPnl.description:
Profit and loss this trade realized, in the quote asset, after its fee.
 Signed base-10 decimal string, for example "4.1" or "-0.75". Empty on a
 buy, which only opens or adds to a position.
realizedPnl.title: realized_pnl

reason.description: The reason the bot gave for the order.
reason.title: reason

time.description: When the trade happened, in simulated time.
time.title: time

tradeIndex.description:
The trade's position among the backtest's trades, numbered from 0 in
 the order they filled. ListBacktestTrades pages in this order.
tradeIndex.title: trade_index

strategies.v1.BacktestTrade.title: BacktestTrade

strategies.v1.Baseline.description: Baseline is a simple strategy a backtest is compared with.

metrics.description: Its results over the same period.
metrics.title: metrics

strategies.v1.Baseline.title: Baseline

strategies.v1.Bot.description: Bot is one bot of the caller.

activity.description:
What the bot did in each of the last 24 hours, oldest first, ending with
 the current UTC hour, which is still under way. An hour it did nothing
 in is there with zero counts. A bot deployed again within the day counts
 every one of its runs. Counts lag the bot by up to about a minute.
activity.title: activity

funding.description:
Where the bot's initial funding came from, and how much. Absent until
 the deploy flow records the deploy proposal the bot came from.
funding.title: funding

lastDecisionAt.description:
When the bot last decided: the time of the event behind its newest
 decision, over all its deployments. Omitted before its first decision.
 Lags the bot by up to about a minute.
lastDecisionAt.title: last_decision_at

markets.description:
Markets the bot trades, as its version's money card names them, for
 example BTC-USDT.
markets.title: markets

name.description: The bot's name, as approved when the bot was deployed.
name.title: name

pauseReason.description:
Why the bot paused. Set only with PAUSED, which is read only once the
 bot's pause has been reported to the service.
pauseReason.title: pause_reason

quoteAsset.description: Quote asset of the bot's markets, for example USDT.
quoteAsset.title: quote_asset

runningSince.description: When the bot last started running. Set only while it is RUNNING.
runningSince.title: running_since

statusReason.description:
Why the bot paused, in words: the bot's own message when it decided
 to pause, else a sentence for pause_reason. Set only with PAUSED.
statusReason.title: status_reason

subaccountId.description:
Public ID of the bot's own subaccount, which the caller's main account
 owns.
subaccountId.title: subaccount_id

uptimeRatio.description:
Share of the time since the bot was first deployed during which it was
 running, as an exact decimal from 0 to 1 rounded to 6 decimal places,
 for example "0.9875". A bot runs from each start to the stop the user
 recorded; time it spent paused counts as running. Empty before the bot
 first starts.
uptimeRatio.title: uptime_ratio

strategies.v1.Bot.title: Bot

strategies.v1.Bot.PauseReason.description: PauseReason is why a PAUSED bot paused, beside the status_reason text.
strategies.v1.Bot.PauseReason.title: PauseReason

strategies.v1.BotActivityHour.description:
BotActivityHour is what a bot did in one UTC hour, by when each event
 reached it.

decisions.description:
Its decisions: events the bot was called for, whether the call
 succeeded, failed, or ended before the bot's code ran.
decisions.title: decisions

expired.description:
Events it skipped because they were already too old when it could run,
 for example while it was behind: never decisions.
expired.title: expired

fills.description: Its fills, whether or not its code handles them.
fills.title: fills

start.description: The hour's start: a whole UTC hour.
start.title: start

strategies.v1.BotActivityHour.title: BotActivityHour

strategies.v1.BotDecision.description: BotDecision is one handler call of a bot.

decidedAt.description: When the event that woke the bot reached it.
decidedAt.title: decided_at

event.description: The handler the event woke, for example on_timer or on_fill.
event.title: event

logs.description:
The bot's log lines from the call, oldest first: at most 20, each at
 most 256 bytes of UTF-8 and 1 KiB in all. A shortened line ends with
 "…", and a last line of "…" stands for the lines left out.
logs.title: logs

orders.description:
The orders the bot asked for, in the shape the manifest's behaviour
 examples use, with what a live call adds; a key is left out when unset.
 An order: {"buy" or "sell": market, "qty" or "quote", "limit", "tif",
 "post_only", "max_slippage_bps", "stop_loss", "take_profit", "reason",
 "client_order_id"}. A trigger (bot.buy_when, bot.sell_when): {"buy" or
 "sell": market, "above" or "below": its price, "qty", "limit", "tif",
 "price_source", "reason", "client_trigger_id"}. A cancel: {"cancel": the
 order's or trigger's client ID, or the trigger's ID}. An order refused
 before it was sent: {"refused": market, "client_order_id", "reason"}.
 Amounts and prices are decimal strings. An order on a market the
 service doesn't know names it "market #<id>", shows its amounts and
 prices as unscaled integers, and carries "unscaled": true. Empty when
 it decided to do nothing.
orders.title: orders

strategies.v1.BotDecision.title: BotDecision

strategies.v1.BotError.description: BotError is one failed handler call of a bot.

event.description: The handler the event woke, for example on_timer or on_fill.
event.title: event

message.description:
What failed, at most 512 bytes of UTF-8, ending with "…" when
 shortened: the bot's own error when its code raised, the rule its result
 broke, or a sentence saying the call ran out of its time or memory or
 could not finish.
message.title: message

time.description: When the event whose call failed reached the bot.
time.title: time

strategies.v1.BotError.title: BotError

strategies.v1.BotFunding.description:
BotFunding is where a bot's initial funding came from, as its deploy
 proposal recorded it.

initialFunding.description:
What moved into the bot's subaccount when it was deployed, one entry
 per asset.
initialFunding.title: initial_funding

subaccountId.description:
Public ID of the subaccount the funding came from. Zero means the main
 account.
subaccountId.title: subaccount_id

subaccountLabel.description:
Current label of that subaccount, as its owner named it. Empty for the
 main account or a subaccount without a label.
subaccountLabel.title: subaccount_label

strategies.v1.BotFunding.title: BotFunding

strategies.v1.BotLogEntry.description:
BotLogEntry is one entry of a bot's recent activity: a decision, a line its
 call wrote, or a failed call.

sequence.description:
Position in the log of the bot's current deployment, increasing within
 that deployment. A new deployment starts a new log, whose positions start
 low again. A decision comes first, then the lines its call wrote, then
 its error if the call failed.
sequence.title: sequence

time.description:
When the event behind it was observed: a decision's lines and its error
 have the decision's time. Two decisions can have the same time, for
 example two markets' candles of one minute.
time.title: time

strategies.v1.BotLogEntry.title: BotLogEntry

strategies.v1.BotLogEntry.Kind.description: Kind is what a log entry records.
strategies.v1.BotLogEntry.Kind.title: Kind

strategies.v1.BotStatusCount.description: BotStatusCount is how many of the caller's bots are in one status.

count.description: How many of the caller's bots are in it.
count.title: count

strategies.v1.BotStatusCount.title: BotStatusCount

strategies.v1.BotVersion.description: BotVersion is one run of a bot on one version.

runtimeVersion.description: Runtime version the version was validated against.
runtimeVersion.title: runtime_version

startedAt.description: When the bot started running this version.
startedAt.title: started_at

stoppedAt.description:
When the stop of this run was recorded. Omitted while the run has no
 stop.
stoppedAt.title: stopped_at

versionId.description: The version the bot ran. GetStrategyVersion reads it.
versionId.title: version_id

strategies.v1.BotVersion.title: BotVersion

strategies.v1.CommunityBacktest.description:
CommunityBacktest is a community listing's platform backtest: the backtest
 the platform starts of the published version when it is published, over
 the default window (the most recent 365 days of data), with the default
 settings, 1,000 of the quote asset and the standard fee schedule. Its
 author chooses none of these, so every listing's results compare alike.
 It is pinned to the publish: publishing a later version starts a new one,
 and nothing runs it again on a schedule. It is the platform's own run: it
 shows nothing of the author's own backtests.

failure.description: Why it failed. Set only when status is FAILED.
failure.title: failure

metrics.description:
The results over the report's period, for the base cost scenario: the
 report's metrics. Set only when status is DONE.
metrics.title: metrics

notBacktestableReason.description:
Why the bot can't be backtested. Set only when status is
 NOT_BACKTESTABLE.
notBacktestableReason.title: not_backtestable_reason

report.description:
The whole result, as the platform's run made it. Set only by
 GetCommunityStrategy, when status is DONE.
report.title: report

status.description:
Where it is. NOT_BACKTESTABLE when the bot can't be backtested on
 candles, which not_backtestable_reason explains; the listing then shows
 no results. FAILED when it ended without results, which failure
 explains: a backtest whose runs couldn't finish is run once more by the
 platform before it fails.
status.title: status

window.description:
The simulated window. Unset when status is NOT_BACKTESTABLE and the
 backtest never started.
window.title: window

strategies.v1.CommunityBacktest.title: CommunityBacktest

strategies.v1.CommunityStrategy.description:
CommunityStrategy is one public community listing with its published
 version: everything a reader needs to judge it, and nothing of its
 author's account. The settings shown are the version's defaults, never
 the author's own values.

backtest.description: The platform backtest of the published version, with its report.
backtest.title: backtest

code.description: The published version's code.
code.title: code

description.description: The listing's description.
description.title: description

flow.description:
The published version's flow: what wakes the bot, what it checks and
 what it may do. Unset for a version stored before flows existed.
flow.title: flow

markets.description: The markets the published version trades, for example BTC-USDT.
markets.title: markets

publishedAt.description: When the shown version was published.
publishedAt.title: published_at

runtimeVersion.description: The runtime version it was checked against.
runtimeVersion.title: runtime_version

settingsForm.description: The settings a user may change, with their defaults.
settingsForm.title: settings_form

tags.description: The strategy's types.
tags.title: tags

strategies.v1.CommunityStrategy.title: CommunityStrategy

strategies.v1.CommunityStrategySummary.description:
CommunityStrategySummary is one public community listing, as lists show
 it.

backtest.description: The platform backtest of the published version, without its report.
backtest.title: backtest

listingId.description: Public listing ID. GetCommunityStrategy reads the listing.
listingId.title: listing_id

markets.description: The markets the published version trades, for example BTC-USDT.
markets.title: markets

publishedAt.description: When the shown version was published.
publishedAt.title: published_at

tags.description: The strategy's types.
tags.title: tags

strategies.v1.CommunityStrategySummary.title: CommunityStrategySummary

strategies.v1.CreateStrategyRequest.description: CreateStrategyRequest creates one strategy of the caller.

idempotencyKey.description:
Client-chosen key, unique per caller, that makes the call idempotent: the
 same key and request return the strategy the first call created, as it
 stands now, and never create a second one; another request with the same
 key, a SaveDraftVersion's included, is IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. Required.
idempotencyKey.title: idempotency_key

templateId.description:
A bot template, from ListStrategyTemplates: its manifest and code are
 checked and saved as revision 1.
templateId.title: template_id

versionId.description:
One of the caller's own versions, saved as revision 1 of the new
 strategy.
versionId.title: version_id

strategies.v1.CreateStrategyRequest.title: CreateStrategyRequest

strategy.description: The strategy, as it stands now.
strategy.title: strategy

version.description: The check result of revision 1's version. Unset for a blank strategy.
version.title: version

strategies.v1.DataGap.description: DataGap is a span with missing market data.

affected.description:
True when the bot was exposed across it: it held a position, watched a
 price level or had an order waiting on that market. What happened inside
 the gap is unknown, so the result is less certain.
affected.title: affected

strategies.v1.DataGap.title: DataGap

strategies.v1.DeleteStrategyRequest.description: DeleteStrategyRequest deletes one strategy of the caller.
strategies.v1.DeleteStrategyRequest.title: DeleteStrategyRequest

strategies.v1.DeleteStrategyResponse.title: DeleteStrategyResponse

strategies.v1.DeployBotRequest.description: DeployBotRequest deploys one deploy proposal of the caller.

subaccountAuthorization.description:
The user's signed authorization for the bot's new subaccount. Needed
 only when the deploy creates a subaccount: without it, such a deploy
 answers SUBACCOUNT_AUTHORIZATION_REQUIRED. A deploy that reuses one of
 the caller's closed bot subaccounts ignores it.
subaccountAuthorization.title: subaccount_authorization

strategies.v1.DeployBotRequest.title: DeployBotRequest

strategies.v1.DeployBotResponse.description: DeployBotResponse is the proposal's status when the call returns.

status.description:
The status: DEPLOYING once the bot's start is recorded (the bot then
 starts without the user), LIVE, or FAILED with failed_at and failure.
 SETTING_ACCESS means the exchange is still applying the bot's limits, and
 FUNDING without wait that the funding is still reaching the bot's
 subaccount: call again. FUNDING with wait: do what wait says, then call
 again.
status.title: status

strategies.v1.DeployBotResponse.title: DeployBotResponse

strategies.v1.DeployProposalSummary.description:
DeployProposalSummary is what a deploy proposal binds, for showing beside
 its link.

backtest.description:
The version's latest backtest. Omitted when the bot cannot be
 backtested; not_backtestable_reason then says why.
backtest.title: backtest

funding.description: What moves into the bot's new subaccount from the funding account.
funding.title: funding

fundingSubaccountId.description: The subaccount the funding comes from. Zero means the main account.
fundingSubaccountId.title: funding_subaccount_id

moneyCard.description: What the bot may do with money.
moneyCard.title: money_card

notBacktestableReason.description:
Why the bot was not backtested, when it cannot be: the deploy page tells
 the user before they approve. Unset when backtest is set.
notBacktestableReason.title: not_backtestable_reason

revision.description:
The strategy's revision proposed, whose version is version_id. Zero once
 the strategy is deleted.
revision.title: revision

settings.description: Every setting, with its value, in settings-form order.
settings.title: settings

strategyId.description: The strategy the proposal came from. Zero once the strategy is deleted.
strategyId.title: strategy_id

strategies.v1.DeployProposalSummary.title: DeployProposalSummary

strategies.v1.DeployStatus.description: DeployStatus is where a deploy proposal is.

botId.description: Public ID of the bot. Zero until the bot exists.
botId.title: bot_id

expiresAt.description: When the proposal expires if not deployed.
expiresAt.title: expires_at

failedAt.description:
The step the deploy failed in: VALIDATING, CREATING_SUBACCOUNT,
 SETTING_ACCESS, FUNDING or DEPLOYING. Set when a deploy fails, by the deploy flow, beside
 failure; unset in any other state.
failedAt.title: failed_at

failure.description:
Why the deploy stopped and what the user can do. Empty unless state is
 FAILED.
failure.title: failure

step.description:
The current step as the user sees it, for example "Funding the
 account…".
step.title: step

subaccountId.description: Public ID of the bot's subaccount. Zero until it exists.
subaccountId.title: subaccount_id

updatedAt.description: When the state last changed.
updatedAt.title: updated_at

wait.description:
What a running deploy waits for from the user before it can go on.
 Unset when it waits for nothing. Calling DeployBot again once the user
 has done it continues the deploy.
wait.title: wait

strategies.v1.DeployStatus.title: DeployStatus

strategies.v1.DeployStatus.State.description: State is a deploy proposal's step.
strategies.v1.DeployStatus.State.title: State

strategies.v1.DeployWait.description: DeployWait is what a running deploy waits for from the user.

address.description:
WHITELIST_REQUIRED: the bot's subaccount's smart account address, the
 one to add to the internal whitelist. Empty for any other reason.
address.title: address

reason.description: What the user has to do.
reason.title: reason

strategies.v1.DeployWait.title: DeployWait

strategies.v1.DeployWait.Reason.description: Reason is what the user has to do.
strategies.v1.DeployWait.Reason.title: Reason

buyAndHoldEquity.description: Buy-and-hold's equity at the same time, from the same starting balance.
buyAndHoldEquity.title: buy_and_hold_equity

equity.description: The bot's equity, as an exact decimal in the quote asset.
equity.title: equity

 from its closed trades, the days its market data fully covers, and its
 gaps, never from the calendar span alone.

strategies.v1.ExplainStrategyRequest.description: ExplainStrategyRequest asks for the review summary of a version.
strategies.v1.ExplainStrategyRequest.title: ExplainStrategyRequest

strategies.v1.ExplainStrategyResponse.description:
ExplainStrategyResponse is what a user reviews before deploying a version.

 exactly what the user approves.

backtest.description:
The latest backtest. Omitted when there is none; backtest_absent_reason
 then says why.
backtest.title: backtest

backtestAbsentReason.description:
Why there is no backtest, for example that the bot cannot be backtested
 on candles. Empty when backtest is set.
backtestAbsentReason.title: backtest_absent_reason

limitations.description:
What the bot does not do, for example "stopping the bot does not sell its
 holdings".
limitations.title: limitations

moneyCard.description: What the bot may do with money, its markets and its events.
moneyCard.title: money_card

scenarios.description: Each behaviour example and its last result, in manifest order.
scenarios.title: scenarios

settings.description: The settings a user may change.
settings.title: settings

warnings.description:
What to weigh before deploying, for example "never backtested" or "trades
 a thin market".
warnings.title: warnings

strategies.v1.ExplainStrategyResponse.title: ExplainStrategyResponse

strategies.v1.FlowEdge.description: FlowEdge is one edge of a flow.

branch.description: "true" or "false" out of a condition; empty otherwise.
branch.title: branch

strategies.v1.FlowEdge.title: FlowEdge

strategies.v1.FlowNode.description: FlowNode is one trigger, condition or action of a flow.

action.description:
For an action: BUY, SELL, CANCEL, LOG, NOTIFY, PAUSE, WATCH, UNWATCH or
 TRIGGER. Empty otherwise.
action.title: action

event.description:
For a trigger woken by a manifest event: the event, as the money card
 names it, for example "schedule mon 09:00 UTC". Empty otherwise.
event.title: event

label.description:
What the node shows: a plain description of the code, for example
 "RSI(BTC-USDT, 1d, 14) > 75" or "Buy BTC-USDT for budget". For a
 trigger: a schedule in words, for example "Every Monday 09:00 UTC";
 another manifest event as the money card names it (the same text as
 event); otherwise what wakes the bot, for example "An order fills".
label.title: label

nodeId.description: Stable within the version, for example "t0", "c3" or "a1".
nodeId.title: node_id

settings.description: The settings the node reads, by name.
settings.title: settings

span.description: Where it is in the code. Not set for a trigger.
span.title: span

strategies.v1.FlowNode.title: FlowNode

strategies.v1.FlowNode.Kind.description: Kind is what a node is.
strategies.v1.FlowNode.Kind.title: Kind

GetBotResponse is a bot with its money rules, settings and recent
 decisions. The bot's subaccount is read like any other, by its
 subaccount_id: its balances with LedgerReadService.GetBalances, its open
 orders with OrdersReadService.GetOpenOrders, and its profit and loss with
 ProfitAndLossService.

decisions.description:
Its last decisions, newest first, from the run it is on now: at most 20,
 fewer when they are large. Empty until its run's first decision reaches
 the service, up to about a minute after the bot made it.
decisions.title: decisions

errors.description: Its last errors, newest first, from the run it is on now: at most 20.
errors.title: errors

moneyCard.description: What the bot may do with money, from the version it runs.
moneyCard.title: money_card

settings.description:
Its settings, with their values, in settings-form order, each with its
 description, kind and asset from the version's settings form. Empty
 until the deploy flow records the deploy proposal the bot came from.
settings.title: settings

strategies.v1.ListBotLogsRequest.description: ListBotLogsRequest reads a bot's recent activity.

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return: default 100, max 200.
limit.title: limit

pageToken.description:
Opaque, keyset-backed and exclusive cursor from a previous response's
 next_page_token, or follow_token. It is bound to the caller, bot_id,
 start_time and the deployment whose log the first page read; reuse it
 only with the same values. Its pages read that deployment's log even
 after the bot is deployed again.
pageToken.title: page_token

startTime.description:
Earliest entry time, inclusive. Unset reads from the oldest entry kept.
 It filters by the time of the event behind each entry, which doesn't
 follow the order of the log: to read what is written later, use
 follow_token, never a later start_time.
startTime.title: start_time

strategies.v1.ListBotLogsResponse.description: ListBotLogsResponse returns one page of a bot's recent activity.

deployedAgain.description:
The bot was deployed again after the deployment whose log this response
 read: a new run started, whose entries are in a new log, read by listing
 again without page_token. It doesn't end this log: entries of this
 deployment can still arrive after it, with no set time limit, and
 follow_token keeps reading them for as long as they are kept.
deployedAgain.title: deployed_again

entries.description: Entries, oldest first: in increasing sequence.
entries.title: entries

followToken.description:
Cursor for what is written later: pass it as page_token, now or later,
 to read the entries after the last one this response read, by sequence,
 in the same deployment's log. Set on the last page. An entry that left
 the window before it was read is not returned.
followToken.title: follow_token

nextPageToken.description: Cursor for the next page. Empty when no more results exist now.
nextPageToken.title: next_page_token

code.title: code

expectedNotesRevision.description:
Optional: the notes revision this draft was written against, zero for
 notes never saved. When set, any other current notes revision is
 NOTES_REVISION_CONFLICT, checked together with expected_revision, so a
 writer that measured the draft and the notes together saves them as it
 measured them.
expectedNotesRevision.title: expected_notes_revision

expectedRevision.description:
The revision this draft was made from: the strategy's current revision,
 zero for its first save. Any other value is DRAFT_REVISION_CONFLICT.
expectedRevision.title: expected_revision

idempotencyKey.description:
Client-chosen key, unique per caller, that makes the call idempotent: the
 same key and request return the revision the first call saved, even
 after later saves moved the strategy past it; another request with the
 same key, a CreateStrategy's included, is IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.
 Optional: without it, a retry after a save that landed is
 DRAFT_REVISION_CONFLICT.
idempotencyKey.title: idempotency_key

 object whose shape the reference's manifest section describes. Write
 amounts as decimal strings. At most 65536 bytes (64 KiB) as compact JSON.

version.description:

expectedRevision.description:

 DRAFT_REVISION_CONFLICT, checked together with expected_notes_revision,
 so a writer that measured the draft and the notes together saves them as
 it measured them.
expectedRevision.title: expected_revision

idempotencyKey.description:
Client-chosen key, unique per caller, that makes the call idempotent: the
 same key and request return the notes revision the first call saved,
 even after later saves moved the notes past it; another request with the
 same key, of any strategies write that takes a key, is
 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT. Optional: without it, a retry after a save that
 landed is NOTES_REVISION_CONFLICT.

strategies.v1.StartBacktestRequest.description:
StartBacktestRequest starts a backtest of a version.

 A retry is bound by idempotency_key: the same key and request return the
 backtest the first request started, even when an unset window bound would
 now resolve differently, and never count again against the backtest quota
 or the attempts.

 Across keys, a backtest's identity is its version, effective window,
 effective settings, effective initial balances, and what the platform
 resolves when the request arrives: the caller's fee rates, the platform's
 spread, slippage and fill assumptions, and the simulation's versions. A
 request whose identity matches an earlier backtest of the caller returns
 that backtest rather than running again, so a request that spells out a
 default refers to the same run, while a request that changes any of them,
 or arrives after the platform's part changed, starts a new one:
 - effective window: start_time and end_time, each floored to a whole
   second; an unset end is the end of the longest window with data when
   the request arrives, and an unset start is 365 days before the window's
   end, or fewer for a bot whose candle, schedule and on_start calls would
   not fit a backtest's calls (see start_time), or the start of that
   longest window when its data is shorter;
 - effective settings: every setting of the version's settings form, by
   name, with its default value where the request leaves it out;
 - effective initial balances: initial_balances, or when it is empty,
   1,000 of the bot's quote asset; one per asset, sorted by asset;
 - every decimal in its canonical form, without leading zeros or trailing
   fractional zeros, so "50", "50.0" and "050" are the same amount.

endTime.description:
End of the window, exclusive, floored to a whole second. Unset means the
 end of that longest window.
endTime.title: end_time

idempotencyKey.description:
Client-chosen key, unique per caller, that makes the call idempotent: the
 same key and request return the backtest the first call started; another
 request with the same key is IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT.
idempotencyKey.title: idempotency_key

initialBalances.description:
Starting balances of the simulated account, one per asset of the bot's
 markets, each amount more than 0: a zero or negative amount is
 FUNDING_INVALID. Empty, whether left out or sent as an empty list, means
 1,000 of the bot's quote asset, for example 1000 USDT, whatever its
 settings, such as a budget that is the amount of each buy. Part of the
 backtest's identity: the same run with other balances is another
 backtest.
initialBalances.title: initial_balances

settings.description:
Values for the version's settings form, at most 64, each setting once.
 Settings left out take their default value.
settings.title: settings

startTime.description:
Start of the window, inclusive, floored to a whole second. Unset means
 the most recent 365 days of data: 365 days before the window's end, or
 the start of the longest window with data for the bot's markets and
 timeframes when that is shorter. A backtest holds at most 30,000 calls
 of the bot, across its three cost scenarios. When the bot's code
 handles candles, each close of a candle series it declares under
 candles is a call in each scenario; when it handles its schedule, each
 firing is one; and on_start, when the code defines it, is one at the
 start of each. Unset keeps 365 days only when all of those calls
 together, over 365 days, fit; otherwise it means the most whole days
 whose calls fit, at least one. The calls combine: a bot on one series of
 minute candles alone gets 6 days, on two 3, on a 15-minute schedule
 alone 104, and on an hourly series with an hourly schedule 208, though
 either of those alone keeps 365 days. Only those calls are sized: calls
 the bot gets from its orders and price levels can still take a backtest
 past its calls, as can a bot too busy for even one day.
startTime.title: start_time

strategies.v1.StartBacktestRequest.title: StartBacktestRequest

 reported complete), even after the bot has been deployed again, and

swap.quickswap.v1.BrokerStatsSeries.description:
BrokerStatsSeries is the activity of the broker's QuickSwaps, or of the
 QuickSwaps a referral partner referred (GetReferralStats), or of one
 group of them, in columns.

 A QuickSwap counts in the bucket it was created in, with its current
 status, its credited deposit and its destination payout, so a bucket's
 numbers keep moving until its QuickSwaps end. On the totals series a fee
 counts in the bucket it was charged in, as in GetFeeTotals. On a group
 series the fees charged to the group's QuickSwaps count in the bucket the
 QuickSwap was created in.

 Deposited counts the deposits credited to the QuickSwaps and taken in for
 execution: including a deposit later found ineligible and returned,
 excluding a deposit held for review before credit, each valued in USD
 when it was taken in, as QuickSwap.deposited_value_usd. Delivered counts
 what was paid to the destination of the QuickSwaps whose DESTINATION
 withdrawal is FINALIZED: after service, broker and affiliate fees, before
 the destination network fee, each valued in USD when it was requested, as
 QuickSwap.delivered_value_usd. A fee is valued in USD when it was charged.
 Each value is fixed once, within minutes, and never repriced, so a past
 bucket keeps its value.

 Amounts are exact, in base units of 18 decimals, each list parallel to
 GetBrokerStatsResponse.asset_ids. USD values are scaled by 1e4 (4
 decimals), summed exactly and then rounded down. A value without a USD
 value counts in unvalued_count and is left out of the USD totals.

 Always the first series.
