swap.quickswap.v1.Withdrawal.description:
Withdrawal is one outgoing payment. A QuickSwap can end with several, for
 example a partial refund plus the destination payout; the best case is a
 single destination withdrawal.

address.description:
Recipient address in the network's native text form. Empty on a
 COMPLIANCE_TRANSFER, whose recipient Polyester does not record.
address.title: address

amount.description:
Amount delivered to address after the network fee, in zipped_asset_id's
 token units; set once FINALIZED. Like tx_hash, it is the amount recorded
 for this withdrawal and can be corrected for up to 24 hours after the
 QuickSwap ends (terminal_at). Unset on the RETURN of a deposit returned
 because its risk screen failed (SOURCE_SCREENING_FAILED): that return is
 sent from the deposit address and reports no delivered amount. Unset on
 a COMPLIANCE_TRANSFER too.
amount.title: amount

depositIndex.description:
Index (Deposit.index), in the same response, of the deposit whose funds
 this withdrawal moves. Not stable across reads, like Deposit.index.
depositIndex.title: deposit_index

finalizedAt.description: When the withdrawal became final; unset until FINALIZED.
finalizedAt.title: finalized_at

flowId.description:
Public, URL-safe lifecycle flow identifier of this withdrawal, usable with
 GET /v1/chain/flows/{flow_id}; empty until the flow exists. The flow is
 the authoritative, latest state of the transfer, including a correction
 made after tx_hash, amount and network_fee stop being updated. Lifecycle
 flow amounts are 18-decimal unified units (amount_e18), not token base
 units. For the RETURN of a deposit returned because its risk screen
 failed, it is the deposit's flow (Deposit.flow_id), which ends REFUNDED
 with the return as its transaction. For a COMPLIANCE_TRANSFER, it is the
 deposit's flow too, which ends FAILED with reason
 ZIPPER_COMPLIANCE_TRANSFERRED and the transfer as its transaction.
flowId.title: flow_id

index.description:
Zero-based position in the withdrawals list. Not stable: a withdrawal's
 position can change between reads, so do not use it as an identifier.
index.title: index

memo.description:
Recipient destination tag or memo; empty when the network uses none,
 and on a COMPLIANCE_TRANSFER.
memo.title: memo

networkFee.description:
Actual network fee withheld from this withdrawal, in the same units; set
 once FINALIZED. Can be corrected for up to 24 hours after the QuickSwap
 ends, like amount. Unset on the RETURN of a deposit returned because its
 risk screen failed, and on a COMPLIANCE_TRANSFER, like amount.
networkFee.title: network_fee

role.description: Why this withdrawal pays its recipient.
role.title: role

submittedAt.description: When the withdrawal was submitted; unset until submitted.
submittedAt.title: submitted_at

txHash.description:
Recipient-network transaction recorded for this withdrawal; empty until
 the transaction is committed on the recipient network. It can be
 corrected for up to 24 hours after the QuickSwap ends (terminal_at) and is
 not updated after that. For the authoritative, latest state of the
 transfer, read flow_id.
txHash.title: tx_hash

unsentAmount.description:
Set only when state is NOT_SENT: the amount for which no withdrawal was
 made because it was below the withdrawal minimum of its asset and
 network. In zipped_asset_id's token units, rounded down to the token's
 smallest unit.
unsentAmount.title: unsent_amount

zippedAssetId.description: Asset and network paid, as a zipped_asset_id.
zippedAssetId.title: zipped_asset_id

swap.quickswap.v1.Withdrawal.title: Withdrawal

swap.quickswap.v1.WithdrawalRole.description: WithdrawalRole is why a withdrawal pays its recipient.
swap.quickswap.v1.WithdrawalRole.title: WithdrawalRole

swap.quickswap.v1.WithdrawalState.description:
WithdrawalState is the progress of one withdrawal. FINALIZED and NOT_SENT
 are final: they never change. A FAILED withdrawal never changes either, but
 it does not end the QuickSwap: while any withdrawal is FAILED, the

swap.v1.TwapExecution.description:
TwapExecution spreads the Swap evenly over a duration, one slice per slot.
 Slot k starts k slice intervals after execution starts. Each slice trades
 what is left of the amount over the slots left, and each slice nets at
 least the Swap's minimum rate (min_amount_out_e18 over amount_e18) on what
 it converts, judged slice by slice; slices whose intermediate one later
 second leg converts together (below) are judged together. Each order's
 price limit allows for the taker fee in force when the order can match
 within its window, the highest rate scheduled from when the order is
 prepared until it can last be accepted, some minutes after its sending
 window since a resent copy of it can still be accepted then. An order the
 exchange first accepts after that window (only under severe delay) may pay
 a later scheduled fee, and a slice it takes below the minimum fails the
 Swap closed (MINIMUM_NOT_MET). A slice's first order is sent only within
 its slot: a slot missed is skipped, never sent late. On a two-leg route, a
 slice's second leg is sent once its first leg has settled, at any time
 before the deadline, even after the slice's slot, and the next slice
 starts only once it is over. When no second-leg order can meet the
 protection or the second market's order limits, the slice's intermediate
 asset is added to the next slice's second leg. What a second-leg order
 leaves unfilled, and what is still unconverted when execution ends, stays
 on the account (intermediate_remainder_e18), and the Swap then ends
 PARTIALLY_COMPLETED; a rest smaller than one order step of the second
 market is ordinary residue and the Swap can still end COMPLETED. A TWAP
 needs a larger amount than a market execution, since every slice must be a
 valid order.
slice_interval_ms must not exceed duration_ms

durationMs.description:
Total execution duration in milliseconds, from 60000 (1 minute) to
 3600000 (60 minutes). The duration starts when execution starts.
durationMs.title: duration_ms

sliceIntervalMs.description:
Interval between slices in milliseconds, from 10000 (10 seconds) up to
 duration_ms. The slice count is duration_ms / slice_interval_ms, rounded
 up.
sliceIntervalMs.title: slice_interval_ms

triggers.v1.ConditionalTrigger.description:
ConditionalTrigger configures a standalone stop-loss or take-profit. There
 is no direction field: the strategy and the child order's side set the
 direction in which the watched price must move to fire the trigger.

 - A SELL stop-loss fires when the price falls to or below the trigger
   price: it limits the loss on a held position.
 - A BUY stop-loss is a breakout buy: it fires when the price rises to or
   above the trigger price.
 - A SELL take-profit sells into a rise: it fires when the price rises to or
   above the trigger price.
 - A BUY take-profit buys a dip: it fires when the price falls to or below
   the trigger price.

 The comparison is inclusive: a price equal to the trigger price fires the
 trigger, as does one past it. Trigger reads report the direction as
 StopDetails.trigger_direction, ABOVE or BELOW.

 A trigger price that the watched price has already reached when the trigger
 takes effect, at or past it in the firing direction, is not refused at
 create: CreateTrigger returns a trigger ID, then the trigger ends
 STATUS_FAILED with failure reason
 TRIGGER_FAILURE_REASON_TRIGGER_WOULD_TRIGGER_IMMEDIATELY. It never fires,
 places no order, and its reserved funds are released. Read the trigger
 after the create to tell this outcome from an armed trigger.

side.description:
Child order side. Required. With the strategy, it sets the fire
 direction: a SELL stop-loss and a BUY take-profit fire at or below the
 trigger price; a BUY stop-loss and a SELL take-profit fire at or above

 supported. Fixed at create: to change it, cancel the trigger and create a

triggers.v1.LadderTrigger.description:
LadderTrigger configures the supported LINEAR limit-GTC ladder. All levels
 are admitted immediately as limit GTC orders and may rest concurrently.

 Quantity: with N levels and the total quantity Q (qty_scaled), every level
 but the last gets Q / N rounded down to a multiple of the pair's step_size
 from GetSpotConfig, and the last level gets the rest, Q minus N - 1 times
 that share. All quantities are scaled by the pair's base_quantity_scale.
 For example, Q = 1000 over 3 levels with a step of 10 places 330, 330 and
 340. Each level must be a valid order on its own: on the step size, at
 least min_qty_base, and at least min_notional_quote at its price; so Q
 must itself be a multiple of the step size. A share that rounds down to
 zero, or a level that is not a valid order, rejects the create with
 ERROR_CODE_LADDER_LEVEL_REJECTED, naming that level in level_index (0 for
 a share of zero) and why in cause_code. Nothing is created.

 Prices: with S the number of tick_size steps from price_min_ticks to
 price_max_ticks, level i, counted from 0, is priced floor(i * S / (N - 1))
 steps above price_min_ticks. The first level is at price_min_ticks and the
 last at price_max_ticks, for either side. A range of fewer than N - 1 steps
 rejects the create with ERROR_CODE_LADDER_RANGE_TOO_NARROW.

 To size a ladder from a quote amount, convert it to Q at these level
 prices and quantities before creating it.
price_max_ticks must be greater than price_min_ticks

postOnly.description: Reject each level instead of taking liquidity.
postOnly.title: post_only

Maximum generated level price in quote units scaled by 1e9; must be
 greater than price_min_ticks.

clientListId.description:
Optional filter by OCO client ID: the take-profit and the stop-loss of
 the OCO created with this client_list_id, which follows the same rule as
 OcoIntent.client_list_id: other IDs are rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT and
 ERROR_CODE_CLIENT_LIST_ID_INVALID. Use it to find an OCO whose create
 failed with TRIGGER_CREATE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN.
clientListId.title: client_list_id

clientTriggerId.description:
Optional filter by client trigger ID: the triggers created with this
 client_trigger_id, running or ended. Use it to find a trigger whose
 create failed with TRIGGER_CREATE_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN. An ID is unique per
 sub-account, pair and trigger type only while its trigger is active and
 for 60 seconds after it ends; then a new create can use it again. So the
 filter can match several triggers, newest first: add symbol_id and
 trigger_type to keep one ID's scope. The newest of them is the latest
 create with the ID, not necessarily the create being resolved, which may
 not have taken effect: compare its created_at with when that create was
 sent, or use a new client trigger ID for every create. An empty result
 says only that no trigger of the filters' scope was created with the ID
 before the read, or that it ended more than 24 hours ago: a create still
 in flight can take effect after the read. To settle a create of unknown
 outcome, retry the identical create with the same client trigger ID
 within its window, which returns the trigger it created, if any, instead
 of creating a second. An OCO's take-profit and stop-loss have no client
 trigger ID: find them by client_list_id. 1 to 36 bytes in UTF-8, as
 TriggerIntent.client_trigger_id: empty or longer IDs are rejected with
 INVALID_ARGUMENT and ERROR_CODE_CLIENT_TRIGGER_ID_INVALID.
clientTriggerId.title: client_trigger_id

triggers.v1.ModifyTriggerRequest.description:
ModifyTriggerRequest applies a limited patch to an existing trigger.
 Supported for stop-loss, take-profit and trailing-stop triggers; a running
 ladder or TWAP supports only cancel and answers TRIGGER_NOT_MODIFIABLE. A
 trigger of any type that has ended answers TRIGGER_STATUS_INVALID for at
 least 60 s after it ends; after that it may answer TRIGGER_NOT_FOUND.

activationPriceTicks.description:
Updated activation price in quote units scaled by 1e9. Set to zero to
 clear an existing activation price; omit to leave it unchanged.
 Once trailing tracking has begun, a new or different nonzero value
 rejects the whole request with
 ERROR_CODE_TRIGGER_ACTIVATION_PRICE_NOT_MODIFIABLE and leaves the trigger
 unchanged. Clearing with zero and repeating the current value remain
 accepted, including while paused. Before tracking begins, the activation
 price remains editable.
activationPriceTicks.title: activation_price_ticks

limitPriceTicks.description:
Not modifiable: a trigger's child limit price is fixed at create. Setting
 this field rejects the whole request with
 ERROR_CODE_TRIGGER_CHILD_PRICE_NOT_MODIFIABLE (InvalidArgument, HTTP 400)
 and leaves the trigger unchanged; cancel the trigger and create a new one
 to change the child limit price.
limitPriceTicks.title: limit_price_ticks

maxSlippageBps.description:
Updated maximum allowed slippage in basis points (1 bp = 0.01%). Set to
 zero to clear the cap. A buy stop-loss or take-profit with a market
 child accepts 1 to 10000, as at creation. A trailing stop on either
 side, and a sell stop-loss or take-profit, accept 1 to 9999: 10000 is
 rejected with ERROR_CODE_MAX_SLIPPAGE_INVALID, because a 100% cap would
 leave a sell no positive price, and a trailing stop takes none on
 either side.
maxSlippageBps.title: max_slippage_bps

maxSlippageTicks.description:
Non-negative maximum absolute price delta in quote units scaled by 1e9
 (1e-9 quote units, not the pair's tick size; the value need not be a
 multiple of the pair's tick size). Set to zero to clear the cap.
maxSlippageTicks.title: max_slippage_ticks

 markets, is rejected with ERROR_CODE_API_KEY_MARKET_DENY.
symbolId.title: symbol_id

triggers.v1.OcoIntent.description:
OcoIntent configures an OCO over a quantity the account already holds: a
 take-profit and a stop-loss that both trade `side` for `qty_scaled`. The
 quantity is reserved once, when the OCO is created, and both legs share it,
 so it can be sold or bought only once. A SELL OCO protects a held base
 position: its take-profit is above the last price and its stop-loss below
 it. A BUY OCO buys with held quote: its take-profit is below the last price
 and its stop-loss above it.

 The first leg to reach its trigger price places its order for the OCO's
 remaining quantity. If that order fills only partly, the other leg keeps
 protecting the rest: when its own trigger price is reached it cancels the
 working order and places its own for what is left. When the whole quantity
 has been traded, the leg whose order traded last ends COMPLETED and the
 other ends CANCELED with reason OCO. Cancelling either leg, or the OCO with
 CancelOco, cancels both.

clientListId.description:
Client-provided OCO ID for idempotency, unique per sub-account and pair
 among OCOs. While the OCO is active and for 60 seconds after both legs
 ended, retrying the create with the identical intent returns the same
 OCO, and a different intent with the same ID returns
 CONFLICT_DUPLICATE_CLIENT_TRIGGER_ID. 1 to 36 ASCII characters using
 letters, digits, period, underscore, colon, slash, or hyphen, as a
 client_order_id; other IDs are rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT and
 ERROR_CODE_CLIENT_LIST_ID_INVALID.
clientListId.title: client_list_id

qtyScaled.description:
Positive quantity both legs trade, scaled by the pair's
 base_quantity_scale; a multiple of the pair's quantity step.
qtyScaled.title: qty_scaled

selfTradePreventionMode.title: self_trade_prevention_mode

side.description:
The side both legs trade: SELL protects a held base position, BUY spends
 held quote. Required.
side.title: side

symbolId.description: Stable numeric pair ID from GetSpotConfig.
symbolId.title: symbol_id

takeProfit.description:
The take-profit leg. Its trigger price must be above the stop-loss's for
 a SELL OCO and below it for a BUY OCO. Required.
takeProfit.title: take_profit

triggers.v1.OcoIntent.title: OcoIntent

OcoLeg configures one leg of an OCO: the price that triggers it and the

triggerPriceSource.description:

 an index price the OCO is rejected with
 TRIGGER_FAILURE_REASON_INDEX_PRICE_UNAVAILABLE on both legs. MARK_PRICE
 is not supported.
triggerPriceSource.title: trigger_price_source

triggerPriceTicks.description: Positive trigger price in quote units scaled by 1e9. Required.
triggerPriceTicks.title: trigger_price_ticks

Price source used for trigger evaluation. Fixed for the lifetime of the

Current trailing trigger threshold in quote units scaled by 1e9. This is

triggers.v1.TrailingStopTrigger.description:
TrailingStopTrigger configures a spot trailing-stop strategy. A trailing
 stop that sells tracks the highest price since it activated and fires a
 market IOC child when the price falls the trailing distance from it. A
 trailing stop that buys tracks the lowest price since it activated and
 fires when the price rises the trailing distance from it; its child is an
 IOC limit order at its maximum price, or at its slippage cap above the fire
 price when that is lower, so it never buys above the maximum price. Without
 an activation price, tracking starts when the trigger is placed. Attached
 trailing stops may use either side, opposite their parent order.

activationPriceTicks.description: Optional positive activation price in quote units scaled by 1e9.
activationPriceTicks.title: activation_price_ticks

limitPriceTicks.description:
Positive maximum price of a trailing stop that buys, in quote units scaled
 by 1e9: the most its child pays per unit. Required when `side` is BUY and
 set aside for it with the child's fee; at least the activation price, or
 at least the price it watches (trigger_price_source) when no activation
 price is set. A rise that fires above it still fires, and the child fills
 only at or below it. Must be unset when `side` is SELL. Fixed at create.
limitPriceTicks.title: limit_price_ticks

maxSlippageBps.description:
Maximum slippage in basis points (1 bp = 0.01%), from 1 to 9999 on
 either side. 10000 is rejected with ERROR_CODE_MAX_SLIPPAGE_INVALID,
 because a 100% cap would leave a trailing stop that sells no positive
 price to sell at.
maxSlippageBps.title: max_slippage_bps

maxSlippageTicks.description:
Positive maximum absolute price delta in quote units scaled by 1e9. The
 "ticks" in this name are 1e-9 quote units, not the pair's tick size,
 and the value need not be a multiple of the pair's tick size: the
 child's protection price, the price that fired it moved by this delta,
 is put on the tick grid toward that price, as for a market order
 (orders.v1.MarketIoc).
maxSlippageTicks.title: max_slippage_ticks

trailingDistanceBps.description: Distance in basis points (1 bp = 0.01%), from 1 to 10000.
trailingDistanceBps.title: trailing_distance_bps

trailingDistanceTicks.description: Positive distance as a price delta in 1e-9 quote-unit ticks.
trailingDistanceTicks.title: trailing_distance_ticks

triggerPriceSource.description:
Price the trailing stop watches: its activation, its peak or trough and
 its fire all follow this price. Unspecified or LAST_PRICE watches the last
 traded price. INDEX_PRICE watches the market's index price; a market
 without an index price fails the trigger with
 TRIGGER_FAILURE_REASON_INDEX_PRICE_UNAVAILABLE. MARK_PRICE is not
 supported. Fixed at create: to change it, cancel the trigger and create a
 new one.
triggerPriceSource.title: trigger_price_source

version.description:
Per-trigger state version: 1 for the trigger's first state, then higher
 for every later published state change, whether a request or the market
 caused it. A higher version is always newer, and two copies of a trigger
 with the same version show the same state. GetTrigger, ListTriggers and
 realtime trigger updates carry the same version for the same state. List
 results can briefly lag realtime updates, and after a reconnect or a
 service recovery a realtime update can repeat an earlier state, so keep
 the copy of each trigger with the highest version and ignore any copy
 whose version is not higher than the one you hold.

triggers.v1.TriggerIntent.description: TriggerIntent contains one standalone trigger's initial configuration.

clientTriggerId.description:
Client-provided trigger ID for idempotency, unique per sub-account, pair
 and trigger type. While the trigger is active and for 60 seconds after it
 reaches a terminal status, retrying the create with the identical intent
 returns the same trigger, and a different intent with the same ID returns
 CONFLICT_DUPLICATE_CLIENT_TRIGGER_ID. After those 60 seconds the ID is
 free: a create that uses it is a new intent and creates a new trigger. To
 learn the outcome of an earlier create after that window, find it with
 the ListTriggers client_trigger_id filter instead of retrying the create.
 Use a new client trigger ID for every create, so a lookup never finds an
 older trigger that used the same ID. After a create fails
 with INTERNAL_ERROR, the ID may already be used: a retry then returns
 CONFLICT_DUPLICATE_CLIENT_TRIGGER_ID and needs a new client trigger ID.
 1 to 36 bytes in UTF-8 (up to 36 ASCII characters); empty or longer IDs
 are rejected with INVALID_ARGUMENT and
 ERROR_CODE_CLIENT_TRIGGER_ID_INVALID.
clientTriggerId.title: client_trigger_id

feeAsset.description:
Asset charged for the children's fees, for every strategy. Defaults to
 QUOTE. A trigger whose children BUY may select BASE only on a pair whose
 allow_buy_fee_from_base is true in GetSpotConfig; a trigger whose
 children SELL must use QUOTE. Otherwise the create is refused with
 ERROR_CODE_FEE_ASSET_NOT_ALLOWED.
feeAsset.title: fee_asset

qtyScaled.description: Positive total quantity scaled by the pair's base_quantity_scale.
qtyScaled.title: qty_scaled

selfTradePreventionMode.description:
Child self-trade prevention mode against orders of the same root account,
 including all its subaccounts. Defaults to EXPIRE_MAKER.
selfTradePreventionMode.title: self_trade_prevention_mode

stopLoss.description:
Standalone stop-loss. A SELL stop-loss fires when the price falls to or
 below the trigger price; a BUY stop-loss is a breakout buy that fires
 when the price rises to or above it. A trigger price already reached
 when the trigger takes effect ends the trigger STATUS_FAILED with
 TRIGGER_FAILURE_REASON_TRIGGER_WOULD_TRIGGER_IMMEDIATELY after the
 create is accepted, without firing.
stopLoss.title: stop_loss

symbolId.description: Stable numeric pair ID from GetSpotConfig.
symbolId.title: symbol_id

takeProfit.description:
Standalone take-profit. A SELL take-profit fires when the price rises to
 or above the trigger price; a BUY take-profit buys a dip and fires when
 the price falls to or below it. A trigger price already reached when
 the trigger takes effect ends the trigger STATUS_FAILED with
 TRIGGER_FAILURE_REASON_TRIGGER_WOULD_TRIGGER_IMMEDIATELY after the
 create is accepted, without firing.
takeProfit.title: take_profit

trailingStop.description: Trailing stop: a market-IOC sell or a maximum-price IOC buy.
trailingStop.title: trailing_stop

triggers.v1.TriggerMarketIoc.description:
TriggerMarketIoc configures an immediate market child. When the trigger
 fires, the child is protected like a market order: it fills only within its
 slippage cap of the price that fired it. A market child with a cap never
 fills worse than the cap; on a gap past it, it may fill partly or not at all.
 A buy reserves its funds when it is created, at the trigger price raised by
 the cap, and its child never buys above that price.

maxSlippageBps.description:
Maximum allowed slippage in basis points (1 bp = 0.01%), from 1 to 10000.
 A sell child accepts values below 10000; a 100% cap would leave it no
 positive price to sell at.
maxSlippageBps.title: max_slippage_bps

maxSlippageTicks.description:
Positive maximum absolute price delta in quote units scaled by 1e9. The
 "ticks" in this name are 1e-9 quote units, not the pair's tick size,
 and the value need not be a multiple of the pair's tick size: the
 child's protection price, the price that fired it moved by this delta,
 is put on the tick grid toward that price, as for a market order
 (orders.v1.MarketIoc).
maxSlippageTicks.title: max_slippage_ticks

post.summary: Preview the account's next auto-withdraw run from its balances now:  when it starts, whether it would pay, and per asset what it would pay,  what would stay and why, its USD value and the expected network fee. It  plans exactly as the run does; balances, prices and fees can change  before the run starts. A price that is not current leaves the value  unset instead of failing the read. When prices cannot be read at all,  the values stay unset too, unless the rule has a USD minimum: prices  then decide what pays, so the read answers UNAVAILABLE and can be  retried.

post.description:
Retrieve order state and a bounded page of its lineage executions by order or client order ID.
 Use GetUserTrades for paginated execution history and optional settlement legs.
 Recent accepted orders may wait briefly for read availability; retry UNAVAILABLE with the same lookup key.
 The successor of a BatchReplaceOrders item refused when it applied reads
 REJECTED with the refusal's code, at version 1, for 60 seconds from the
 batch's acceptance: its order ID, batch_request_id, the batch's admission
 as its created time, and its own lineage at generation 1. It has no
 terminal time: the refusal's own time is its BatchReplaceItemReject's
 eventTsNs on the trading WebSocket. It never existed as an order, so it
 carries no order terms: its pair, side, type, time in force, self-trade
 prevention mode and fee asset are unset, and its price and quantities read
 0 as placeholders. The client takes its terms from the batch it sent.
 After that window it is not found: see BatchReplaceOrdersRequest.
 Costs one unit of the account's trading read limit.

It has no  terminal time: the refusal's own time is its BatchReplaceItemReject's  eventTsNs on the trading WebSocket. It never existed as an order, so it  carries no order terms: its pair, side, type, time in force, self-trade  prevention mode and fee asset are unset, and its price and quantities read  0 as placeholders. post.description: Cancel up to 50 orders by order ID or client order ID in one request. A request can be refused as a whole before admission, canceling nothing: for example an invalid request ID or number of items, an item that sets both identifiers or neither, or a failed authentication, permission or receive-window check. Once a request reaches admission, each item's cancellation is accepted or rejected on its own, with per-item results and aggregate counts.

Create up to 20 orders in a single request with per-item results. Supports mixed symbols and attached risk payloads. A request can be refused as a whole before admission, admitting nothing: for example an invalid request ID or number of items, an item whose fields cannot be decoded over REST (a malformed decimal, or more than one execution or sizing field), or a failed authentication, permission or receive-window check. Once a request reaches admission, each item is admitted or rejected on its own, never all-or-nothing: a rejected item does not stop the other items from being admitted.

Modify up to 50 orders for one symbol as a quote refresh. Each item amends its order in place, keeping its order ID and queue priority, when it keeps the price, does not raise the total quantity and keeps the client order ID; otherwise it replaces the order with a successor under a new order ID. Returns an admission receipt for status and private realtime reconciliation. A request can be refused as a whole before admission, changing nothing: for example an invalid request ID or number of items, an item that names no order, supplies no patch field or breaks a field rule, or a failed authentication, permission or receive-window check. Once a request reaches admission, each item is admitted or rejected on its own.

Set or disable a dead-man switch timeout for automatic cancel-all. Supports optional symbol and side scope with idempotent heartbeat refresh. On expiry it cancels open orders in scope, including those that triggers placed (TWAP slices, ladder levels and exit orders). By default it does not cancel triggers: standalone stop-loss, take-profit and trailing triggers and TWAPs keep running and can place new orders; a ladder stops once its levels are canceled. An attached stop-loss, take-profit or trailing leg whose exit order is canceled ends, and so do the parent's other legs when oco is set, so the position loses that protection. Other attached legs keep protecting the parent's filled quantity; those of a parent canceled before any fill end with it. Set include_triggers to also stop every matching trigger, attached legs included, when the switch fires.

Cancel all matching open orders for an account. Supports an optional list of symbols and a side filter plus dry-run preview. Returns up to 200 canceled order IDs, oldest first, with the total count. Unless it is a dry run, it covers every matching order admitted before its requestId was first admitted, from any interface, including orders not yet open and replacement orders: an order whose create or replace response arrived before the first request with this requestId was sent is covered, while requests still in flight or with an unknown outcome have no defined order with it. A retry with the same requestId keeps the original scope and covers no order admitted since; use a fresh requestId for a new cancellation. Each covered order eventually ends; any still open when the cancellation applies is canceled. It cancels open orders, including those that triggers placed (TWAP slices, ladder levels and exit orders). By default it does not cancel triggers: standalone stop-loss, take-profit and trailing triggers and TWAPs keep running and can place new orders; a ladder stops once its levels are canceled. An attached stop-loss, take-profit or trailing leg whose exit order is canceled ends, and so do the parent's other legs when oco is set, so the position loses that protection. Other attached legs keep protecting the parent's filled quantity; those of a parent canceled before any fill end with it. Set include_triggers to also stop every matching trigger, attached legs included, in the same request; matched_triggers counts them. Every request counts 10 against the cancel rate limit, however many orders it cancels, a dry run and a retry included.
Cancel a single open order by order ID or client order ID. Supports optional subaccount and symbol scoping.
Create a single order with side, type, quantity, and optional price fields. Supports optional client order IDs and attached risk instructions (take-profit, stop-loss, trailing stop).
Modify a single open order by order ID or client order ID. Supports amend-or-replace behavior policies, price and quantity updates, and attached risk updates.
Check current order eligibility and available balance without creating an order or reservation. Returns resolved sizing and price protection when available.

post.description: Move up to 500 Trading to Trading transfers together, authorized by one MFA check: every leg is credited, or none moves. A batch debits at most 50 distinct source account and asset pairs from at most 10 source accounts. A batch without the MFA-elevated session or fresh step-up it needs is refused HTTP 403 with code AUTH_MFA_ELEVATION_REQUIRED or AUTH_STEP_UP_REQUIRED.

Create or return one authenticated Trading to Trading internal transfer. Root-owner same-owner transfers and root-owner transfers to explicitly whitelisted destinations accept an MFA-elevated session (MFA completed in the last 30 minutes); delegated and other interactive transfers require fresh step-up. Without them the transfer is refused HTTP 403 with code AUTH_MFA_ELEVATION_REQUIRED or AUTH_STEP_UP_REQUIRED.
Read an accepted transfer by request ID or transfer ID for an authorized source account. JWT session authentication only.

Read a batch's current outcome and the state of every leg by the request ID that Batch Create Internal Transfers returned, or by the idempotency key the caller sent it. The caller must be allowed to read the transfers of every source account of the batch.

Cancel up to 50 triggers by trigger ID in one request. Returns per-trigger accept or reject results in request order with aggregate counts. Each trigger counts one against the cancel rate limit; a retry with the same request_id and trigger IDs within 2 minutes returns the original results.

Cancel all of the account's triggers that match an optional list of symbols, a side and a list of trigger types in one request, with a dry-run count. It cancels no order. Every matching trigger created before the requestId was first accepted ends canceled with reason TRIGGER_CANCEL_REASON_CANCEL_ALL, releases its reserved funds and places no order after the response; a trigger created later keeps running. An order's attached legs and an OCO's two legs end together when any of them matches. Every request counts 10 against the cancel rate limit, however many triggers match, a dry run and a retry included. A retry with the same requestId and criteria within 2 minutes returns the original count and cancels nothing again.

Cancel an OCO by its ID: both legs end CANCELED and the reserved quantity is released. Cancelling either leg with Cancel Trigger does the same. An ID that is not an OCO, such as a trigger ID or a leg's ID, is refused TRIGGER_NOT_FOUND and nothing is canceled.

Cancel a trigger by trigger ID and release its reserved quantity. Use Cancel All Triggers to cancel every trigger matching symbols, side and trigger types in one request; Cancel All Orders and the dead-man switch cancel triggers only with include_triggers. A trigger that has ended answers TRIGGER_STATUS_INVALID for at least 60 s after it ends; after that it may answer TRIGGER_NOT_FOUND. Treat either as already done.

Create a one-cancels-the-other order list: a take-profit and a stop-loss over a quantity the account already holds. The quantity is reserved once for both legs. When one leg's order trades the whole quantity, the other is canceled; a partly filled order's rest stays protected by the other leg. Cancel All Triggers cancels OCOs, and so do Cancel All Orders and the dead-man switch with include_triggers; without it they cancel no OCO, but an OCO leg's working order they cancel cancels the OCO.
Create a standalone trigger order. Supports stop, trailing, TWAP, and ladder trigger configurations.
Retrieve a single trigger by trigger ID, including lifecycle state and strategy-specific fields. Costs one unit of the account's trading read limit.

List append-only trigger events for a trigger, including child-order actions, with optional event-category filtering and reverse-time pagination. Costs two units of the account's trading read limit per 100 rows the limit asks for, rounded up.

List triggers for an account with optional symbol, status, trigger-type and client trigger ID filters. Ended triggers stay listable for at least 24 hours. Follow realtime trigger updates and use this list to recover and reconcile, not to poll. Costs one unit of the account's trading read limit per 100 rows the limit asks for, rounded up.

Modify a trigger by trigger ID using a limited patch for trigger pricing and trailing/slippage parameters. Supported for stop-loss, take-profit and trailing-stop triggers; a running ladder or TWAP supports only cancel and answers TRIGGER_NOT_MODIFIABLE. A trigger that has ended answers TRIGGER_STATUS_INVALID for at least 60 s after it ends; after that it may answer TRIGGER_NOT_FOUND.

Pause a trigger by trigger ID without deleting it. Supported for stop-loss, take-profit and trailing-stop triggers; a running ladder or TWAP supports only cancel and answers TRIGGER_NOT_MODIFIABLE. A trigger that has ended answers TRIGGER_STATUS_INVALID for at least 60 s after it ends; after that it may answer TRIGGER_NOT_FOUND.

Resume a paused trigger by trigger ID. Supported for stop-loss, take-profit and trailing-stop triggers; a running ladder or TWAP supports only cancel and answers TRIGGER_NOT_MODIFIABLE. A trigger that has ended answers TRIGGER_STATUS_INVALID for at least 60 s after it ends; after that it may answer TRIGGER_NOT_FOUND.

tags.description:
PriceAlertService manages the caller's price alerts. An alert belongs to
 the caller's root account, the person, not to a trading account: a session
 and the root account's API keys see the same alerts, and an API key scoped

 API key also needs its policy to grant the call's permission: READ_PRICE_ALERTS
 to list alerts, MANAGE_PRICE_ALERTS to create, update or cancel them. No
 call changes balances, orders or account settings.

tags.description:
AssistantService is the Polyester trading assistant. A user sends a
 message, which starts a run: the assistant's answer, with the tools,
 skills and subagents it uses. The run continues on the server when no
 client watches it, and its events can be replayed and resumed with
 WatchRun.

 Requests are authenticated with a session token. Every conversation, run,
 approval and memory belongs to the authenticated user; another user's
 resource is reported exactly as a missing one. The assistant reads the
 user's account data with the user's own permissions, and an action that
 changes the account, such as placing an order, runs only after the user
 approves it with DecideApproval.
tags.name: AssistantService

tags.description: Convert one asset of an account's Trading balance into another through the spot order books.
tags.name: Swap

tags.description:
SwapService converts one asset of an account's Trading balance into another
 through Polyester's spot order books, on the direct market or through USDT
 or USDC, at market or as a TWAP over up to 60 minutes. A Swap
 executes as immediate-or-cancel spot orders on the account, at the
 account's spot taker fee on each market and with no other fee, protected by
 the end-to-end min_amount_out the caller accepts: each order's price limit
 covers the taker fee scheduled within its window, so any part that trades
 nets at least that rate, and anything that cannot stays on the account. An
 order the exchange first accepts after its window (only under severe
 delay) may pay a later scheduled fee; if that takes a fill below the rate,
 the Swap finishes with MINIMUM_NOT_MET. Quotes are estimates and reserve
 nothing.

 Requests are authenticated with a session token or a signed API key. The
 caller needs the SWAP permission on the account: the trading roles grant it
 on sub-accounts, and API keys and sub-account policies must include the SWAP
 action. A Swap's orders also remain subject to the sub-account's spot
 trading policy.

 Follow a Swap with GetSwap until is_terminal is true; a market Swap usually
 completes within seconds, a TWAP by its deadline.
tags.name: SwapService

tags.description:
AutoWithdrawService manages scheduled in-kind auto-withdraw rules for a
 root account or subaccount. A rule pays each asset's balance out on an
 hourly, daily, weekly, biweekly or monthly UTC slot, through the normal
 withdraw path, only to destinations on the account's external withdraw
 whitelist. Changing or
 resuming a rule requires a person with withdraw rights and a fresh
 single-use MFA step-up, and pausing it requires such a person without a
 step-up; API keys can read rules, runs and previews but never change
 them. An API key reads only when its policy grants READ_AUTO_WITHDRAW (or
 MANAGE_AUTO_WITHDRAW), and only its own account: a root-account key reads
 the root account, and a subaccount key reads its subaccount.
tags.name: AutoWithdrawService

tags.description:
StatementExportService is the account statement API. A statement covers
 one account, optionally one asset, for a period of at most 366 days, and is
 produced in the background as one CSV file: create an export, poll it with
 GetStatementExport until it is READY, then download its file (see
 StatementExport). API keys need the READ_STATEMENTS policy action. A root
 account has at most 5 exports QUEUED or PROCESSING at a time, one account
 produces one export at a time, and a READY file can be downloaded for 7
 days. CancelStatementExport stops a QUEUED or PROCESSING export, which
 frees its place for the account's next export and under the root's 5.
tags.name: StatementExportService

 notifications of the caller's main account. ListNotifications,
 GetNotification and GetNotificationCounts also take an API key of the main
 account whose policy grants READ_NOTIFICATIONS; a key scoped to a
 sub-account is refused with PERMISSION_DENIED (AUTH_API_KEY_ACCESS_DENIED),
 since notifications belong to the main account. Marking notifications read
 or unread takes a session token only.
tags.name: NotificationService

tags.description: Realized and unrealized profit and loss, in USD, of the main account or one subaccount.
tags.name: Profit and Loss

tags.description:
ProfitAndLossService reports the profit and loss of the main account or one
 subaccount, in USD. Spot PnL uses the weighted average cost of each asset:
 buying raises the cost of the holding, selling realizes the proceeds minus
 the average cost of what was sold, and every fee is a realized expense.
 Every trade is valued with the USD price at its execution time. Deposits,
 withdrawals and transfers are never PnL: deposited coins have no known
 cost, and a transfer between the main account and its subaccounts carries
 its cost along.

 Figures follow settled trades and transfers within seconds; as_of says when
 they were last published. Every read needs the READ_PNL action, which every subaccount role and
 every subaccount's read floor include; an API key needs it in its policy.
tags.name: ProfitAndLossService

tags.description: Public trading quota reference data and authenticated effective trading limits.

tags.description:
RateLimitService serves public trading quota reference data and authenticated
 effective trading limits. A trading read costs units of the read limit of
 the account it reads: one unit per call, or for a list, one unit per 100
 rows its limit asks for, rounded up (two for order history, fills and
 trigger events). A read over the limit is refused RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (REST 429
 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED) with its RateLimitDetail.
tags.name: RateLimitService

tags.description: Write, test and propose trading bots: the bot format, validation, behaviour examples, backtests, deploy proposals, reads of the caller's bots, and community listings.
tags.name: Strategies Service

tags.description:
StrategiesService writes, tests and proposes the caller's trading bots and
 reads them. Bots belong to the caller's main account, and each runs on its
 own subaccount, created when the user deploys it. No call moves money,
 creates a subaccount or deploys a bot: deploying takes the user's MFA and
 wallet signature on the deploy page ProposeDeploy links. StopBot stops a
 bot, which only ever reduces what it does.

 Requests name no account, except the funding subaccount of ProposeDeploy:
 every call acts for the caller's main account, and StopBot also for a
 member of a bot's subaccount whose role may stop it. An
 API key must be scoped to the main account, and its policy must grant the
 call's permission: READ_STRATEGIES for reads, DRAFT_STRATEGIES to create,
 save, rename and delete strategies and test versions, PROPOSE_STRATEGY_DEPLOY to
 propose deploys, STOP_STRATEGIES to stop bots. An API key scoped to a subaccount is refused
 (PERMISSION_DENIED, AUTH_API_KEY_ACCESS_DENIED) even when its policy grants
 the permission. GetStrategyReference, ListStrategyTemplates,
 ListCommunityStrategies and GetCommunityStrategy need no credentials.
 PublishStrategyVersion and UnpublishStrategy take the user's own session:
 publishing makes a strategy's code public, so only the user does it, on
 the website. A session a connected app holds on the user's behalf makes
 the reads with the account:read scope, and creates, saves, renames and
 deletes strategies, tests versions, proposes deploys and stops bots with
 strategies:manage; a call outside the session's scopes refuses it
 (PERMISSION_DENIED, AUTH_SESSION_KIND_NOT_ALLOWED). No connected app
 deploys a bot: deploying takes the user's MFA and wallet signature.
 Every call is safe to retry.
tags.name: StrategiesService

tags.description: Broker-only swaps of an external deposit into external withdrawals.
tags.name: QuickSwap

tags.description:
QuickSwapService is the broker-only QuickSwap API, served over ConnectRPC
 and REST. Every RPC requires the broker's API key, sent as a bearer token
 in the Authorization header; the broker is derived from it, never from the
 request. End users need no account. Brokers see only their
 own QuickSwaps.

 The broker API key is a server credential. Call this API from the broker's
 backend, never from a browser or mobile app. The broker's members create,
 rotate and revoke keys with QuickSwapBrokerService, and a key may rotate
 itself.

 A QuickSwap's status advances as the deposit and execution progress; poll
 GetQuickSwap to follow it, at most once every 5 seconds per QuickSwap while
 it is not terminal. Polling can stop once is_terminal is true.

 REST errors are application/problem+json (see ErrorDetail) with these HTTP
 statuses: 400 for INVALID_ARGUMENT and FAILED_PRECONDITION, 401 for
 UNAUTHENTICATED, 403 for PERMISSION_DENIED, 404 for NOT_FOUND, 409 for
 ALREADY_EXISTS (IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT) and ABORTED (ADDRESS_CONFLICT), 413
 when a request body is too large, 429 for RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED (with a
 Retry-After header when the request rate was exceeded), 500 for an
 internal error, and 503 for UNAVAILABLE and DEADLINE_EXCEEDED.
tags.name: QuickSwapService

tags.description: Self-service administration of a QuickSwap broker org: affiliate vaults, API keys and members, reporting on its QuickSwaps and fees, and its vaults' payouts.
tags.name: QuickSwap Broker

tags.description:
QuickSwapBrokerService administers a broker org, over ConnectRPC and REST.
 Every request names its broker. The caller is either the broker's API key,
 sent as a bearer token (see QuickSwapService), or a member's interactive
 session token; a person who is not a member of the broker gets NOT_FOUND /
 BROKER_NOT_FOUND. Each RPC maps to one broker action:

 | Action | Owner | Admin | Finance | Affiliate manager | Viewer | API key |
 | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
 | Read (GetBroker, ListKeys, ListVaults, GetVault, ListMembers, ListQuickSwaps, GetQuickSwap, GetFeeTotals, GetBrokerStats, ListVaultBalances, ListPayouts, GetPayout, ListUpcomingPayouts, ListVaultPayoutRules, ListVaultLedger, ListVaultAllowlist, ListVaultAllowlistChanges) | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes | yes, except ListMembers |
 | Create vaults (CreateAffiliateVault, SetVaultStatus) | yes | yes | no | yes | no | yes |
 | Manage keys (CreateKey, RotateKey, RevokeKey) | yes | yes | no | no | no | RotateKey of itself only |
 | Manage members (InviteMember, SetMemberRole, RemoveMember) | yes | yes, never the Owner | no | no | no | no |
 | Transfer ownership | yes | no | no | no | no | no |
 | Manage the payout address allowlist (RequestVaultAllowlistChange) | yes | no | yes | no | no | no |

 A member managing keys, members or the payout address allowlist must also
 send a fresh step-up proof in
 the X-Auth-Step-Up header, obtained by completing an MFA challenge for
 fresh step-up; each proof authorizes one change. Reads, vaults and a key
 rotating itself need none. A denied action fails with PERMISSION_DENIED /
 ACTION_DENIED, a missing or used proof with PERMISSION_DENIED /
 STEP_UP_REQUIRED.

 An API key's calls count against the broker's read_rps for the key. A
 member's session calls count against the member's account, across every
 broker the member belongs to: changes (vaults, keys, members, invites,
 ownership and the payout address allowlist) against the account's change
 quota, and reads against the account's own read rate. These limits are
 checked before the call runs, so a call they refuse changes nothing: over a
 limit it fails with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED / BROKER_LIMIT and a Retry-After
 header in seconds, and while a member's change quota cannot be checked, the
 change fails with UNAVAILABLE carrying a RateLimitDetail (REST: the message
 "rate limit authority unavailable"). Any other UNAVAILABLE on a change can
 leave its outcome unknown: read the state again before retrying it.

 REST errors are application/problem+json (see ErrorDetail) with the HTTP
 statuses of QuickSwapService, except that CreateKey and RotateKey answer
 DEADLINE_EXCEEDED with 504: the outcome is unknown and a retry may create
 another key, so list the broker's keys before retrying.
tags.name: QuickSwapBrokerService

tags.description: Public, read-only view of completed QuickSwaps across every broker, and their aggregate statistics.
tags.name: QuickSwap Explorer

tags.description:
QuickSwapExplorerService is the public, read-only view of QuickSwaps, over
 ConnectRPC and REST. It needs no credentials and lists QuickSwaps of every
 broker, Polyester's own QuickSwap app included.

 Only completed QuickSwaps are shown, listed or read by swap_id: one in
 progress, refunded, returned or expired never is. Each shows its assets
 and networks, the amounts deposited and delivered with their USD values
 fixed when they happened, the markets traded, and the transactions and
 addresses of its deposit and destination payout, as public on their
 networks. It shows no memo or destination tag, no return or refund
 address and nothing about the broker (see ExplorerQuickSwap).

 GetQuickSwapStats aggregates the same completed QuickSwaps over a window:
 totals with exact amounts per asset, a time series of counts and USD
 values, and per-route totals, with USD values fixed when they happened.

 QuickSwaps created before the Explorer launched are listed, but never
 match an asset filter and are not counted in statistics.

 Calls are rate limited per client address: over the limit a call fails
 with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED and a Retry-After header.
tags.name: QuickSwapExplorerService

tags.description: A referral partner's own record: enrollment, status, rates, referral code, the QuickSwaps it referred, its commission ledger and its stats.
tags.name: QuickSwap Referral

tags.description:
QuickSwapReferralService is a referral partner's own record, over
 ConnectRPC. A referral partner shares a link with their code; QuickSwaps
 made through it on Polyester's own QuickSwap app give the user a discount
 and pay the partner a commission, both out of the broker fee (see
 ReferralProgram). Referrals never apply to QuickSwaps through other
 brokers or the API.

 Every RPC takes the caller's interactive session token and acts only on
 the caller's own partner record; a broker API key is refused with
 PERMISSION_DENIED / ACTION_DENIED. A person who has not enrolled gets
 NOT_FOUND / REFERRAL_PARTNER_NOT_FOUND from every RPC but
 EnrollReferralPartner.

 A partner's code can be changed while it is not disabled, up to 9 times.
 The old code is reserved and never given to anyone else: links with it keep
 crediting the partner, at the program's current rates, and QuickSwaps
 already referred keep their partner.

 A partner reads the QuickSwaps it referred with ListReferredQuickSwaps
 and GetReferredQuickSwap, never another partner's or a QuickSwap without
 its referral. They return no identity of the person who swapped and no
 account, address, memo, transaction hash or flow ID; amounts are exact and
 times are rounded down to the minute.

 Commissions are credited to the partner's earnings sub-account, which the
 partner owns: its balance, payouts and payout addresses are managed like
 any sub-account's, with AutoWithdrawService and the withdraw whitelist.
 ListReferralLedger lists each commission credit with its QuickSwap and
 each auto-withdraw payout from that sub-account.

 GetReferralStats reads the activity of the QuickSwaps the partner
 referred and its commission over time, in GetBrokerStats' columns, with
 a breakdown by route, source or destination asset. It shows the
 partner's commission only, never the other fees of those QuickSwaps.

 Every RPC is rate limited per account: over the limit it fails with
 RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED, a RateLimitDetail and a Retry-After header.
 GetReferralStats instead shares GetBrokerStats' budget, the caller's read
 rate: over it the call fails with RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED / BROKER_LIMIT and a
 Retry-After header.
tags.name: QuickSwapReferralService

tags.description:
DustConversionService converts dust, Trading balances too small to trade, into
 one target asset at index prices less a disclosed fee. A conversion moves
 every source and credits the payout atomically, or moves nothing.

 Limits: a balance converts when no open market accepts an order for it and it
 is worth at most 10 USD; one conversion takes at most 20 balances worth at
 most 200 USD together; an account converts once every 6 hours, refused
 conversions excepted; each target has a daily conversion limit.

 Quoting, converting and reading conversions need the CONVERT_DUST permission;
 listing balances needs READ_BALANCES. Sessions have both for the root
 account. On a subaccount, the role must be owner, admin, trader or leveraged
 trader, and the subaccount's policy must grant CONVERT_DUST, which its
 default policy does not. An API key's policy must grant CONVERT_DUST, and a
 subaccount-scoped key's subaccount policy too. No step-up is required: the
 value stays in the account.
tags.name: DustConversionService
